interaction_model.visible_feedback: The running change continues undisturbed to its settled end; no second movement starts, so quarter motions and reveals never overlap
interaction_model.input: Further activations of either control while a change is still running
interaction_model.affected_object: The running change

experience_qualities: Deliberate and elegant rather than quick or snappy
Genuine sense of depth, distinctly not a flat crossfade
Continuous and endless, with no felt boundary at either end of the run
Calm and legible centre against expansive, cinematic imagery
One clean movement at a time, never stacked or stuttering
completion_and_return: Each change completes when the incoming image rests at its final full-view size and becomes the single visible picture
The sequence loops in both directions, so there is no terminal state
The immediately previous picture is always one step away via the opposite control
The centred wording and both side controls persist unchanged before, during and after every change
locked_observable_requirements: Exactly one image fills the whole view at any resting moment
The outgoing image separates into four equal quarters that move away in different directions, each clipped to its own frame
The incoming image is revealed from behind and eases forward, growing to its final full-view size, producing a depth read rather than a crossfade
The change begins immediately on activation, with no lead-in delay
Inputs arriving during a change are ignored, never queued, so changes never overlap
The sequence wraps in both directions with no visible first or last item
Centred wording remains fixed, unmoved and legible throughout every change
Large stepping controls sit at both side edges, vertically centred: backward left, forward right
adaptable_details: Number of images in the sequence and their subject matter
Duration and easing curve of the change, provided it reads as deliberate and elegant
The specific outward directions and paths taken by the four quarters
How far the incoming image starts back in depth before easing forward
Visual styling of the stepping controls and their affordance treatment
Wording content, typographic treatment and any legibility aid behind it
Whether an ambient or automatic advance supplements the manual stepping
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any view that can devote its full frame to a small curated set of photographic or richly visual images with only sparse centred wording over them, and where the visitor steps through the set. Changing the split into a different count or non-equal division, replacing the depth-forward reveal with a blend, wipe or slide, showing several images at once, or overlaying dense readable content that must reflow with each image would each create a different Skill.

source_sites.title: How to Create a Tiled Background Slideshow

name: flip_forward_tile_to_fullscreen_detail
description: A picture tile picked from a grid rushes toward the viewer while the rest of the set sinks back, turning over as it stretches to cover the window and landing blank side up, then a short progress marker gives way to that item's own writing and imagery, which scrolls inside the covering surface until a close mark turns the tile back down into its slot.

canonical_document.name: flip_forward_tile_to_fullscreen_detail
canonical_document.description: A picture tile picked from a grid rushes toward the viewer while the rest of the set sinks back, turning over as it stretches to cover the window and landing blank side up, then a short progress marker gives way to that item's own writing and imagery, which scrolls inside the covering surface until a close mark turns the tile back down into its slot.
canonical_document.experience_scope: Region experience that begins in the collection overview and temporarily takes over the whole view: it starts on selection of one tile, occupies the entire window during detail reading, and ends when the tile is turned back down into the overview it came from.
content_and_composition: One set of many equivalent picture tiles arranged so the whole set is legible at a glance, each tile acting as both preview and the surface that becomes the detail page
Exactly one selected tile at a time is promoted; all remaining tiles form a single receded layer behind it
The promoted tile has two faces: the picture face seen in the overview and a blank, unpictured face that lands upward and becomes the detail reading surface
Detail content consists of that item's own writing plus its own imagery, composed as a self-contained scrollable body inside the covering surface
A persistent close mark stays within easy reach for the whole detail state, held clearly separable from the content behind it
A brief progress marker occupies the blank surface before the detail body settles, readable against whatever tone that surface carries
experience_progression: Overview: the whole set is taken in at a glance with no single item dominating
Promotion: the chosen tile advances toward the viewer while the rest of the set falls back into the distance
Turn and cover: the advancing tile turns over as it stretches out until it covers the window, landing blank side up
Signalled pause: a short, clearly marked wait on the blank surface reads as deliberate rather than stalled
Settling: the item's own writing and imagery replace the marker and become the page being read
Reading: the detail body scrolls on its own while the receded set stays fixed behind
Return: the surface turns back down and shrinks into the slot it came from, restoring the overview exactly as it was left
attention_and_information_flow: Attention starts distributed evenly across the whole set, with no item privileged
On selection attention collapses onto one item as depth separation pushes the remaining set out of contention
At the moment of covering, the only visible information is the blank surface and the pause marker, so expectation is held on one point
Attention then transfers from the item's picture identity to its written and pictorial detail, which becomes the sole foreground content
The close mark remains a quiet secondary cue throughout reading, present but lower in salience than the body
On return, attention widens back to the full set with the origin slot reading as the place just visited

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The move runs to completion as one continuous gesture; the tile's origin slot is remembered so the same path can be retraced later
interaction_model.state_change: Overview state becomes opening state: one tile is promoted forward and turned over while all others recede in depth
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The tile visibly advances, rotates over and stretches until it covers the window blank side up, while the rest of the set shrinks back into the distance
interaction_model.input: Choosing any picture tile in the overview
interaction_model.affected_object: The chosen tile plus the remaining set as a background layer

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Selection becomes available again only once the view has settled, so no second item can be promoted mid-move
interaction_model.state_change: No state change; the extra selections are ignored
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The in-progress move continues undisturbed with no competing motion or flicker
interaction_model.input: Additional picks made while an opening move is still running
interaction_model.affected_object: The running transition

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The pause is short and clearly signalled so waiting reads as intentional; the close mark is reachable across the pause and detail states
interaction_model.state_change: Pause state gives way to detail state
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A brief progress marker is shown, held at clearly readable contrast against the covering surface, and then replaced by the item's own writing and imagery
interaction_model.input: Autonomous advance after the surface lands blank side up
interaction_model.affected_object: The blank covering surface

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Scrolling is bounded by the detail body; the background never scrolls or shifts, and reading can be abandoned at any point via the close mark
interaction_model.state_change: Reading position advances within the detail body only
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The detail content moves on its own while the receded set behind stays completely fixed
interaction_model.input: Scrolling inside the detail
interaction_model.affected_object: The item's writing and imagery on the covering surface

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The collection is handed back exactly as it was left, including scroll position and layout of the set, so the visit leaves no trace
interaction_model.state_change: Detail state returns to overview state
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The surface turns back down and contracts into the exact slot it came from while the set rises back to its original depth and arrangement
interaction_model.input: Activating the close mark
interaction_model.affected_object: The covering surface and the receded set

experience_qualities: Continuous rather than jump-cut: detail feels like the same object grown, not a new place
Deliberate and calm, with a paused beat that is signalled instead of hidden
Depth-layered, with a clear front object and a distinctly separated, low-distraction backdrop set
Single-focus and uninterruptible during the opening move
Reversible and tidy, ending exactly where it began
completion_and_return: Detail state persists until the user closes it; there is no automatic exit
Closing reverses the same turn-and-shrink path back into the origin slot
The overview is restored to its exact prior state rather than rebuilt fresh
The experience can be repeated with any other item from the restored overview
locked_observable_requirements: The whole set must be graspable at a glance before any item is promoted
Selection promotes exactly one item forward while all remaining items recede into the distance and read as clearly separated from it
The promoted item turns over while it stretches out and lands blank, unpictured side up covering the window
A short, clearly signalled pause with a progress marker precedes the appearance of the detail content
The detail content is that item's own writing and imagery presented on the covering surface at readable contrast
The detail body scrolls while the receded set behind remains fixed
A close mark stays within easy reach and distinguishable from the body during the detail state
Closing turns the surface back down into the exact slot it came from and restores the set as it was left
Selections made while an opening move is still running are ignored
adaptable_details: Number, size, aspect ratio and arrangement of tiles in the set
How far and fast the front item travels and how deep the rest recede
Turn direction and pacing of the flip and stretch
Visual form of the progress marker and exact length of the pause
Placement, shape and label of the close mark
Typography, color treatment in any hue family or lightness range, and internal layout of the detail body
Subject matter of the pictures and length of the accompanying writing
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any set of equivalent, visually distinct preview tiles where each tile has its own longer body of writing and imagery worth a full-view read, and where the set must survive the visit unchanged. Works under any host color scheme, since separation is carried by depth, scale and contrast rather than by particular hues or a light or dark stage. Replacing the grown-item surface with a separate destination view, a side panel, or an overlay that does not originate from the chosen tile, or dropping the turn-over and blank-landing beat, produces a different Skill; sets whose items have no reusable front-face image also fall outside it.

name: tossed_print_heap_focus_gallery
description: A heap of tilted, overlapping, uniformly suppressed instant-print-style cards that opens on one click into a single fully clarified card resting square in the centre, with the rest of the heap shoved to the edges and re-strewn on every selection, and notes revealed by turning the centre card over.

canonical_document.name: tossed_print_heap_focus_gallery
canonical_document.description: A heap of tilted, overlapping, uniformly suppressed instant-print-style cards that opens on one click into a single fully clarified card resting square in the centre, with the rest of the heap shoved to the edges and re-strewn on every selection, and notes revealed by turning the centre card over.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A self-contained page region. It begins as a closed heap occupying the region's footprint and, after activation, becomes an open browsing arrangement inside the same region; it never takes over the whole view and has no terminal end state beyond the open browsing state.
content_and_composition: One gallery region holding a small browsable set of image cards, each with a short caption
A subset of the browsable cards additionally carries a short personal note on the card's reverse side
Extra non-browsable cards mixed into the heap purely to add depth, so the heap reads as fuller than the number of items that can actually be selected
Closed state: all cards overlapping, tilted at varied angles and uniformly held at reduced contrast and clarity, reading as one strewn pile rather than a set of choices

Open state: exactly one focused card centred, untilted and lifted to the region's highest contrast and full clarity; every other card pushed outward to crowd the region's edges as low-salience depth and texture
A persistent row of small dot indicators beneath the heap, one dot per browsable card, marking which card is current; dots belonging to cards that have a note carry a small turn-arrow mark
Note text presented as personal handwriting on the reverse face of the focused card, replacing its image face
experience_progression: Closed: suppressed tilted heap, clearly not yet open, no single item favoured
Opening: the first card glides to the centre while all remaining cards slide outward to clear space around it
Browsing: one card stays centred and legible; each new selection re-spreads the surrounding cards and carries the chosen card inward
Optional turn: the centred card flips to its handwritten note and flips back
Every step resolves back to one legible card resting square at the centre
attention_and_information_flow: While closed, attention is on the heap as a single object; the uniform suppression and overlap hold every individual card below reading salience, so no content competes for reading
Opening collapses attention onto the centred card, which is the only fully clarified, upright, high-contrast element; the periphery is downgraded to depth
The dot row is the only place where set size and current position are stated, keeping that information out of the visual heap
Turn-arrow marks on dots pre-announce which cards hold extra reading before the user commits to them
Turning the card over swaps image prominence for text prominence in the same central slot, so the note is read where the photo was

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The whole-area click target exists only in the closed state; once open, clicks are handled by the dot controls. Repeat clicks during the opening motion are ignored.
interaction_model.state_change: Region goes from closed to open; the first card becomes the focused card
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The first card glides to the centre and settles square at full clarity and peak contrast while all other cards slide outward to clear space around it, lifting the closed suppressed look
interaction_model.input: A single click anywhere in the region while it is closed
interaction_model.affected_object: The whole heap and the first browsable card

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Further clicks are ignored while the rearrangement is running. If the current card is turned over to its note, it is turned face-up first and only then is the newly chosen card brought in, so the centre never ends up mid-turn.
interaction_model.state_change: Focus transfers to the clicked card and the surrounding arrangement is regenerated
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The previously focused card leaves the centre and drops back to peripheral salience, every other card re-spreads to fresh tilted positions at the edges, and the chosen card is carried in to rest square at full clarity and peak contrast at the centre; the clicked dot becomes the current one
interaction_model.input: Click on a dot other than the current one
interaction_model.affected_object: The focused card and the surrounding peripheral cards

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Fully reversible by clicking the same dot again. Clicks are ignored while a turn or a rearrangement is still in progress, and any card change forces a return to the image face first.
interaction_model.state_change: The centre card toggles between its image face and its note face
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The card turns over in place to show the short note in personal handwriting at the same readable contrast the image face held; clicking the same dot again turns it back to the image face
interaction_model.input: Click on the dot that is already current
interaction_model.affected_object: The focused centre card

experience_qualities: Playful and casually strewn rather than aligned or gridded
Tactile, hand-made, physical-object feel of loose prints on a surface
Depth and abundance without clutter, because the extra cards are texture only
Personal and intimate at the moment the handwritten note appears
Calm and decisive: every action ends with one clearly legible focus
Fresh on each selection, since the surrounding scatter is never the same twice
completion_and_return: No terminal completion; the open browsing state persists and remains available
Each interaction returns the region to its resting composition of one centred legible card surrounded by lower-salience edge clutter
The turned-over note always returns to the image face, either by repeating the same dot click or automatically when another card is chosen
Opening is a one-time transition for the region; there is no stated return to the closed heap
The current card and its face-up/face-down state persist until the next input
locked_observable_requirements: Closed state must read as a heap: overlapping, tilted, uniformly suppressed in contrast and clarity, and visibly not yet open
The heap must look fuller than the browsable set, with the surplus cards serving only as depth and never selectable
A single click anywhere in the closed region opens it; no separate opening control
Opening moves the first card to the centre while the others move outward to make room
In the open state exactly one card is centred, untilted and carries the region's highest contrast and clarity while all others crowd the edges at visibly lower salience
The peripheral arrangement is re-strewn on every selection rather than reused
One dot per browsable card sits below the heap and marks the current card
Dots whose card has a note carry a small turn-arrow mark
Clicking the current dot turns the centre card over to a handwritten-style note; clicking again turns it back
Inputs are ignored while a rearrangement or turn is in progress
Choosing a different card while one is turned over restores the face-up side first
Every step resolves to a single legible card resting square at the centre
adaptable_details: Exact tilt angles, offsets and spread distances
How many surplus depth-only cards are in the heap
Number of browsable items, as long as the set stays small
Card framing, border, shadow and surface treatment
Dot and turn-arrow styling, size and spacing
Motion timing, easing and turn direction
Colour scheme, how deep the suppression of unfocused cards goes, and the surround surface treatment, provided the focused card stays clearly the most legible element
Handwriting typeface choice and caption placement on the card
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits small curated sets of image-plus-short-text items where an informal, personal, keepsake tone is wanted and visitors should dwell on one item at a time. It stays the same Skill across subject matter, colour scheme and card styling. It becomes a different Skill if the collection grows large enough to need scrolling, paging or search, if items lose the two-sided image/note duality so there is nothing to turn over, if focus is driven by dragging, dealing or continuous carousel scrolling instead of discrete dot selection, or if the region opens automatically so the closed heap is never encountered.

name: cover_opens_into_full_window_page_turn_preview
description: An evenly spaced shelf of labelled cover faces; choosing one swings its cover open and enlarges it into a full-window two-page spread that is read spread by spread with tactile turns, then closes back onto the shelf in its original spot.

canonical_document.name: cover_opens_into_full_window_page_turn_preview
canonical_document.description: An evenly spaced shelf of labelled cover faces; choosing one swings its cover open and enlarges it into a full-window two-page spread that is read spread by spread with tactile turns, then closes back onto the shelf in its original spot.
canonical_document.experience_scope: Whole-view experience with two linked phases: a persistent region-level collection grid in the underlying view, and a full-window focused preview overlay that begins when one item is chosen and ends when the preview is closed, returning control to the grid.
content_and_composition: One collection grid of many equally sized front faces, evenly spaced with generous calm rhythm, each face carrying two short text labels (primary title and secondary attribution)
Each face acts as its own entry control into the preview
One focused preview object per session: a two-panel spread occupying the full window, visually reading as an opened physical object with a left and right facing page
A short bounded run of spreads inside the preview (a sample, not the whole work)
Persistent preview controls: previous and next turn affordances plus a close affordance, layered above the spread
The originating grid remains behind the preview as a dropped-away, non-scrolling backdrop, with the chosen item's slot conceptually reserved
experience_progression: Calm survey: the visitor takes in the evenly spaced faces and senses that any one can be looked into
Selection and opening: the chosen face's cover swings open and the object scales up from its place in the grid until it fills the window as a spread
Sequential reading: spreads advance or reverse exactly one at a time through the bounded sample, with end-of-sample resistance instead of advance
Closing: the opening motion plays in reverse, the object shrinks and its cover shuts, setting it back into the grid
Return: the visitor is handed back to the grid at exactly the position they left, with that item closed and its preview reset to its first spread
attention_and_information_flow: Initially attention is distributed evenly across the collection; no single face dominates, and labels supply just enough identity to choose
On selection attention narrows sharply: surroundings drop away and the enlarging object becomes the sole focus
Inside the preview the spread content carries nearly all attention; turn and close affordances stay quietly available at the edges
Each turn reveals one new increment of interior content and retires the previous one, so revealed information grows strictly in reading order
On close attention widens back to the collection, re-anchored on the item just previewed

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The opening is a single continuous motion tied to the item's original position, so it can always be played back in reverse to that exact origin
interaction_model.state_change: Collection browsing gives way to focused preview of that item, starting at its first spread
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The cover swings open and the object enlarges continuously from its position in the grid until it becomes the full-window two-page spread while the surroundings drop away
interaction_model.input: Activating an item's front face (click or equivalent tap)
interaction_model.affected_object: That item's front face and the whole surrounding view

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Suspension is bound to the preview's lifetime and released on close, with the earlier scroll position restored unchanged
interaction_model.state_change: Underlying scrolling is suspended for the whole duration of the preview
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The background stays completely still behind the focused spread; only the preview responds
interaction_model.input: Preview being open
interaction_model.affected_object: Scrolling of the underlying collection view

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Inputs arriving while a turn is in progress are ignored, so the sequence can never desynchronise; the direction is symmetric so any turn can be undone by the opposite affordance
interaction_model.state_change: Exactly one spread step in the pressed direction, never more
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A page visibly turns across the spread with an unhurried, physical, handled-copy feel, settling into the next facing pair
interaction_model.input: Forward or backward turn affordance
interaction_model.affected_object: The open spread inside the preview

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Self-resolving: the page always returns to rest, leaving the current spread intact
interaction_model.state_change: No change of spread; the sequence boundary is asserted
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The page lifts slightly and settles back down instead of turning
interaction_model.input: Forward affordance at the last spread, or backward affordance at the first
interaction_model.affected_object: The edge page of the spread

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Prior scroll position is restored exactly, and the item's preview is reset so a later opening begins again at its first spread
interaction_model.state_change: Focused preview ends and collection browsing resumes
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The opening motion reverses: the spread shrinks back toward its slot, the cover shuts, and the item is set back in place among the others
interaction_model.input: Close affordance
interaction_model.affected_object: The focused preview object and the underlying collection view

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: No device-specific behaviour or extra gesture is required to open, turn or close
interaction_model.state_change: Same transitions as pointer activation
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Identical motions and feedback regardless of input device
interaction_model.input: Touch taps on any affordance
interaction_model.affected_object: All preview and entry controls

experience_qualities: Calm, evenly paced and uncluttered in the collection phase
Decisive narrowing of focus on selection
Tactile, physical, unhurried handling of a real printed object
Strictly ordered and never skipping or desynchronising
Reassuringly reversible: every entry has an exact matching exit
Restrained sampling rather than exhaustive reading
completion_and_return: The preview has no automatic end; it completes only when the visitor closes it
Reaching the last spread does not exit the preview; it announces the boundary and holds
Closing returns the visitor to the collection at exactly the scroll position they left
The previewed item returns to its closed state in its original slot
Its preview state resets to the opening spread rather than persisting where the visitor stopped
locked_observable_requirements: A calm, evenly spaced collection of front faces each labelled with a primary and secondary text line, every face openable
Opening is origin-anchored: the cover swings open and the object grows from its own place in the collection to fill the window
The focused view is a two-panel facing spread occupying the full window, not a single panel
The surrounding view drops away and its scrolling is held completely still for the full duration of the preview
Each turn press advances or reverses exactly one spread with a visible physical page-turn motion
Presses during an in-progress turn are ignored so the sequence never desynchronises
At the first and last spread the edge page lifts slightly and settles back rather than turning
Closing plays the opening in reverse back to the item's original slot with the cover shut
Closing restores the earlier scroll position exactly and resets the preview to its first spread
Touch and pointer activation produce identical behaviour
adaptable_details: Number of items and grid density or column count
Proportions and styling of the front faces and their labels
Duration, easing and depth cues of the opening, turning and closing motions
Number of spreads in the sample run
Placement and styling of the turn and close affordances
How strongly the surroundings drop away (dim, blur, fade or recede)
Subject matter and visual style of the interior content
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits collections whose entries have a distinct front face and a short, ordered, spread-shaped interior worth sampling — printed-work previews, look-books, brochures, illustrated stories, portfolio case sheets. It stops being this Skill if the focused view becomes a continuously scrolled single-column reader, if advance is free-form or multi-step rather than exactly one spread per press, if the focused view opens detached from the item's position instead of growing out of it, or if closing does not restore the collection to the exact spot and closed state it left.

name: tilted_texture_word_stage_with_treatment_switcher
description: One giant word sits centered on a tilted board in depth under a heavy soft shadow, its letterforms filled with texture; a header list swaps the stage for other word, texture and angle samples while marking the current one.

canonical_document.name: tilted_texture_word_stage_with_treatment_switcher
canonical_document.description: One giant word sits centered on a tilted board in depth under a heavy soft shadow, its letterforms filled with texture; a header list swaps the stage for other word, texture and angle samples while marking the current one.
canonical_document.experience_scope: Whole-view experience: begins on arrival with one sample already on stage and continues indefinitely as samples are exchanged in place; the persistent heading and treatment list frame the stage and never leave, so the experience has no exit point of its own.
content_and_composition: Exactly one oversized word occupies center stage at any moment, with its letterforms carrying an image or texture fill instead of a flat uniform fill
Small supporting copy sits beneath the word, deliberately minor in weight relative to it
The word and its fill read as a single tilted printed board placed in depth, lifted off the surface by one heavy soft shadow
A faint halo hugs the glyph edges of the oversized word as a default resting state
A persistent header holds a fixed heading plus a list of every available treatment, one entry per sample
One list entry is always visibly marked as the sample currently on stage; the rest read as still waiting to be compared
All samples share identical framing, so only the word, its texture and its tilt angle differ between them
experience_progression: Arrival: one sample already occupies the stage with its entry marked as current
Selection: the stage content is replaced by another sample's word, texture and angle while heading and list hold position
Open-ended comparison: any entry remains reachable from any sample, so samples can be revisited in any order
No terminal state or finish line; the payoff is repeated comparison rather than completion
attention_and_information_flow: Scale and texture pull attention to the filled letterforms first; the supporting copy stays secondary and is read after, if at all
Depth cues (tilt plus heavy soft shadow) separate the word from its surroundings and keep it the single focal object
The marked list entry continuously answers which treatment is on show, and the unmarked entries advertise how much remains to be compared
Because framing is constant across samples, attention lands on the differences that matter: the fill and the angle
Pointer contact on the word removes the halo, quieting the edge detail and letting the fill itself dominate

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The wash reverses as soon as the pointer leaves; hovering never changes which sample is on stage
interaction_model.state_change: Entry moves from resting to hovered
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The entry takes on a wash clearly separated in tone from the resting entries, previewing it as pickable
interaction_model.input: Pointer moved over a treatment entry in the header list
interaction_model.affected_object: That list entry

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Every entry stays reachable from every sample, so any earlier sample can be returned to directly in any order; picking the already-current entry leaves the view as it is
interaction_model.state_change: The stage is replaced with the chosen sample's word, texture and tilt angle; the marker moves to the chosen entry
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A different oversized word appears in the same framing with a new fill and new angle, while the heading and the list itself stay put; the chosen entry becomes visibly marked as current
interaction_model.input: Choosing a treatment entry in the header list
interaction_model.affected_object: The stage sample and the list's current marker

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The halo fades back in when the pointer leaves; leaving mid-fade returns it from wherever it reached, so the effect is fully reversible and never traps a state
interaction_model.state_change: Halo fades from present to absent over roughly a second
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The glow around the letter edges gradually dissolves, leaving the textured letterforms bare
interaction_model.input: Pointer resting on the oversized word
interaction_model.affected_object: The faint halo hugging the word's glyph edges

experience_qualities: Physical and poster-like: printed board rather than screen graphic
Quietly showing off rather than loud or busy
Weighty depth from tilt plus one heavy soft shadow
Legible orientation: the current sample and remaining samples are always obvious
Comparable by design, because constant framing isolates the fill and angle as the only variables
Calm, slow feedback on hover instead of snappy motion
completion_and_return: No completion state and no finish line; the view stays available indefinitely
Switching samples is a replacement in place, not a departure, so the surrounding heading and list persist across every switch
Selection state persists as the visible marker on the current entry until another entry is chosen
Halo hover state self-restores to its resting glow after the pointer leaves
locked_observable_requirements: Exactly one oversized word on stage at a time, with texture or imagery visible inside its letterforms
Supporting copy present but clearly subordinate to the word
Tilted presentation in depth with one heavy soft shadow reading as a lifted printed board
Identical framing across all samples so only word, texture and angle change
Persistent heading and treatment list that do not move when the stage changes
Always-visible marking of which treatment is currently on show
A clearly separated tonal wash on a list entry under the pointer before it is picked
Every treatment reachable from every sample, in any order
A faint glyph-edge halo that fades out over about a second while the pointer rests on the word and returns when it leaves
adaptable_details: The specific words used in each sample
The kind of texture or imagery filling the letterforms (photographic, material, patterned, graduated)
The number of samples in the list
The exact tilt angles chosen per sample
Typeface choice, letter weight and casing
Placement of the list within the header and its visual style of marking (as long as the current sample stays obvious)
Wording and length of the small supporting copy
Exact halo tint, spread and the precise fade duration around the one-second feel
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any context where a single short word or very brief phrase can carry the whole visual statement and where several alternative fills of that same idea are worth comparing side by side over time: showcase pages, hero openers, style or capability galleries, campaign statements. It does not transfer to long headlines, paragraph text or multi-item content grids, because the effect depends on one dominant letterform object in fixed framing. Showing multiple samples simultaneously, letting samples advance on their own, or dropping the constant framing so each sample gets its own layout would each create a different Skill, as would replacing the texture-in-letterform fill with a treatment applied around or behind flat single-tone type.

name: hinged_lid_tile_field
description: An edge-to-edge field of solid tiles sharing one uniform opaque tone, each holding one oversized character and each capped by a cover that hangs slightly ajar; hovering a tile swings its cover further open on its own hinge edge, raising the luminance of the face and deepening the interior shadow, then swinging back to rest when the pointer moves on.

canonical_document.name: hinged_lid_tile_field
canonical_document.description: An edge-to-edge field of solid tiles sharing one uniform opaque tone, each holding one oversized character and each capped by a cover that hangs slightly ajar; hovering a tile swings its cover further open on its own hinge edge, raising the luminance of the face and deepening the interior shadow, then swinging back to rest when the pointer moves on.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A region experience that can fill an entire view: it begins as soon as the tile field is visible in its collective resting state and continues indefinitely as the pointer moves across it; there is no entry gate, no end state and no separate detail view.
content_and_composition: One dense grid filling its container edge to edge with no visible gutters or framing chrome, so the many tiles read as a single continuous material surface
Many equivalent tiles, high enough in count that the field reads as a mass rather than a short list
Exactly one primary content item per tile, presented oversized so it dominates its own cell
Per tile, a two-layer stack: a recessed base holding the content item and a solid cover layer of the same material above it
A fixed hinge edge assigned per tile, varying across the field between left, right, top and bottom, so opening directions differ from neighbour to neighbour
An interior shadow cast under each raised cover, whose length and depth belong to that tile only
Persistent elements: the single uniform opaque tone shared by all tiles, the uniform tile size and spacing, and the collective slightly-ajar resting posture of every cover
experience_progression: Collective rest: every cover sits slightly ajar, the field reading as one calm textured surface with shallow uniform shadows
Focus: the pointed tile's cover swings further open around its hinge edge, gaining apparent depth as its face rises in luminance and its inner shadow stretches
Held focus: the opened tile remains the single raised, brighter element while all other tiles hold their resting posture
Release: the same motion runs backwards and the tile rejoins the collective resting state, leaving the field ready for the next tile without any accumulated change
attention_and_information_flow: At rest, prominence is evenly distributed so the impression is of density and material rather than of any individual item
Pointing narrows attention to exactly one tile through depth, luminance and shadow contrast rather than through hue change, outline or labelling
The revealed information is spatial rather than textual: the viewer learns that each flat cell is actually a lidded compartment with volume behind it
The varying hinge directions keep attention wandering, since each newly touched tile opens in a different direction than the last
Neighbouring tiles are deliberately unaffected, so the contrast between one raised tile and the flat field carries the whole emphasis
No instructional text, tooltip or callout ever appears; the motion alone teaches how the field responds

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Fully reversible at any moment; the tile owns its own state and needs no confirmation, click or selection
interaction_model.state_change: Cover rotates from its slightly-ajar resting angle to a further-open angle around its own fixed hinge edge; tile reads as gaining depth
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Cover swings away like a lid, the tile face rises slightly in luminance, and the shadow inside the tile lengthens and deepens as the gap grows
interaction_model.input: Pointer enters or rests over a single tile
interaction_model.affected_object: That tile's cover layer, face lighting and interior shadow

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Re-entering during the return motion reverses direction again from the current angle rather than snapping or restarting
interaction_model.state_change: Return from open angle back to the shared slightly-ajar resting angle
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The same swinging motion played in reverse, with luminance and shadow easing back to the resting appearance
interaction_model.input: Pointer leaves a tile
interaction_model.affected_object: The previously opened tile

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Interruption mid-motion is normal and safe; every tile always settles back to the shared resting posture regardless of how briefly it was touched
interaction_model.state_change: Each tile begins opening, then turns around from whatever partial angle it reached when the pointer left
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A trail of partially opened lids easing back down at their own pace, each hinging in its own direction, with no queueing, snapping or skipped frames
interaction_model.input: Pointer sweeps quickly across several tiles in a row
interaction_model.affected_object: Each tile touched along the path, independently

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Strict per-tile isolation is the boundary rule; effects never propagate across the grid
interaction_model.state_change: No state change
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Neighbours remain exactly at rest, with no bleed, ripple, dimming or group motion
interaction_model.input: Pointer over one tile while its neighbours are adjacent
interaction_model.affected_object: Neighbouring tiles

experience_qualities: Playful and tactile, like flipping open a wall of small lidded boxes
Material and monolithic at rest, as though the whole field were carved from one uniform solid slab
Calm rather than busy, because the resting state is nearly still and only one tile moves at a time
Physical and mechanical, with motion constrained to a hinge rather than free floating
Immediate and low-commitment, since nothing is selected, opened permanently or navigated to
Self-explanatory, inviting sweeping exploration without instructions
completion_and_return: No completion or terminal state; the experience idles indefinitely
Every tile always returns to the shared slightly-ajar resting angle, so the field self-heals to its original appearance
No persistent state is kept: previously hovered tiles retain no visited or opened appearance
Multiple partially open tiles may coexist transiently during fast movement, but all resolve back to rest on their own
locked_observable_requirements: A dense edge-to-edge field of uniform tiles sharing one opaque tone, reading as one continuous solid material rather than as separated cards
One oversized content item per tile, filling its cell
A cover layer per tile that rotates around a fixed hinge edge; motion is hinged rotation, never scaling, sliding, fading or lifting straight up
Hinge edges vary across the field between left, right, top and bottom
A shared resting state in which all covers sit slightly ajar rather than fully closed or fully open
Hover-only activation with no click, tap-to-select or navigation required
Coordinated triple feedback on the active tile: increased open angle, a slight rise in face luminance, and a stretching interior shadow
Strict single-tile isolation, with neighbours visually untouched
Symmetric reverse motion on pointer exit that can turn around from any partial angle without snapping
adaptable_details: The specific content type inside tiles, as long as each item is single, short and oversized within its cell
Exact tone, value and surface finish of the tile material, provided it stays uniform across every tile and leaves headroom for the luminance rise
Grid density, tile count, tile aspect ratio and how the grid reflows across viewport sizes
Resting ajar angle, open angle, easing curve and motion duration
The distribution pattern of hinge directions across the field, whether alternating, grouped or arbitrary
Exact luminance-rise amount and shadow length, softness and direction
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any large set of short, equivalent, glanceable items that can each occupy one uniform cell and be shown as a dense field — glyphs, icons, symbols, swatches, tags, small thumbnails. It stops fitting when items need long text, unequal sizes, or per-item detail content, because the tile can only reveal depth and shadow, not additional information. Making the cover fully open to expose hidden content, requiring a click, persisting an opened state, animating groups or the whole grid together, or replacing hinged rotation with lifting, scaling, tilting or flipping would each create a different Skill.

name: speck_gathered_form_and_word_stepper
description: One abstract form and its name stand alone at center, each built from countless specks that swarm into place, keep quietly stirring, then fly apart and re-gather as the next form and word when the viewer steps forward or back; dragging across the scene pulls nearby specks into a trailing swirl that drifts home on its own.

canonical_document.name: speck_gathered_form_and_word_stepper
canonical_document.description: One abstract form and its name stand alone at center, each built from countless specks that swarm into place, keep quietly stirring, then fly apart and re-gather as the next form and word when the viewer steps forward or back; dragging across the scene pulls nearby specks into a trailing swirl that drifts home on its own.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A self-contained scene region that owns one full-attention stage: it begins with the first form assembling on arrival and continues indefinitely as the viewer steps through the bounded set; it never hands off to a second simultaneous focus and has no terminal end state.
content_and_composition: Exactly one featured abstract form at a time, centered and dominant, rendered as a dense field of small specks rather than a solid graphic
One short name for the current form, seated just beneath it and also composed of specks that resolve into readable lettering
A per-item two-tone pairing applied across the speck field, its hues unspecified, with the two tones separated enough to read as a pair and the pairing held distinct from those of neighbouring items
Two round stepping controls, one at each side of the scene, on the same layer as and flanking the centered form
A low-distraction surround, assumed neither light nor dark, so the speck field and its label are the only foreground content
A short, fixed, clearly bounded set of items whose extent is legible from the presence or absence of the side controls
experience_progression: Arrival: scattered loose specks converge into the first form while its lettering assembles beneath, readable within a second or two
Settling: the item's two-tone pairing creeps in as the form comes to rest, carrying enough contrast against the surround to keep the speck lettering readable
Resting: the assembled form and word hold their identity while never appearing fully frozen, with continuous low-amplitude stirring
Stepping: on a directional step the current form and lettering flow apart into loose specks and re-gather as the neighboring form and its word, with the new tone pairing creeping in
The same dispersal-and-regather motion plays in reverse direction when walking back, so movement between neighbors always reads as one shared mechanism
The sequence has no finale; it remains at whichever item the viewer last chose
attention_and_information_flow: Attention rests on a single form at a time; nothing else competes for focus
Meaning arrives in order: silhouette first, then its name, then its tone pairing
During a step, legibility is briefly surrendered to motion and then restored, making the change itself the moment of interest
Position within the set is communicated only by which side controls are present, keeping ahead/behind availability obvious without a written index
Pointer play redirects attention to the material of the image itself rather than to any new content

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Assembly is brief and self-completing; the resting state remains gently in motion so the scene never looks stalled
interaction_model.state_change: Scattered specks resolve into the assembled form and readable label with its tone pairing applied
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Loose specks stream inward and tighten into shape and lettering, the pairing seeping in as motion slows
interaction_model.input: First view of the scene
interaction_model.affected_object: First form, its name and the surrounding speck field

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The opposite control retraces the same path back to the previous item; a step in progress resolves into a settled item rather than an ambiguous middle state
interaction_model.state_change: Current item disperses and the neighboring item in that direction assembles in its place
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Form and word break into travelling specks that re-cohere as the neighboring shape and word while the neighbour's distinct two-tone pairing arrives
interaction_model.input: Activating the forward or back round side control
interaction_model.affected_object: Current form and its lettering, plus the tone pairing

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The control reappears as soon as a move in its direction becomes possible again; the ends cannot be overshot
interaction_model.state_change: That control is absent and unactivatable while no neighbor exists in its direction
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Only the control for a possible move is shown, so the boundary of the set is visible rather than announced by a failed press
interaction_model.input: Reaching either end of the set
interaction_model.affected_object: The directional control for the unavailable direction

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Captured specks drift back to their places on their own once the pointer moves away or the touch ends, restoring the form without any explicit reset
interaction_model.state_change: Nearby specks are captured out of their resting arrangement into orbiting, trailing motion around the moving point
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A live wake of specks trails and circles the pointer, temporarily loosening the form where it passes
interaction_model.input: Sliding a pointer or finger across the scene
interaction_model.affected_object: Specks near the moving point

experience_qualities: Playful and toy-like: the image invites disturbance and repairs itself
Continuously alive: nothing ever reads as a frozen still frame
Legible quickly: the form and its name resolve within a second or two
Focused and uncluttered: one subject, one word, one tone pairing at a time
Materially soft: transformations read as swarming rather than sliding or cutting
Bounded and safe: the viewer can always tell whether more remains ahead or behind
completion_and_return: No completion state; the scene rests on the last chosen item with ongoing idle stirring
Stepping is fully reversible in both directions along the same visual path
Pointer disturbance always self-resolves back to the settled arrangement
The set does not wrap around; the ends are hard stops expressed by control absence
locked_observable_requirements: Both the featured form and its name are built from the same field of discrete specks
Initial assembly from scattered specks reaches readability within about a second or two
Only one featured item holds attention at any moment

Each item carries its own two-tone pairing that arrives as the form settles, distinct from its neighbours' pairing and contrasting enough with the surround to keep the speck lettering readable, with no particular hues required
The resting state is never fully static
Transitions between neighbors happen by dispersal and re-gathering of the same specks, for both directions
A directional control exists and is actionable only while a move in that direction is possible, making the set's boundaries visible
Pointer or touch movement captures nearby specks into trailing, circling motion and they return to place unaided when it stops
adaptable_details: Number of items in the short set
Specific silhouettes used as featured forms
The hues chosen for each item's tone pair, and how the surround sits in luminance relative to them
Speck count, size and density
Exact assembly, dispersal and return timing within a quick, readable range
Radius and strength of pointer capture
Styling and iconography of the round side controls
Typeface and size of the assembled label
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits a short, curated set of single-subject items whose visuals reduce to bold, low-detail silhouettes or emblems paired with one short name, presented as a full-attention centerpiece. It still fits if the forms become logos, glyphs or simple product outlines, and it adopts whatever tone pairs and surround luminance the host setting supplies. It becomes a different Skill if items grow to a long or open-ended list, if content requires photographic or fine detail that specks cannot carry, if several items must be visible or comparable at once, if the label expands into paragraphs of reading material, or if advancing becomes automatic or scroll-driven rather than a deliberate step between neighbors.

name: circular_disc_flip_slideshow
description: A single round frame holds one captioned image; hovering either half fades in a tilted arrow hint, and pressing that half flips the disc over around an axis through the pressed point to reveal the neighbouring image, endlessly in both directions.

canonical_document.name: circular_disc_flip_slideshow
canonical_document.description: A single round frame holds one captioned image; hovering either half fades in a tilted arrow hint, and pressing that half flips the disc over around an axis through the pressed point to reveal the neighbouring image, endlessly in both directions.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A self-contained centered region occupying the visual center of the view: the round frame, its caption and its hover hints. The experience begins when the pointer enters a half of the frame and ends when a flip settles into a still, fully readable image; nothing outside the frame region moves or changes.
content_and_composition: One circular frame centered in the view, clipping the artwork to a disc and acting as the only focal object
Exactly one visible image at rest, drawn from a small ordered set of a handful of items
One short text label per image, subordinate to the picture and readable only in the settled state
Two invisible interactive halves of the frame, left and right, each mapped to one direction through the set
One small transient direction marker per hovered half, positioned inside that half and tilted according to how high or low the pointer sits within it
Generous quiet space around the frame so no competing content shares the attention band
experience_progression: Rest: a still, clean, fully readable image with its label
Anticipation: pointer enters a half and a direction marker fades in, tilting as the pointer moves
Commit: press or tap turns the disc, pivoting around an axis that passes through the pressed spot, with springy weighted motion
Arrival: motion settles without residual wobble into a still, undistorted, fully readable neighbouring image and its label
The sequence repeats indefinitely in either direction and wraps from either end back to the opposite end, so the set never presents an end stop
attention_and_information_flow: The circular silhouette and centered placement hold attention on the picture; the label is a secondary read
Direction hints appear only on hover and only in the hovered half, so navigation affordances stay dormant until intent is shown
During the flip the image is transitional and not meant to be read; readability is deliberately restored only at arrival
Direction of travel is legible before and during the change, from the hint side and from the pivot and turning direction

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Moving to the other half swaps which marker shows; leaving the frame fades the marker out with no other change
interaction_model.state_change: Marker becomes visible for the hovered side and continuously reorients
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Marker fades in inside that half, tilted to match the pointer's vertical position within the half, tracking as the pointer moves
interaction_model.input: Pointer moves into the left or right half of the frame
interaction_model.affected_object: Small direction marker for that half

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Pressing the opposite half after arrival returns to the previous image by an equivalent turn in the opposite direction, making every step reversible
interaction_model.state_change: Advances one step through the set in that half's direction
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The disc turns over with springy physical motion around an axis passing through the pressed point, then settles into the neighbouring image, still and fully readable, with its label
interaction_model.input: Press or tap on one half of the frame
interaction_model.affected_object: The disc holding the artwork and its label

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Input becomes effective again once the turn has settled, so rapid presses degrade into single clean steps
interaction_model.state_change: None; the input is ignored
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The current turn continues undisturbed and settles normally, with no queued or stacked motion
interaction_model.input: Press or tap while a turn is already running
interaction_model.affected_object: The in-progress turn

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Wrapping is available in both directions, so browsing can continue indefinitely either way
interaction_model.state_change: Wraps to the opposite end
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The turn looks identical to any other step, with no bounce, block or edge signal, so the set reads as endless
interaction_model.input: Stepping past the first or last item of the set
interaction_model.affected_object: Position within the ordered set

experience_qualities: Physical and weighted, like turning over a solid disc rather than fading a panel
Springy and lively on arrival but conclusively still once settled
Focused and calm, with a single object of attention
Directionally legible, so the user always knows which way through the set they are heading
Endless and forgiving, with no dead ends and no punishment for impatient input
completion_and_return: Every step completes in a fully settled, undistorted, readable image and label state
The set loops endlessly in both directions with no terminal state
Each step is reversible by pressing the opposite half, returning to the previously seen image
Hover hints leave no residue once the pointer leaves the frame
locked_observable_requirements: A single centered circular frame is the only focal container and clips the artwork to a disc
Exactly one item is shown at rest, accompanied by one short label
The frame is split into two direction halves whose hover reveals a small tilted direction marker whose tilt follows pointer height within that half
Pressing a half turns the disc over toward the neighbouring item, pivoting around an axis passing through the pressed point
Turning motion reads as springy and physical, and every arrival settles into a still, clean, fully readable image
Input during a turn is ignored rather than queued
Traversal wraps at both ends so the set never appears to run out
adaptable_details: Number of items in the small set
Subject matter of the imagery and wording of the labels
Frame size, border treatment, backdrop and label placement relative to the frame
Exact springiness, duration and easing character of the turn
Shape, size, styling and fade timing of the direction marker
Whether keyboard or swipe input maps to the same directional steps
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits small ordered sets of single-focus visual items with short labels that benefit from being the centerpiece of a low-density view: artwork, photography, product shots, portfolio stills, illustrated highlights or quote cards. It stops being this Skill if multiple items are visible at once, if the frame stops being a single round disc-like object, if the change becomes a slide, fade or scroll rather than a pivoted turn about the pressed point, if the set gains visible ends, or if items carry dense readable content that must remain legible during the transition.

name: stepped_exhibition_room_circuit
description: A hushed exhibition room where framed items line lit walls above a visible floor, one item is held centred while its neighbours recede to the sides, footstep markers step the visitor along the wall and swing the view around each corner of a closed circuit, and a tiny caption card rises into a large readable detail panel that lowers again to the exact paused position.

canonical_document.name: stepped_exhibition_room_circuit
canonical_document.description: A hushed exhibition room where framed items line lit walls above a visible floor, one item is held centred while its neighbours recede to the sides, footstep markers step the visitor along the wall and swing the view around each corner of a closed circuit, and a tiny caption card rises into a large readable detail panel that lowers again to the exact paused position.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A whole-view experience that begins the moment the view is entered, already standing inside the room with one item centred, and continues indefinitely as the visitor walks the circuit; the detail reading is a nested sub-experience that opens and closes inside it without ending the walk.
content_and_composition: One primary visual item held centred and largest, read as the current focus
Immediate neighbouring items visible to left and right, smaller and receding toward the edges, showing that the collection continues
Wall surface with directed lighting above a visible floor plane, giving the room its depth and grounding the items
A small caption card attached to each item, tiny and quiet at rest
One detail panel, absent at rest, appearing large and legible in front of the room when raised
Two persistent footprint-style step markers fixed at the bottom of the view, one per travel direction
A small close control belonging to the raised detail panel
Multiple walls arranged so that the ends of one wall meet the adjoining wall, forming a closed loop of items
experience_progression: Arrival: the room is already inhabited, with one item centred and neighbours receding
Lateral advance: repeated steps move focus item by item along the current wall, each step re-centring the next item and pushing the previous one aside
Corner turn: a forward step taken at the last item of a wall swings the view around the corner onto the adjoining wall instead of stopping
Circuit: continued travel in either direction wraps through all walls and returns to the starting item, so the tour never dead-ends
Detail reading: a reversible sub-stage in which the caption's full text is raised for reading and then lowered, returning the walk to the same paused position
attention_and_information_flow: Prominence is concentrated on the single centred item; off-centre items are legible as context but visibly subordinate
At rest only a minimal caption identifies the centred item, keeping the room quiet and the image dominant
On demand the full text takes over as the largest legible element, temporarily outranking the item and the room
When the panel lowers, prominence returns to the centred item with no change in position along the walk
Corner turns reveal a new stretch of the collection while retaining the same centred-item reading pattern

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Both directions are always available, so any step can be undone by one step the other way; further steps and clicks are ignored until the current move settles
interaction_model.state_change: Focus moves one item in the chosen direction; the neighbour becomes the centred item and the former focus recedes to the opposite side
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A single continuous travel move along the wall, with items growing toward the centre and shrinking toward the edges and the caption card following the new focus
interaction_model.input: Activating one of the two footprint step markers at the bottom
interaction_model.affected_object: The room view and the set of items on the current wall

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Wrapping works in both directions, so a step back turns the corner in reverse; no end of wall ever blocks travel; input remains ignored until the turn settles
interaction_model.state_change: The view turns the corner onto the adjoining wall and centres its first item, wrapping the circuit rather than stopping
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The view swings around the corner, the previous wall leaves the frame and the next wall's items come into view with one held centred
interaction_model.input: Taking a forward step while the last item of the current wall is centred
interaction_model.affected_object: The whole room view

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Ignored while another move is still settling; the previous position can be regained by stepping or clicking back
interaction_model.state_change: Focus travels directly to that item and it becomes the centred one
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A single continuous move that passes the intervening items and ends with the clicked item held centred and largest
interaction_model.input: Clicking an off-centre item
interaction_model.affected_object: The clicked item and the room view

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Any already-open panel retracts before the new one appears, so only one is ever raised; the walk position is untouched
interaction_model.state_change: If the item is off-centre it is first brought to the centre, then the detail panel is raised for that item
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The travel move resolves first, then the full text rises into view large and legible in front of the room while the tiny caption gives way to it
interaction_model.input: Clicking the caption card of an item
interaction_model.affected_object: The clicked item and the detail panel

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The walk resumes from the identical position with no drift, re-centring or loss of place
interaction_model.state_change: The panel lowers and the item returns to its resting state with only the tiny caption card
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The full text recedes back out of view, leaving the centred item and the room exactly as they were
interaction_model.input: Activating the small close control on the raised panel
interaction_model.affected_object: The detail panel

experience_qualities: Quiet, hushed and unhurried, like an exhibition hall rather than a feed
Inhabited and spatial: floor, lit wall and corners make the collection feel like a place
Deliberate, one-piece-at-a-time attention with clear peripheral context
Continuous and endless, with no dead ends in either direction
Calm and settled motion in which each move completes before another begins
Reading feels like leaning in and then stepping back, never like leaving the room
completion_and_return: The walk has no completion state; the circuit loops in both directions indefinitely
Detail reading always completes by lowering the panel and returning to the resting caption
Position along the walk persists across opening and closing details, so the visitor is left exactly where they paused
Only one detail panel exists at a time; opening another implies the previous one has closed
locked_observable_requirements: Exactly one item is held centred and dominant at any moment, with neighbours visibly receding toward the sides
The room reads as a space: items hang on a lit wall above a visible floor
Walls form a closed circuit joined at corners, and travel wraps in both directions with no dead end
A forward move at a wall's last item turns the corner onto the adjoining wall rather than stopping or jumping
Two footprint-style step markers at the bottom are the primary travel control, one per direction
At rest each item shows only a tiny caption card; the full text appears only on demand as a large legible panel
Clicking an off-centre item travels straight to it; clicking its caption centres it first and then raises the panel
A small close control lowers the panel, and an open panel retracts before another is raised
Steps and clicks are ignored until the current move settles
Closing the panel returns the view to the exact paused position along the walk
adaptable_details: Number of walls and number of items per wall
Framing, matting and lighting style of the items and the floor material
Proportions, placement and styling of the detail panel and its close control
Visual styling of the footprint markers and their labels
Travel and turn timing, easing and camera feel
Caption wording, length and typography of the detail text
Whether additional wall dressing such as baseboards, spotlights or shadows is present
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits an ordered, curated collection of flat visual items where each item has a short label and a longer body of text worth reading, and where the count is small enough that walking item by item stays pleasant. Content type matters only in that each item must be a single framed visual that can hang on a wall. Replacing the centred-one-at-a-time focus with a simultaneous grid or list, replacing the guided step-and-turn travel with free-roam camera control, opening details as a separate destination view, or dropping the closed circuit so travel dead-ends at the last item would each create a different Skill.
