canonical_document.name: lever_pulled_chance_wheel_booth
canonical_document.description: An illustrated booth holding a big numbered wheel and an upright lever: enter through an animated title card, watch the first spin run itself, then pull the lever down against a hard stop, release, and wait out a long coast-down until a panel swings open with the number.
canonical_document.experience_scope: Whole-view experience that begins with a full-viewport illustrated entry card, hands over to a live booth scene filling the viewport, and continues indefinitely round after round with no terminal end; the entry card belongs to the experience only as its opening stage.
content_and_composition: One full-view illustrated entry card as the opening layer, carrying animated lettering as its headline and exactly one control to go in.
One staged booth scene revealed beneath, occupying the entire viewport, with an illustrated surrounding environment framing it.
Exactly one large numbered chance wheel as the focal object of the scene.
One upright lever standing beside the wheel, visually part of the booth and the only manipulable control.
One pointer or marker fixed relative to the wheel that designates the landed segment.
One result panel positioned with the booth, closed by default, that opens to display a single winning number.
Persistent elements across rounds: booth, wheel, lever, pointer, environment and the visitor's current viewing angle and distance.
experience_progression: Entry card holds the view while its lettering animates an invitation; nothing of the scene is usable yet.
Visitor confirms entry, the card clears, and the booth is handed over with prominence settling on the lever beside the wheel.
A first round plays out unprompted: the wheel turns and enters a long slowdown, demonstrating the ritual without instruction.
The wheel settles on a segment and the result panel swings open, presenting the winning number.
The number remains legibly on show for as long as the visitor wants, with no timer and no auto-advance.
The visitor starts a new pull; the panel closes first, the wheel spins again, and the new number appears after it settles, looping indefinitely.
attention_and_information_flow: Animated lettering owns attention first and the scene is withheld entirely behind the card.
On dismissal prominence transfers to the lever, marking it as the thing to touch, with the wheel as the large secondary focus.
During a held pull attention concentrates on the lever's proportional travel and its refusal to move past the stop.
During the spin the wheel carries attention, and the long deceleration stretches anticipation as the pointer narrows toward one segment.
Once settled, attention moves to the opened panel, the only place a readable value appears.
Information is deliberately withdrawn before it is replaced: the old number is closed away before the next one is revealed, so exactly one outcome is ever readable.

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: One-way transition; the entry card does not return for the rest of the session
interaction_model.state_change: Card is dismissed and the scene becomes live with a round already starting
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The card clears away to expose the booth, and the wheel begins turning without further input
interaction_model.input: Activating the single control on the entry card
interaction_model.affected_object: Entry card layer and the booth scene behind it

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Cannot be skipped or interrupted; it resolves into the same resting state a manual round produces
interaction_model.state_change: Wheel spins, decelerates and settles, then the panel opens
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A complete spin-to-result cycle plays out on its own so the ritual reads as self-explanatory
interaction_model.input: Autonomous first round immediately after entry
interaction_model.affected_object: Wheel and result panel

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Dragging upward or reversing mid-pull banks nothing further; the visitor may hold as long as they like without committing
interaction_model.state_change: Lever swings down in proportion to how far the pointer has travelled until a hard stop; banked force grows with that travel and is itself capped
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The lever visibly follows the pull, resists past its limit, and holding it builds tension before anything spins
interaction_model.input: Pressing on the lever and dragging downward
interaction_model.affected_object: Lever and the spin force being banked

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The spin cannot be interrupted or re-aimed once released; the settled outcome persists until a new pull begins
interaction_model.state_change: Lever returns to rest while the wheel independently spins with the banked force, slows and settles on a segment, after which the panel opens
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A snap back to rest, a long coast-down on the wheel, then the panel swinging open with the number
interaction_model.input: Releasing the lever
interaction_model.affected_object: Lever, wheel and result panel

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The previous value is not recoverable; each round shows exactly one value
interaction_model.state_change: Open panel closes before the new spin resolves
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The panel swings shut and clears the old number so the next outcome arrives on an empty stage
interaction_model.input: Beginning another pull while a result is displayed
interaction_model.affected_object: Result panel

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Movement is clamped rather than blocked, can be released at any moment, and the resulting framing persists into later rounds
interaction_model.state_change: Viewpoint swings around the booth and moves nearer or further within fixed bounds
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The scene reframes continuously as the visitor looks around, and stops firmly at the near, far and angular limits
interaction_model.input: Pressing and dragging anywhere other than the lever
interaction_model.affected_object: Viewpoint on the booth

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Viewpoint control resumes as soon as the lever is released, ensuring a pull is never mistaken for a look-around
interaction_model.state_change: Viewpoint control is suspended for the duration of the hold
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The framing stays completely still while pulling, so the scene never drifts mid-pull
interaction_model.input: Holding the lever
interaction_model.affected_object: Viewpoint movement

experience_qualities: Playful, fairground-attraction mood established before the scene is even shown
Tactile and mechanical: the control moves with the hand and refuses to exceed its limit
Anticipation carried by a long, unhurried slowdown rather than an instant answer
Self-explanatory through demonstration instead of instruction
Calm reading moment at the payoff, with no pressure to move on
Explorable staging that lets the visitor choose their vantage on the apparatus
Clear separation between looking and acting, so neither interferes with the other
completion_and_return: No terminal completion; the experience loops one round at a time for as long as the visitor stays.
Each round completes when the wheel settles and the panel opens, and that state holds indefinitely.
Reset is implicit and visitor-triggered: starting a new pull closes the panel and returns the scene to its pre-result state.
The lever always returns to rest on its own after each release.
Viewing angle and distance persist across rounds; the entry card never reappears.
locked_observable_requirements: An opening full-view card with animated lettering that is dismissed by a single control directly into the live scene.
The first round runs autonomously, with no pull required, so the ritual is demonstrated before it is asked for.
A single manipulable lever beside the wheel is the only way to spin it.
Downward pull moves the lever in proportion to pointer travel and meets a hard stop.
Banked spin force is capped, and upward or reversed dragging contributes nothing.
Release snaps the lever back to rest while the wheel keeps turning independently.
A long deceleration to a definite stop precedes the existence of any result.
The outcome is delivered by a panel that swings open and stays legible until the visitor chooses to go again.
Starting the next pull closes the panel before the new value appears, so only one value is ever readable.
Free orbiting and distance change within fixed bounds, suspended while the lever is held.
adaptable_details: Illustration style, colour treatment, era and props of the booth and surroundings
Number of wheel segments and the value range shown
Whether the outcome is a number or another short value such as a word, prize or action
Shape, size and placement of the lever and result panel
Exact spin duration, deceleration curve and snap-back timing
Wording and typography of the entry card and the animation used on its lettering
Size of the viewing bounds and the starting framing of the scene
Presence of sound or ambient motion in the environment
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits single-outcome chance and randomizer experiences where one short value is the payoff and one physically manipulated control in a staged, navigable scene is the attraction. It stays the same skill across different scene styles, outcome vocabularies and wheel layouts. It becomes a different skill if the pull is replaced by an instant click with no proportional travel or cap, if the result appears during or before the wheel settles instead of after, if several outcomes are produced or compared at once, if the result no longer persists until the visitor acts, or if the scene is reduced to a small inline widget with no viewpoint control or pushed behind foreground text as a background substrate.

name: sketched_underline_oversized_word_row
description: A near-empty screen-height view of a few oversized centered words where hovering one draws a rough, freshly-sketched underline across its full width that is never the same shape twice, and retracts itself when the pointer leaves.

canonical_document.name: sketched_underline_oversized_word_row
canonical_document.description: A near-empty screen-height view of a few oversized centered words where hovering one draws a rough, freshly-sketched underline across its full width that is never the same shape twice, and retracts itself when the pointer leaves.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A whole-view experience occupying one screen-height composition; it begins on arrival with the resting row visible and has no end state, with the marking sub-experience beginning and ending per pointer visit to a single label. Only one mark exists at a time and nothing accumulates.
content_and_composition: A small set of oversized text labels, each also acting as a chosen destination; the supplied case uses three and the effect depends on the set staying short enough to read at a glance
Labels arranged as a single row read left to right, centered in the view both horizontally and vertically
The words are the entire composition: surrounding space is deliberately empty, with no competing imagery, decoration or dense supporting text
A single transient stroke layer sitting directly beneath the text baseline of exactly one label at a time, spanning that label's full width
The stroke's visual character is rough and hand-sketched, reading as drawn by hand in the moment rather than as a precise geometric rule
Resting state has no mark at all, so every label carries equal visual weight
experience_progression: Resting: bare row, all labels equally readable
Marking: stroke sweeps in from one end to the other under the hovered label and settles
Held: stroke persists, fully drawn, while attention stays on that label
Unmarking: same stroke retracts toward its far end until the label is bare
Return to resting, with the next visit producing a differently shaped stroke
attention_and_information_flow: On arrival the whole short choice set is grasped simultaneously because nothing is emphasized
The drawing stroke is the only moving element, so it becomes the sole focus and confirms which choice is currently singled out
Prominence is exclusive: marking one label implicitly de-emphasizes the others without changing them
Removing the mark restores flat, equal readability so no residue biases the next glance

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The draw runs to completion; leaving mid-draw does not cut it short
interaction_model.state_change: From no mark to a fully drawn mark
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A rough stroke sweeps from one end of the label to the other, spanning its full width, settling in roughly half a second with a smooth accelerate-then-decelerate feel; its shape differs from the previous stroke
interaction_model.input: Pointer enters a label
interaction_model.affected_object: The stroke layer beneath that label's text

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Fully reversible; the label returns exactly to its resting appearance
interaction_model.state_change: From drawn mark back to no mark
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The same stroke retracts toward its far end until the text is bare again
interaction_model.input: Pointer leaves a label
interaction_model.affected_object: That label's stroke

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Repeated entry during the draw is absorbed rather than replayed
interaction_model.state_change: No state change; the draw continues undisturbed
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The stroke keeps advancing smoothly with no visible restart, jump or re-seed of its shape
interaction_model.input: Pointer re-enters a label while its stroke is still drawing
interaction_model.affected_object: The in-progress stroke

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Queued rather than interrupted, so the mark is never left as a half stroke
interaction_model.state_change: Draw completes first, then retraction begins
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The stroke finishes sweeping to full width and only then pulls back toward its far end
interaction_model.input: Pointer leaves a label while its stroke is still drawing
interaction_model.affected_object: The in-progress stroke

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Rapid back-and-forth pointer movement stays responsive and never leaves a stranded partial mark
interaction_model.state_change: Retraction is cancelled and a new mark begins immediately
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The receding stroke stops receding and a freshly shaped stroke draws in at once, with no waiting for the old one to finish
interaction_model.input: Pointer re-enters a label while its stroke is retracting
interaction_model.affected_object: The retracting stroke

experience_qualities: Calm and almost empty at rest
Handmade, lively and slightly imperfect rather than mechanical
Instantly legible because the choice set is tiny and unadorned
Responsive and forgiving under fast pointer movement
Non-accumulating: the view always returns to the same quiet baseline
completion_and_return: No terminal state; the view loops between resting and marked indefinitely
Each pointer visit completes with either a fully drawn mark or a fully cleared label, never a stalled fragment
No mark persists after the pointer leaves, and no label retains a trace of having been visited
Only one label is marked at any moment
locked_observable_requirements: One screen-height view whose whole composition is a few oversized centered words, with deliberate emptiness around them
Exactly one label marked at a time, and no mark in the resting state
The mark is a stroke underline spanning the hovered label's full width, positioned beneath its text
The mark reads as rough and freshly hand-drawn, and its shape is never repeated identically
The mark draws directionally from one end to the other and retracts toward its far end, using the same stroke rather than fading
Draw settles in roughly half a second with a smooth ease-in-then-out feel
Re-entry during drawing must not restart the draw
Leaving during drawing lets the draw complete before retracting
Re-entry during retraction cancels the retraction and immediately starts a fresh mark
Labels themselves stay visually unchanged so all choices remain equally readable
adaptable_details: Number of labels, as long as the set stays short enough to grasp at a glance
Wording of the labels and what they lead to
Typeface, letter case, and the stroke's tone or thickness, as long as the stroke stays plainly separated from both the label text and the surrounding emptiness
Sweep direction and which end the retraction pulls toward
Exact roughness character of the stroke and how much it varies between visits
Row arrangement adapting to narrow viewports as long as the words remain the whole composition
Small timing adjustments around the roughly half-second settle
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any short set of large text choices that should own an entire quiet view — entry screens, service or section pickers, minimal menus — where the content is a handful of words rather than dense copy. It stops being this Skill if the mark becomes a precise, always-identical geometric rule or a simple fade, if the labels themselves transform (scale, tone shift, move) instead of receiving a separate mark, if multiple marks can be visible at once or a mark persists as a selected state, if the mark is applied to dense body text or long lists where full-width strokes lose their poster-like clarity, or if the composition gains competing imagery and supporting content so the words are no longer the whole view.

name: oversized_morphing_toggle_on_calm_stage_with_confetti_spray
description: A calm, nearly empty field with one oversized two-state icon at its center, the icon clearly separated from its low-distraction surround; each press bends and travels the icon's outline into the opposite symbol while a spray of small dots in assorted distinguishable tones flies out from the pointer, arcs, falls and fades, leaving the stage clean and ready for another press.

canonical_document.name: oversized_morphing_toggle_on_calm_stage_with_confetti_spray
canonical_document.description: A calm, nearly empty field with one oversized two-state icon at its center, the icon clearly separated from its low-distraction surround; each press bends and travels the icon's outline into the opposite symbol while a spray of small dots in assorted distinguishable tones flies out from the pointer, arcs, falls and fades, leaving the stage clean and ready for another press.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A whole-view experience for a small single-purpose page, or a self-contained focal region: it begins on arrival with the resting state visible and has no end state — it loops indefinitely between the two states, each press producing a complete transform-plus-flourish cycle that returns the view to calm.
content_and_composition: One oversized focal mark occupying the dominant share of the view, centered in an otherwise near-empty field
A low-detail backdrop layer of uniform low-distraction tone that serves as calm negative space and is itself pressable
Exactly two mutually exclusive symbol states of the same mark; the currently active state is unambiguously readable at rest
A transient particle layer of many small dots in assorted tones, each readable against the backdrop, rendered above it and around the focal mark, existing only briefly after each press
Optional minimal supporting text or label kept subordinate so it never competes with the focal mark
No panels, menus, or secondary controls competing for attention
experience_progression: Arrival: uncluttered low-distraction field, oversized mark at rest in strong separation from its surround, current state obvious
Press: outline of the mark begins bending and travelling toward the opposite form while dots launch from the pointer position
Flourish: dots arc outward, slow, fall and fade while the mark settles into its new form
Return to calm: particles fully disappear, view is clean again with the new state at rest
Loop: the next press repeats the cycle in the opposite direction, indefinitely and in either order
attention_and_information_flow: At rest, nearly all prominence belongs to the single oversized mark because of scale and surrounding emptiness
During the change, attention splits briefly between the reshaping outline and the outward-flying dots, then collapses back onto the mark
The only information carried is which of the two states is active; it is legible before, during and after the change because the same mark persists
Transient particles never obscure the mark long enough to hide state, and leave no lasting visual residue

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Fully reversible by pressing again; a press during an in-progress change is accepted and the mark continues from its current shape toward the newly targeted form without snapping or being ignored
interaction_model.state_change: Active state flips to the opposite state
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The outline bends and travels continuously into the new symbol as one deforming mark rather than a swap, cut or cross-fade
interaction_model.input: Single press on the oversized focal mark
interaction_model.affected_object: The focal mark's outline

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Self-clearing with no cleanup required; overlapping sprays from rapid presses coexist and each expires independently, and no spray blocks or intercepts a following press
interaction_model.state_change: A scattered spray of dots is emitted and then self-expires
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Dots scatter outward from the exact press point, arc, fall, fade and vanish on their own without any dismissal action
interaction_model.input: The same single press, at its pointer position
interaction_model.affected_object: Transient dot layer of assorted tones

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Harmless and repeatable; backdrop presses can never alter or corrupt the two-state reading of the mark
interaction_model.state_change: No change to the mark's state
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Spray appears at the pressed point while the focal mark stays exactly as it was
interaction_model.input: Press on the empty backdrop away from the mark
interaction_model.affected_object: Transient dot layer of assorted tones only

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Every press remains responsive; returning to the original state is always one press away and feels no heavier than leaving it
interaction_model.state_change: Alternating states with stacked, independently expiring sprays
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Continuous back-and-forth reshaping with layered bursts, never a frozen or half-broken symbol
interaction_model.input: Rapid repeated presses
interaction_model.affected_object: Focal mark and particle layer together

experience_qualities: Calm, uncluttered, strongly separated from its surround and focused at rest
Playful and rewarding on interaction, inviting an immediate second try
Continuous and physical: shape change reads as bending material, not symbol substitution
Light and consequence-free — nothing accumulates, nothing must be dismissed
Symmetrically effortless in both directions
completion_and_return: Each press cycle completes on its own when the mark settles and the last dot fades
The view always returns to a clean calm state with no leftover particles
No terminal state: the experience loops between the two states for as long as the user keeps pressing
The active state persists visibly at rest until the next press; either state is a valid resting state
locked_observable_requirements: Exactly one oversized focal mark dominating an otherwise near-empty low-distraction field, clearly separated from it
The currently active state is unambiguous at first glance without interaction
State change is a continuous outline deformation of the same mark — no instant swap, hard cut or fade between two separate symbols
Press emits a scattered spray of small dots, readable against the surround and varied enough to read as an assortment, originating at the pointer position, not from a fixed anchor
Dots arc, fall, fade and disappear autonomously, leaving the view clean
Particles never intercept, absorb or delay subsequent presses
Pressing the empty backdrop yields the spray alone and leaves the state untouched
Reversal to the previous state is always available and equally effortless
adaptable_details: Which pair of symbols the mark morphs between
Exact backdrop luminance and tone, whether the surround sits lighter or darker than the mark, and the mark's own tone or stroke weight
Dot count, size range, tonal assortment, spread angle and fall behavior details
Duration and easing of both the morph and the flourish
Presence and wording of a small subordinate label
Whether the mark is centered or otherwise placed within its sparse field, and how it scales across viewport sizes
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any sparse, single-focus surface whose meaning reduces to one binary or paired state that a user toggles repeatedly — a minimal single-action page, a hero-scale mode switch, a focal control in a media or utility view. It depends on the state being expressible as two forms of one continuous mark and on the surrounding space staying empty and quiet enough for the mark to own attention. Adding competing content, a dense layout, more than a small handful of states that cannot morph into one another, persistent accumulating particles, or replacing the outline deformation with a symbol swap would produce a different skill.

name: drifting_toggle_switch_playground
description: A wide empty canvas crawling with dozens of small two-state switches that wander slowly like little creatures; the one under the pointer becomes clickable, and a click slides its knob across and crossfades its body fill into the opposite state's value, reversible mid-slide and kept as it drifts on.

canonical_document.name: drifting_toggle_switch_playground
canonical_document.description: A wide empty canvas crawling with dozens of small two-state switches that wander slowly like little creatures; the one under the pointer becomes clickable, and a click slides its knob across and crossfades its body fill into the opposite state's value, reversible mid-slide and kept as it drifts on.
canonical_document.experience_scope: Whole-view region: it fills the entire uncluttered canvas, begins the moment the view opens, and never ends — there is no entry sequence, no goal state and no exit.
content_and_composition: One flat, uniform, low-distraction empty field serving as the entire backdrop, with no headings, instructions, chrome or decorative layers
A few dozen small, identical two-state switch objects as the only foreground content, all of equal visual weight
Each object is composed of an elongated body plus a knob resting at one end of that body; knob position and body fill value together encode the object's current state
State is legible at a glance from the object alone — no labels, tooltips, legends or captions anywhere
Objects are scattered freely across the field with no grid, alignment, grouping or reading order, positioned only by their own wandering

Body fill spans two clearly distinguishable resting values: a quiet, recessive one for one state and a distinctly more emphatic, affirmative one for the other, both holding readable separation from the knob and from the backdrop
No persistent interface elements other than the objects themselves
experience_progression: Continuous, endless ambient drift: all objects keep slowly repositioning themselves, so the field is always milling around and never settles or completes
Per-object micro-progression on demand: an object moves from one resting state through a brief continuous transition into the opposite resting state, then stays there and resumes drifting
attention_and_information_flow: Nothing directs attention; prominence emerges from proximity — attention settles on whichever object happens to wander near the pointer
Hovering an object's body marks it as targetable while the empty backdrop offers no such hint, so the interactive surface is discovered by sweeping across the field
Every object continuously broadcasts its own state, so the whole field reads instantly as a mixture of off and on
A flip briefly pulls the eye through its motion and fill change, then the object drops back to equal weight with the others and keeps roaming

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The hint disappears immediately when the pointer leaves the body, including when the object drifts out from under a stationary pointer
interaction_model.state_change: Object becomes the targeted, actionable element; background remains inert
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Cursor changes to a clickable pointer over the object's body only; empty background keeps the default cursor and gives no affordance
interaction_model.input: Pointer moves over a switch object's body
interaction_model.affected_object: The single object under the pointer

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Fully reversible by clicking the same object again; no confirmation, no undo affordance needed, no effect on neighbours
interaction_model.state_change: That object flips from its current binary state to the opposite one and stays there
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Its knob glides smoothly from one end of the body to the other while the body fill crossfades between the recessive and affirmative resting values; all other objects are untouched and keep drifting
interaction_model.input: Single click while the pointer is over a switch's body
interaction_model.affected_object: Only that one switch object

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Interruption is allowed at any instant and any number of times; the object always ends resting cleanly in one of the two states
interaction_model.state_change: Direction reverses immediately toward the previous state
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Knob turns around from wherever it currently sits and the fill crossfade runs back the other way, with no pause, snap or queued replay
interaction_model.input: Click on the same switch while its flip is still in motion
interaction_model.affected_object: The mid-transition object

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Motion never pauses, is not user-controllable, and objects remain within the visible field rather than wandering out of sight
interaction_model.state_change: All objects continuously and slowly change position, wandering independently
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Slow, creature-like crawling drift across the empty canvas, unaffected by hovering or flipping
interaction_model.input: Autonomous ambient motion (no user input)
interaction_model.affected_object: Every switch object in the field

experience_qualities: Open, airy and uncluttered — almost nothing but empty surround and small objects
Playful and creature-like: the field feels idly alive rather than mechanical
Self-explanatory at a glance, needing no instructions
Tactile and satisfying to flip, with an unmistakable before/after read
Unhurried, low-stakes and pressure-free
Endlessly watchable as background amusement even without interacting
completion_and_return: No completion, finish, score or summary exists; the drift loops indefinitely
Each flipped state persists indefinitely as the object continues to roam, until that object is clicked again
No reset, restore or 'clear all' behavior; the field simply carries on in whatever mixture of states the visitor leaves it
locked_observable_requirements: Near-empty, low-distraction backdrop with the switch objects as the sole foreground content, clearly separated from it
Several dozen equal-weight objects, freely scattered rather than laid out
Slow, continuous autonomous wandering that never stops and is not user-driven
Binary state readable at a glance from knob position plus body fill value, with no labels
Targetable hint (clickable cursor) only over an object's body, never over empty space
A single click affects only the object under the pointer
Flip renders as a smooth knob glide across the body combined with a fill crossfade between two clearly distinguishable resting values
The flip is interruptible and reversible mid-motion, turning around from its current position
New state persists while the object keeps drifting
No goal, score, progress or ending
adaptable_details: Exact object count within the 'few dozen' range
Object size and body/knob proportions
Hues, saturation and overall palette, as long as the two resting states stay clearly distinguishable and one reads calm/recessive against one affirmative
Backdrop value and tint, whether light or dark, provided it stays effectively empty, low-distraction and clearly separated from the objects
Drift speed, path shape and randomness of wandering
Flip transition duration and easing
Whether objects may pass near or over one another
Specific clickable-cursor styling
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits whole-view playful, idle or decorative scenes whose foreground is many small, equal-weight, self-contained binary-state objects that need no explanation, and smaller toy regions built the same way. It becomes a different skill if the objects are placed in a fixed grid, list or layout instead of wandering, if drifting stops, if the states drive real consequences or aggregate outcomes such as scores, progress or unlocking, if the objects carry content such as text, images or data, or if state becomes non-binary or multi-step.

name: dot_matrix_level_plates
description: Upright plates built from a grid of chunky dots; a solidly lit block fills upward from the bottom against dimmer unlit dots above, a picture symbol marks what the plate governs, and dragging on the plate moves the fill in whole dot-row jumps.

canonical_document.name: dot_matrix_level_plates
canonical_document.description: Upright plates built from a grid of chunky dots; a solidly lit block fills upward from the bottom against dimmer unlit dots above, a picture symbol marks what the plate governs, and dragging on the plate moves the fill in whole dot-row jumps.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A compact self-contained region containing a small set of side-by-side plates. Each plate is its own complete experience unit that begins when the pointer or keyboard focus lands on it and ends on release or blur; the region itself is persistent and never takes over the whole view.
content_and_composition: Two or more upright rectangular plates arranged side by side as a peer group, each representing one bounded scalar setting
Each plate is composed of a regular grid of chunky discrete dots in fixed rows and columns, reading as an appliance face rather than a track-and-thumb widget

Within a plate, two visual states of the same dot grid: a solidly lit block occupying the lower rows and clearly dimmer unlit dots occupying the rows above it, with a hard horizontal boundary between them
One pictorial symbol per plate identifying what it governs, placed on or with the plate so identity and amount are seen in the same glance
The unlit dots remain visible at all times as the empty remainder, so the plate always shows both current amount and full range
Persistent elements: plate outline, dot lattice, and symbol never disappear regardless of value
attention_and_information_flow: At rest the pair reads as a single glanceable comparison: symbol answers what, height of the lit block answers roughly how much
The boundary between lit and unlit rows is the primary attention anchor; it is the only thing that moves
During interaction the manipulated plate gains prominence because its fill boundary is in motion while its neighbor stays still
Precision is deliberately coarse: the row quantization communicates an approximate level rather than an exact number, so no numeric readout is required to understand the state
Keyboard focus adds a clear outline that temporarily makes one plate the visually addressed element

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Keeping the pointer down continues into dragging, so an unintended jump can be corrected in the same gesture without releasing

interaction_model.state_change: Value tracks the pointer continuously but resolves only to whole rows

canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any small set of bounded scalar values that benefit from a coarse, glanceable, hardware-feeling readout that is also directly adjustable in place, especially where a symbol can stand in for a label. name: charging_console_panel_choice_row
description: A centered row of slanted panels, each clearly separated in tone from its surround, that read as parts of one machine; picking one charges it edge to edge with thin horizontal bars that fly in from the left in scattered order and overshoot before settling, switching on an outer glow and shifting its label to a distinctly different tone, while any previously picked panel drains back to empty.

canonical_document.name: charging_console_panel_choice_row
canonical_document.description: A centered row of slanted panels, each clearly separated in tone from its surround, that read as parts of one machine; picking one charges it edge to edge with thin horizontal bars that fly in from the left in scattered order and overshoot before settling, switching on an outer glow and shifting its label to a distinctly different tone, while any previously picked panel drains back to empty.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A self-contained region experience: a single horizontal group of sibling choice panels placed inside a larger view. It begins when the row is presented with all panels idle and empty, persists for as long as the view shows the control, and each charge/drain cycle begins on an activation and ends when the fill settles or fully drains.
content_and_composition: One choice row as the unit of composition, centered horizontally on a low-distraction surround of restrained internal contrast.
Three peer choice panels of equal size and identical treatment, evenly spaced and visually related so the row reads as one machine rather than three separate form widgets.
Each panel is a slanted (non-rectangular, sheared) surface set clearly apart in tone from the surround, all sharing the same slant direction so the row feels like a continuous assembly.
One short text label per panel, layered above the panel surface and above the fill, holding readable contrast against both empty and fully charged surface.

A fill layer inside each panel composed of many thin horizontal bars stacked to cover the panel edge to edge when fully charged, separated in tone from the empty surface so fill level is unmistakable.
An outer glow layer around each panel, off in the idle state and on in the charged state, reading as illumination against whatever tone the surround carries.
Exactly one panel may hold the charged state at a time; the charged panel is the only persistent visual emphasis in the row.
experience_progression: Initial state: all panels look equally empty, uniform in tone and available, with no glow and no fill, so none is pre-favored.
Activation: the targeted panel begins charging as thin horizontal bars fly in from its left edge in scattered, non-sequential order.
Overshoot and settle: incoming bars travel slightly past their resting positions and spring back, producing a springy tactile arrival rather than a linear wipe.

Charged hold: the panel is fully filled, its outer glow is on and its label has shifted to its charged tone; a faint restless motion continues in the charged fill so the standing choice keeps signalling.

Reassignment: when a different panel is activated, the newly targeted panel charges while the previously charged one drains back toward empty and loses its glow and label tone shift, keeping exactly one filled.
Interruption: an activation arriving while a charge or drain is still running cuts the running motion off and hands control to the new transition instead of letting bars strand partway.
attention_and_information_flow: At rest the row reads as uniform potential: equal prominence across all panels, no single focal point.
After a pick, prominence collapses onto one panel through combined fill density, outer glow and label tone shift, making the current choice legible from a distance.
The faint continuing energy in the charged fill sustains attention on the standing choice without pulling attention away from surrounding page content.
The draining of the abandoned panel is a secondary, receding signal that confirms the previous choice has been released.
Keyboard attention is surfaced with the same glow treatment, so whichever panel currently holds attention is marked in the row's own visual language rather than by a foreign outline.

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Re-activating the already charged panel leaves the charged state standing; the transition is interruptible at any point by activating another panel
interaction_model.state_change: Idle and empty becomes charged and selected; the row's single-selection slot is claimed
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Thin horizontal bars fly in from the panel's left side in scattered order, overshoot slightly and spring back to fill it edge to edge; the outer glow switches on; the label text shifts to a distinctly different tone; a faint restless energy remains in the fill
interaction_model.input: Pointer activation of an idle panel
interaction_model.affected_object: The activated choice panel: its bar fill, outer glow and label

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Rapid repeated switching cuts off any fill or drain still in progress and restarts from the current visual position, so no panel is left with bars stranded halfway and the row always resolves to one charged and the rest empty
interaction_model.state_change: Selection transfers: the new panel charges while the old one releases, so exactly one panel is ever filled
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The new panel fills with flying, overshooting bars and lights its glow and label while the previous panel's bars drain away and its glow and label tone revert to idle
interaction_model.input: Pointer activation of a different panel while one is already charged
interaction_model.affected_object: Both the newly activated panel and the previously charged panel

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Attention can be moved freely across the row and away from it without committing a change; the standing charged choice remains visible while attention travels
interaction_model.state_change: Attention moves along the row; committing transfers the charged state exactly as a pointer activation does
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The panel holding attention is marked with the same outer glow used for the charged state, so the marking belongs to the machine's own visual language; committing runs the same fill, glow, label tone shift and drain of the prior choice
interaction_model.input: Keyboard reach and move between choices
interaction_model.affected_object: The panel currently holding attention, and on commit the selection itself

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The resting motion is subordinate to transitions and is immediately superseded by any charge or drain
interaction_model.state_change: Charged state persists rather than decaying
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A faint restless energy continues inside the fill so the standing choice never reads as static or stale
interaction_model.input: Charged state resting with no input
interaction_model.affected_object: The bar fill of the charged panel

experience_qualities: Machine-like and instrument-panel: the row reads as parts of one apparatus rather than as ordinary form widgets
Springy and tactile, with overshoot and settle instead of abrupt or purely linear change
Energetic charge metaphor: selection feels like powering something up, abandonment feels like it powering down
Scattered rather than orderly arrival of the fill, giving the charge an alive, slightly chaotic texture
Quietly restless when settled, so the current state keeps signalling without becoming noisy
Responsive under fast repeated input, never leaving a half-finished visual state
completion_and_return: A charge completes as a fully filled, glowing, tone-shifted panel that persists as the standing choice until another is picked.
A drain completes by returning the released panel exactly to the shared idle appearance: empty, unglowing, label back to its idle tone.
The row has no terminal end state; it cycles between charge and drain and always resolves to exactly one charged panel.
Interrupted transitions do not leave residue: any cut-off fill or drain resolves into either the fully charged or fully idle appearance.
locked_observable_requirements: A single centered horizontal row of peer choice panels that read as one machine.
Slanted, non-rectangular panel surfaces clearly separated in tone from a low-distraction surround, all sharing the slant.
A uniform idle state in which every choice looks equally empty and available.
Fill built from many thin horizontal bars that cover the panel edge to edge when charged, distinct enough from the empty surface to read at a glance.
Bars enter from the panel's left side in scattered order, not as an orderly sequential sweep.
Overshoot-and-settle arrival, giving a springy rather than abrupt change.
Charged state combines three simultaneous signals: full bar fill, outer glow on, label shifted to a clearly different tone; the shift must be perceptible in whatever palette is used.
A faint continuing restlessness in the charged fill while it stands.
Strict single-charge invariant: exactly one panel filled at any settled moment, with the abandoned one draining back to idle.
Running fills and drains are cut off by a newer pick rather than left stranded partway.
Choices are reachable and switchable without a pointer, with the attention-holding choice marked by the same glow.
adaptable_details: Exact number of choices in the row, as long as it stays a small comparable set.
Slant angle and direction, panel proportions and spacing.

Any palette and overall luminance range, light or dark: the specific surface tone, glow hue and the label's charged hue are free as long as panel-to-surround separation, label readability and a perceptible charged-versus-idle shift hold.
Bar thickness, bar count, gaps between bars and the degree of scatter.
Charge and drain durations, overshoot amount and springiness intensity.
Character of the resting restlessness, such as subtle flicker, drift or pulse.
Label wording and typography.
Whether one choice starts charged or the row starts entirely idle.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits small sets of short-labeled, mutually exclusive choices presented inline as a compact control region: mode and view switches, tier or plan pickers, difficulty or intensity selectors, filter toggles and settings choices, wherever the current selection must be unmistakable and the surrounding surface can carry a machine-like treatment against a low-distraction surround, in any palette or luminance range. It stays the same Skill across differing choice counts, palettes, light or dark host surfaces and motion tuning. It becomes a different Skill if multiple choices can be charged simultaneously, if the charge stops being a directional bar fill of the choice surface itself, if choices grow into rich content cards or long option lists needing scrolling, or if the row is repurposed as a passive progress or status readout rather than something the user picks.

canonical_document.name: spotlight_take_with_picture_trail_to_counter
canonical_document.description: Taking an item pushes every other item back small and nearly faded while the chosen one swells and a trailing stream of its own pictures sweeps out and vanishes into a header counter that pops into existence on the first take and ticks up after; the counter opens a review panel with live totals that closes back to the set exactly as left.
canonical_document.experience_scope: Whole-view experience over a compact item set plus a persistent header indicator and an overlay review mode; the resting state begins on arrival, each take event begins at the press of an item's add control and ends when the set settles back to even weight, and the review mode begins on counter activation and ends on close.
content_and_composition: One compact set of several item cards of visually equal weight at rest, none privileged, each carrying its own picture and its own add control
One persistent header region containing a single accumulator counter that does not exist in the view before the first take
Transient trail of multiple copies of the chosen item's own picture occupying the space between that card and the header counter during a take
One overlay review panel layered above the set, listing one line per collected item with picture, name, price and quantity, a running total, and a close control
The item set remains present and unaltered beneath the review panel
experience_progression: Rest: quiet, even-handed set where every item plainly reads as takeable and no counter is present
Take begins: all non-chosen items recede, become smaller and nearly faded out; the chosen item swells and briefly owns attention alone
Trail: a stream of the chosen item's own pictures sweeps out of it, converges on the header counter and disappears into it

Return: closing dismisses the panel and restores the set exactly as it was left

experience_qualities: Quiet, even-handed arrival where takeability is immediately obvious without any item competing
Each take reads as an event rather than a silent state change
Momentary, self-resolving singling out that hands attention back to the whole set

The accumulator feels like it holds goods and keeps a live running count rather than sitting as decoration

completion_and_return: Each take completes on its own, ending with the set restored to its even-weight rest state
The counter persists after completion, carrying the accumulated count across further browsing

Closing review returns the set exactly as it was left rather than to a fresh state

locked_observable_requirements: At rest, all items in the set carry visually equal weight and each plainly reads as takeable
A take suppresses the other items by pushing them back, smaller and nearly faded out, while the chosen item swells
The travelling trail is made of multiple copies of the chosen item's own picture, not a generic token
The trail sweeps out of the chosen item, converges on the header counter and vanishes into it
The counter does not exist before the first take, pops into existence on that take, and ticks up on each later take

adaptable_details: Number of items and grid columns in the set
Card styling, spacing and how the add control is presented on each card

Number of pictures in the trail and the curvature of its path
Placement of the counter within the header and its numeric styling
Which side the review panel enters from and its width or height
Price and total formatting, and the wording of quantity, remove and close controls
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any compact, evenly weighted set of picture-bearing entries that are gathered into a small persistent indicator and later reviewed as a list with a running amount, such as catalogs, galleries, media libraries, saved-items or wishlist views. Removing per-item pictures (so nothing recognizable can fly), removing the persistent counting indicator, keeping the surrounding items unchanged during a take, or making the gathered-items list the primary destination view instead of a dismissible step aside would each create a different Skill.

canonical_document.name: elastic_search_bar_with_extruded_result_rows
canonical_document.description: A lone soft control stretches wide into a typing field, pinches off a small round companion that shows a spinner during matching, then releases short result rows that peel out from behind the bar and are sucked back in when the field empties.
canonical_document.experience_scope: Region experience anchored on one control area within an otherwise empty view; it begins at the quiet resting state showing only the single control, spans the control, its round companion and the emerging result stack, and ends when the query is emptied and the region has settled back to that same resting state.
content_and_composition: One resting control carrying a short label, alone in a deliberately empty surrounding area with no helper or instructional text
One text-entry field that replaces the label in place inside the widened control
Exactly one small round companion shape positioned beside the control, briefly joined to it by a thinning bridge of the same material
One vertical stack of a small number of evenly spaced result rows, each holding one short scannable entry
Rows read as the same soft elastic mass as the bar, emerging from behind it, with no separate panel frame, border or container chrome
The control itself persists across every stage and remains the visual origin of both the companion and the rows
experience_progression: Rest: a single quiet control holds the whole view, making the one available action obvious without instruction
Activation: the control stretches wider, its label is replaced by a ready-to-type field, and a round companion is pushed out beside it, clinging by a thinning bridge before snapping free
Composing: attention belongs entirely to the query text while the surroundings stay quiet
Honest pause: shortly after typing stops, the companion carries a spinner indicating matching is under way
Emergence: matching entries peel out from behind the bar one after another into an evenly spaced stack
Scanning: rows sit as a short readable list, individually responsive to pointing
Retraction: emptying the field pulls the rows back up into the bar until they vanish and the region settles into the quiet resting state
attention_and_information_flow: At rest all prominence sits on the single control because nothing else occupies the view
During activation prominence shifts inward to the newly opened field, with the companion reading as a secondary satellite
While matching, the only changing information is the spinner on the companion, so the wait is acknowledged without pulling focus from the typed text
As rows appear, prominence spreads downward through the stack in the order of emergence, letting the list be read as a short scannable set
Pointing raises one row above its neighbors momentarily without displacing overall focus
Clearing the query withdraws all revealed information and returns prominence to the lone control

interaction_model.visible_feedback: The control stretches wider, the label is replaced by a ready-to-type field, and a small round companion is pushed out beside it, clinging by a thinning bridge before snapping free

interaction_model.affected_object: The control, its label and the newly created round companion shape

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Resumed typing restarts the pause; fast edits discard superseded queries so only results for the latest text are ever shown

interaction_model.visible_feedback: Matching entries peel out from behind the bar one after another into evenly spaced rows sharing the bar's soft material

interaction_model.visible_feedback: The row swells slightly

experience_qualities: Playful and soft, with a gooey elastic material that stretches, clings and snaps
Quiet and restrained at rest, so a single action reads as obvious
Continuous, as if results are extruded from the same mass as the control rather than opening as a separate surface
Honest about waiting, acknowledging matching briefly rather than hiding it
Scannable and calm once results are present, with light responsiveness per row
completion_and_return: An empty query is the defined return condition: rows retract into the bar and the region rests exactly as it began
No end-state panel or leftover container persists after retraction
The experience can be re-entered any number of times from the resting control
Only the latest query's results persist; superseded query outcomes never surface
locked_observable_requirements: At rest the region shows one inviting control and nothing else, with no instructional text
Activation visibly widens the control and replaces its label with a typing field in the same place
Exactly one small round companion is extruded beside the control, connected by a thinning bridge that snaps free
A spinner appears on the companion shortly after typing stops, before results appear
Result rows emerge sequentially from behind the bar into an evenly spaced stack
Rows share the bar's soft elastic material and never read as a separate detached panel
Pointing at a row makes it swell slightly
Emptying the field pulls rows back up into the bar until they vanish and the quiet rest state returns
Only results for the most recent query text are ever visible
adaptable_details: Wording of the resting label and placeholder
The kind of short entries listed and their internal text layout
Maximum number of rows shown and stack direction
Exact durations of the pause, peel-out sequence and retraction
Size, side and offset of the round companion

Color treatment of control, rows and surround including hue, theme polarity and surface tone, plus softness amount, easing and spinner styling, as long as the control and rows read as one material against a low-distraction surround and the entry text stays comfortably readable
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits a single query control that filters a small set of short entries in a spacious, otherwise empty region where the control can be the sole focus. Dense or paginated result tables, multi-field or faceted filtering, results that must stay permanently visible in their own panel, or a control embedded in a crowded toolbar would break the extruded-from-one-mass reading and constitute a different Skill.
