canonical_document.experience_scope: Whole-view experience split into two fixed zones: a dominant continuously animating character-pattern stage and a subordinate control column beside it. It begins already animating at page open with no start action and has no end state; it runs until the visitor chooses to stop refining and leave.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any page region where a single self-contained continuously animating abstract visual is the subject and the visitor tunes it live: generative art toys, pattern or texture makers, look-and-feel customizers, and large decorative canvases that deliberately expose their controls. It needs a visual whose parameters are continuous, so intermediate values on a drag remain meaningful. It becomes a different skill if the tool yields discrete saved outputs or a gallery of results, if changes require an explicit generate or apply step, if the visual becomes static or only animates on hover, if the controls grow into the dominant surface, or if the artwork recedes into a passive backdrop behind unrelated foreground content with no exposed controls.
content_and_composition: One primary visual object: a single large pattern field drawn entirely from text characters, occupying most of the view at all times.
One secondary control area at a side of the view, visually quieter than the artwork, with grouped and labeled options so each option's effect is guessable before it is touched.

Continuous sliders for the numeric properties: two pattern frequencies, two drifting-center speeds, pattern density, and character size; the character-size control carries a live numeric multiplier readout.
A small set of numbered options (three in the source case) selecting the pattern's underlying geometry, mutually exclusive, with the active one persistently marked.
One toggle selecting an alternate softer blend of the characters.
One free text field holding an ordered run of characters used as the drawing alphabet, read from lightest to heaviest.

Two visual layers: a flat single-tone backdrop plane behind an ink glyph layer whose tone follows the ink-polarity choice.
Persistent elements: the artwork never blanks, empties or restarts; the control column stays visible throughout; the active geometry marker and the size multiplier readout remain on screen.
attention_and_information_flow: Prominence is fixed rather than shifting: the pattern field always holds primary attention and the controls stay deliberately quiet and never expand over the view.
Information is revealed ahead of action through labels and grouping, so an option's likely effect is predictable before it is used.

While a control is being dragged, attention couples to the artwork because the change appears there on the next frame; the multiplier readout and the marked geometry option are the only textual confirmations.
No overlays, loading states, result lists or comparison views ever interrupt the single living image.

interaction_model.state_change: Active run resolves as a failed attempt
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The wipeout plays out comically and harmlessly rather than as a punishing outcome
interaction_model.input: Vehicle wrecking against the course
interaction_model.affected_object: Vehicle and the current attempt

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The finished course can be reopened and replayed, and the next course can be opened to move on; completion marks are still present when the visitor returns later
interaction_model.state_change: Run resolves as a success and the course becomes marked as finished
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Arrival is emphasized as earned, and the course's completion mark appears in the list
interaction_model.input: Vehicle reaching the finish
interaction_model.affected_object: Current attempt and the course list entry

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The list stays reachable so another course can be chosen at any time
interaction_model.state_change: Play surface swaps to the chosen course at its starting arrangement
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The new course is presented fully readable at a glance, ready to drive
interaction_model.input: Selecting a course from the list
interaction_model.affected_object: Play surface contents

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Nothing is lost or reset by leaving; the attempt is neither failed nor restarted
interaction_model.state_change: Run pauses, then resumes from the identical state
interaction_model.visible_feedback: All motion freezes in place and continues from the same position on return
interaction_model.input: Attention leaving the window and returning
interaction_model.affected_object: Live run

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The run continues undisturbed through the refit
interaction_model.state_change: Course refits to the new dimensions
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The whole course remains legible in one view at the new size
interaction_model.input: Resizing the view
interaction_model.affected_object: Framing of the play surface

experience_qualities: Instantly legible — the challenge explains itself spatially
Short attempts with a strong one-more-try pull
Low-stakes and comic on failure rather than punishing
Satisfying, earned arrival on success
Effortless control: one held input, one clear response
completion_and_return: Each attempt completes at a wreck or at the finish
Restart fully resets the course to its exact original state; retries are unlimited and immediate
Finished courses stay marked, so accumulated progress is still visible on a later return
Pausing on focus loss preserves the in-progress attempt rather than ending it
locked_observable_requirements: A single sustained hold drives; release stops the drive immediately
The hold continues while the pointer is outside the play surface and ends only on release
Start, obstacles and finish are all readable at a glance with no explanation
Failure is presented comically rather than punitively
Restart returns every part of the course to exactly its starting arrangement
Retries are immediate and unlimited
Completion marks on finished courses persist across returns
adaptable_details: Vehicle appearance and the nature of the moving protagonist
Obstacle shapes, difficulty and course count
Overall art style, palette and framing of the course
Layout and styling of the course list and its completion marks
Exact form of the comic wipeout and the arrival emphasis
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits compact, self-contained challenge or toy regions embedded in a page where a whole attempt is visible at once and can be repeated in seconds. It becomes a different skill if control expands to a multi-input scheme, if the course cannot be read in a single view, or if progression becomes a long continuous session instead of short discrete retryable attempts.

name: hovering_self_regathering_object_clump
description: A whole collection of flat and figural items hangs clumped as one hovering mass in an open hazy space with a low-contrast surround; pointer sweeps shove pieces aside, a press claims the frontmost piece so it trails behind the pointer with springy lag and knocks into others, and letting go lets it tumble away until the clump pulls it back in.

canonical_document.name: hovering_self_regathering_object_clump
canonical_document.description: A whole collection of flat and figural items hangs clumped as one hovering mass in an open hazy space with a low-contrast surround; pointer sweeps shove pieces aside, a press claims the frontmost piece so it trails behind the pointer with springy lag and knocks into others, and letting go lets it tumble away until the clump pulls it back in.
canonical_document.experience_scope: Whole-view stage experience: begins after a plain hold-until-ready entry that reveals the scene with the mass already formed at centre, occupies the full visible scene, and never ends — the mass continuously re-gathers so there is no completion or exit state.
content_and_composition: One central mass composed of many discrete collectible objects (mixed shapes such as flat covers, flat sleeves and standing figures), packed close enough to overlap and occlude one another
Objects readable individually at close attention: each carries its own imagery/identity, so the set communicates variety as well as volume
Open, airy environment as persistent backdrop: hazy low-contrast distance, sense of ground below and overhead space above
Invisible containment shell — floor, ceiling and unseen side walls — bounding the play volume just outside the visible frame
No instructional text, controls, labels or panels; the mass is the only foreground subject
Centre of the view is the persistent gravitational anchor the mass reoccupies
experience_progression: Entry: plain unstyled holding state while the scene assembles, so nothing partial is ever shown
Reveal: full scene appears with the collection already clumped into a single hovering body at centre
First read: the mass registers as one object with weight and silhouette
Second read: attention narrows inward and individual members become recognisable within the packing
Open-ended play: disturbance and re-gathering alternate indefinitely; no stage completes or locks out another
attention_and_information_flow: Prominence starts on the whole mass as a silhouette, then transfers inward to individual objects as the viewer's focus narrows
Any object the pointer touches gains momentary prominence by moving while its neighbours stay comparatively still
A grabbed object becomes the clear focal subject: it separates from the packing, trails the pointer and is fully visible rather than occluded
Released objects hand prominence back to the mass as they tumble in and re-merge
The environment stays low-contrast and hazy so it never competes with the objects

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Fully self-recovering — stopping the sweep lets everything drift home; repeated sweeps simply re-disturb without accumulating damage
interaction_model.state_change: Nearby pieces are shoved outward from rest, then left unheld
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A parting wake opens through the packing; displaced pieces drift back on their own and re-close the gap
interaction_model.input: Pointer or finger swept through the mass without pressing
interaction_model.affected_object: Objects near the moving pointer path

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Selection is exclusive to one piece; pressing elsewhere claims a different frontmost piece
interaction_model.state_change: That single object becomes held; all others remain free
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The chosen piece detaches from the packing and reads as picked up, with no ambiguity about which one was claimed
interaction_model.input: Press down on a spot where several objects overlap
interaction_model.affected_object: Only the frontmost object under the pointer

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Movement can be interrupted or reversed at any time; the trailing piece catches up and settles behind the pointer
interaction_model.state_change: Held object follows the pointer with lag; contacted objects are knocked out of place
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The piece trails behind the cursor on a springy delay rather than snapping to it, and visibly shoves and scatters pieces along its route
interaction_model.input: Move the pointer while holding
interaction_model.affected_object: The held object and everything it passes

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Nothing is lost or removed; it can be re-grabbed mid-flight or after it rejoins
interaction_model.state_change: Object returns to its own momentum and is re-absorbed by the mass
interaction_model.visible_feedback: It flies off along its last motion, tumbling as it goes, then slows and drifts back into the clump
interaction_model.input: Release the hold
interaction_model.affected_object: The previously held object

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Hard boundary on all sides plus floor and ceiling; no state can strand a piece off-view
interaction_model.state_change: Object meets an unseen boundary of the play volume
interaction_model.visible_feedback: It is turned back into view instead of disappearing, keeping the whole collection always on screen
interaction_model.input: Any motion that would carry an object out of the visible scene
interaction_model.affected_object: The escaping object

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Re-gathering is always available as the resting state and can be interrupted by new input at any moment
interaction_model.state_change: Disturbed objects converge back toward the centre
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The clump slowly reforms into a single hovering body
interaction_model.input: Idle time with no input
interaction_model.affected_object: The whole collection

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Same boundaries and self-recovery apply
interaction_model.state_change: Identical state transitions to pointer interaction
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Identical visible responses on touch devices
interaction_model.input: Touch input equivalent of sweep, press, drag and release
interaction_model.affected_object: Same objects as pointer input

experience_qualities: Weightless and floaty rather than heavy or fast
Tactile — objects feel like solid things that collide, shove and tumble
Springy and trailing rather than instantly snapping
Unhurried, with slow settling and drifting
Self-explanatory without any instructions
Forgiving and lossless — nothing can be broken, removed or thrown away
Open-ended and idly watchable even without interaction
completion_and_return: No completion, score, end state or exit; the experience is perpetual
The clump re-gathering at centre is the implicit reset — every disturbance resolves back to it without user action
No persistent state carried between visits; each arrival begins from the fully formed mass
The whole set is always present and countable on screen at any moment
locked_observable_requirements: The collection appears already clumped into one hovering mass at the centre of an open hazy low-contrast environment
Nothing partial is shown before the scene is ready; the reveal is of a complete formed mass
The mass reads first as a single body and only then as individual recognisable members
Objects overlap and occlude each other densely enough that frontmost-only selection is meaningful
Pointer sweeping shoves nearby pieces aside and they drift back unaided
Pressing claims exactly one piece — the frontmost under the pointer
A held piece trails the pointer with springy lag and collides with what it passes instead of teleporting
Release returns the piece to its own momentum so it tumbles free and is re-absorbed
Invisible floor, ceiling and side boundaries keep every piece inside the view
Objects are never destroyed, consumed or permanently removed
Pointer and touch produce the same behaviours
adaptable_details: What the collected objects depict and their mix of flat and figural shapes
Object count and how tightly the mass is packed
Environment styling: surround luminance level and hue family, haze density, overall lighting feel, ground and overhead treatment
Scale of individual objects relative to the view
How springy the trailing lag feels and how quickly pieces re-gather
Whether the mass idles with slight ambient drift or hangs almost still
Framing and camera distance from the mass
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any moderately dense set of discrete, visually distinct items meant to be freely handled and admired without a task — collections, catalogues, product families, playful brand objects. It stops being this Skill if objects are consumed, sorted into slots, scored, permanently removed, or if selection triggers navigation or detail views; if the mass stops re-gathering into one central body; if held objects snap rigidly to the pointer without lag or pass through neighbours without collision; or if the items become a background substrate behind foreground text and copy rather than the stage subject.

name: hand_pointer_block_sandbox
description: After a full-screen access invitation, a calm low-distraction space with a visible ground plane appears; a mirrored self-view stays tucked at one edge while a small sphere pointer follows the visitor's hand in three dimensions, fading blocks it touches, carrying one when the hand closes into a fist and setting it down solid when the hand opens.

canonical_document.name: hand_pointer_block_sandbox
canonical_document.description: After a full-screen access invitation, a calm low-distraction space with a visible ground plane appears; a mirrored self-view stays tucked at one edge while a small sphere pointer follows the visitor's hand in three dimensions, fading blocks it touches, carrying one when the hand closes into a fist and setting it down solid when the hand opens.
canonical_document.experience_scope: Begins with a full-screen access invitation covering the whole view; after permission it becomes the entire play view — a persistent 3D space with edge-anchored self-view — and never ends, since there is no completion state and the arrangement persists.
content_and_composition: One full-screen opening invitation panel that unmistakably requests camera access and blocks the experience until granted
One calm, low-distraction 3D space with a clear ground reference plane underneath, its surround held clearly separated in luminance from the objects so depth stays judgeable
A small set of a few simple blocks resting on the ground, freely repositionable
One small sphere pointer floating in the space as the visitor's hand proxy, distinct enough from the blocks and surround to be found instantly
One small mirrored live self-view preview persistently tucked at a single edge of the view, small enough not to compete with the play space
Depth cues from the ground plane and object shading keep near-far relationships readable
experience_progression: Full-screen invitation awaits permission
Space, ground, blocks, self-view and pointer become live together
Visitor understands the pointer mirrors their hand within seconds of moving
Open-ended play: contact, hold, carry, release repeats indefinitely with the arrangement carried forward
attention_and_information_flow: Attention starts fully on the access invitation because nothing else is visible or active
After granting, attention moves to the pointer as the only moving element, then outward to the reachable blocks
Contact fading briefly makes the touched pair the most informative thing on screen, signalling what can be grabbed
A held block becomes the focal object as it trails the pointer, while released blocks recede into the calm arrangement
The self-view stays peripheral, consulted only to correct framing, and never draws attention from the play space

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Nothing in the space is shown or active before permission; the invitation remains the entire view until access is granted
interaction_model.state_change: Pre-access blocked state transitions to live tracked play state
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Invitation gives way to the evenly illuminated space with ground, blocks, edge self-view and a pointer that begins responding to hand movement
interaction_model.input: Visitor grants camera access from the opening full-screen invitation
interaction_model.affected_object: Whole view: invitation panel, space, blocks, pointer, self-view

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Depth bounds hold the pointer inside the reachable volume rather than letting it escape the scene
interaction_model.state_change: Pointer position updates continuously in all three axes, clamped within a bounded reachable depth range
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Pointer glides through the space mirroring the hand; at the near and far limits it stops advancing so nothing is pushed beyond reach
interaction_model.input: Tracked hand moves side to side, up and down, and nearer or farther from the camera
interaction_model.affected_object: Sphere pointer

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Moving the pointer away restores both to full solidity with no lasting change
interaction_model.state_change: Neutral state becomes contact state
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Both the pointer and the block fade slightly toward transparency, confirming which block is in reach
interaction_model.input: Pointer overlaps a block
interaction_model.affected_object: Pointer and that block

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Letting go is always possible mid-move; no other block can be picked up while one is held
interaction_model.state_change: Contact becomes held; exactly one block can be held at a time
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The block detaches from rest and trails the pointer smoothly through the space while remaining slightly faded
interaction_model.input: Hand closes into a fist while in contact
interaction_model.affected_object: The contacted block

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The new position simply persists; the visitor may immediately grab it again or another block
interaction_model.state_change: Held becomes at rest in its new position
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The block settles in place and returns to full solidity
interaction_model.input: Hand opens
interaction_model.affected_object: The held block

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Motion resumes from the frozen position once tracking picks the hand up again; the self-view helps the visitor return to frame
interaction_model.state_change: Live tracking becomes frozen state
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Pointer and the block it holds stop in place and stay put, unchanged
interaction_model.input: Hand leaves the camera's view
interaction_model.affected_object: Pointer and any held block

experience_qualities: Calm, low-distraction and uncluttered rather than energetic or dramatic
Legible depth thanks to a constant ground reference
Immediately understandable within seconds of moving a hand
Trustworthy, because the small self-view shows the visitor they are seen and in frame
Forgiving: contact and hold are always reversible and lost tracking freezes rather than scatters
Toy-like and open-ended with no score, goal or pressure
completion_and_return: No finish line and no reset; play continues indefinitely
Whatever arrangement the visitor leaves behind persists as the new resting state
Interrupted tracking resumes from where it froze rather than restarting the experience
locked_observable_requirements: A full-screen, unmistakable access invitation precedes any part of the experience becoming visible or active
A small mirrored self-view stays persistently at one edge while the experience runs
A small sphere pointer mirrors hand position in all three axes, with reachable depth bounded so nothing goes out of reach
Overlap between pointer and a block fades both slightly toward transparency to confirm contact
Closing the hand takes hold, the block trails the pointer smoothly, opening the hand sets it down at rest restored to full solidity
Only one block is held at a time and release is possible at any moment mid-move
Loss of tracking freezes the pointer and held block in place until tracking resumes
A calm, low-distraction surround with a clear ground reference beneath the blocks, the blocks separated from ground and surround enough to read as solid objects
Object arrangement persists with no completion state or reset
adaptable_details: Exact number of blocks, as long as it stays a small set
Block shape, size, hue, luminance level and material, in any scheme that stays calm and keeps blocks readable against ground and surround
Which edge holds the self-view and its exact size
Pointer size and accent treatment, and the exact amount of fade on contact
Ground treatment: plain plane, subtle grid or soft shadow
Wording and styling of the access invitation
Camera framing and field of view of the space
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any small, low-density set of loose foreground objects in an open space that visitors are meant to rearrange freely by hand movement, as a standalone playful section or full-view demo. Requires live camera hand tracking, a bounded reachable volume and a visible ground reference. It becomes a different Skill if pointing is replaced by cursor, touch or scroll input, if objects gain goals, scoring, snapping targets or ordered tasks, if many objects or dense information must be manipulated at once, if multiple simultaneous holds are allowed, or if the space becomes a background substrate behind foreground content instead of the experience itself.

name: overhead_unlit_shaft_descent_run
description: Seen from directly overhead, a ball falls continuously down a long narrow shaft where only the wall beside it is lit and everything further falls off into unreadable depth; the player leans it sideways with held arrow keys to thread between high-salience accent ledges that surface out of the gloom, while a small readout tracks level, seconds and knock-backs until a quiet tally offers a more crowded round.

canonical_document.name: overhead_unlit_shaft_descent_run
canonical_document.description: Seen from directly overhead, a ball falls continuously down a long narrow shaft where only the wall beside it is lit and everything further falls off into unreadable depth; the player leans it sideways with held arrow keys to thread between high-salience accent ledges that surface out of the gloom, while a small readout tracks level, seconds and knock-backs until a quiet tally offers a more crowded round.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A whole-view experience that starts playing immediately on open with no menu or title step, occupies the full frame as the play space with a small persistent overlay readout, and ends at a closing tally that can restart the same view with a fresh ball.
content_and_composition: One controllable falling object as the single focal element, held near the centre of the frame as the view follows its descent
Two long side walls forming a narrow vertical shaft, viewed from directly overhead so descent reads as travel into the frame
A lit band of wall immediately around the object; wall and shaft beyond it fall away through a steep luminance transition into unreadable depth, so visible range is deliberately short

Repeating ledges carrying the only high-salience accent treatment on screen, projecting into the shaft at varying positions and emerging from the unreadable depth ahead rather than being visible in advance
One small permanent readout, always on screen during play, carrying exactly three live values: current level, elapsed seconds, and how many times the object has been knocked back
A quiet closing tally panel at run end restating the run's figures, with one obvious affordance leading into a more crowded round
experience_progression: Play begins autonomously at view open with the object already descending
Continuous descent with hazards surfacing out of the unreadable depth at a short, roughly constant sighting distance
Player-steered threading between hazards; contact events accumulate into the knock-back figure without ending the run
Run closes and motion settles into a quiet tally of the same figures shown live
Confirming returns a fresh object to the start of the shaft for a denser round, looping the whole cycle
attention_and_information_flow: Attention is pinned to the small lit region around the object because nothing beyond it is legible
The hazards carry the only high-salience accent on screen, clearly separated from wall, object and readout, so newly emerging ledges pull the eye the instant they appear
Reading order during play is hazard-first, object-second, readout only glanced at; the readout never competes with the play space
Lateral drift is made readable by the view trailing slightly behind the sideways move rather than locking the object dead centre
At run end attention transfers from the play space to the tally, which becomes the only thing asking for a decision

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Descent is never suspended by steering or contact; it is interrupted only by run end
interaction_model.state_change: Run is live from the first frame with no start gesture
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Wall detail streams past the object while the depth ahead stays unlit and unreadable; elapsed-seconds value climbs
interaction_model.input: Autonomous driver: continuous descent of the object once the view opens
interaction_model.affected_object: Object position along the shaft and the surrounding lit wall band

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Releasing lets the sideways motion bleed away on its own; pressing the opposite direction re-aims the drift without stopping the descent
interaction_model.state_change: Lateral drift builds up gradually while the key is held instead of snapping to a new position
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Object eases toward that side with visible momentum; the overhead view follows the lateral move with a slight lag so the offset is felt
interaction_model.input: Holding a left or right directional key
interaction_model.affected_object: Object's sideways motion and the trailing view

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Hard boundary: the object can never leave the shaft, so mis-steering is always recoverable and never fatal
interaction_model.state_change: Outward motion is converted into a slower inward push
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Object is nudged back toward the middle of the shaft at reduced speed rather than stopping or passing through
interaction_model.input: Object brushing a side wall of the shaft
interaction_model.affected_object: Object's lateral motion at the play-space boundary

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The run continues after the setback; steering stays available throughout the kick and descent resumes on its own
interaction_model.state_change: Descent progress is set back and the knock-back count increments by one
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Object is kicked upward against its fall and the knock-back value in the readout ticks up
interaction_model.input: Object clipping an accent hazard ledge
interaction_model.affected_object: Object's vertical progress and the knock-back figure in the readout

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The tally persists until confirmed, so the figures can be read at leisure before committing to another run
interaction_model.state_change: Run ends and a new, more crowded run replaces it
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Tally clears and a fresh object appears at the start of the shaft, immediately descending again
interaction_model.input: Confirming from the closing tally
interaction_model.affected_object: Whole play space

experience_qualities: Immediate: playable in the first second, with no menu, title or explanation
Claustrophobic and low-key, with a depth that falls off out of legibility and hides what is coming
Weighty steering that feels like leaning rather than teleporting, thanks to drift build-up and bleed-off
Forgiving at the edges but punishing on hazards, so failure is a setback rather than an ending
Measurable: three plain live figures make a run comparable without any framing text
Quiet at the close, so the tally reads as a pause rather than a celebration
completion_and_return: Each run terminates in a quiet tally restating level, elapsed time and knock-backs
One confirm action restarts the same view with a fresh object and a more crowded hazard field
The cycle loops indefinitely through progressively denser rounds
Live figures reset with each new run; the difficulty step carries forward
locked_observable_requirements: Play starts by itself when the view opens, with no menu or start step
Camera looks directly down the shaft so descent reads as motion into the frame
Visibility is short: only the wall immediately around the object is legibly lit, everything beyond falling off through a luminance transition into unreadable depth
Hazards must emerge from that unreadable depth rather than being previewed
Hazards carry a single high-salience accent treatment, clearly separated from every other element on screen
Sideways control builds and bleeds momentum; no instant snap to a lateral position
The view trails lateral movement slightly rather than locking to the object horizontally
Side walls are an inescapable boundary that returns the object inward at reduced speed
Hazard contact pushes the object back against its descent and increments a visible counter without ending the run
A small readout of exactly three live values stays visible for the whole run
Run end is a quiet tally with one obvious route into a denser round
adaptable_details: Exact hazard shape, width and spacing pattern
Descent speed, drift build-up and bleed-off rates, and camera lag amount
Shaft width, wall surface treatment and how quickly legibility falls off into unreadable depth
Exact hues and overall tonal register of the unreadable depth and of the hazard accent, as long as their separation and salience hold
Placement, typography and framing of the readout and tally
How much denser each subsequent round becomes
Whether additional directional inputs beyond arrow keys are accepted
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any short hands-on diversion built on continuous forward travel through a confined space with hazards revealed late, where the payoff is a small comparable score. Replacing the short-sighted falloff with a fully visible course, letting the object exit the shaft or be destroyed on contact, making hazard contact end the run instead of setting it back, snapping the object sideways instead of drifting, or gating play behind a menu each produce a different skill; adding a narrative frame or turning it into a non-interactive descent animation removes it from this category entirely.

name: turn_taking_lob_duel_playfield
description: Two opposing characters trade arcing lobs across a deformable skyline; you drag the resting projectile, which sits at the highest salience in the near character's hand, against a dotted guide with live angle and power readouts, release into a wind-bent spinning flight, and see it miss, crater a structure, or win the match.

canonical_document.name: turn_taking_lob_duel_playfield
canonical_document.description: Two opposing characters trade arcing lobs across a deformable skyline; you drag the resting projectile, which sits at the highest salience in the near character's hand, against a dotted guide with live angle and power readouts, release into a wind-bent spinning flight, and see it miss, crater a structure, or win the match.
canonical_document.experience_scope: Begins when the playfield presents a skyline with two opposing characters and a resting projectile carrying the strongest emphasis in the near character's hand; runs through alternating aim-release-resolve turns; ends at a win announcement that invites a fresh skyline. Works as a bounded region or as a whole-view scene, but is always self-contained within its frame.
content_and_composition: Two opposing characters placed at opposite ends of a horizontally spanning ground line
A row of destructible structures forming the skyline between and beneath them, acting as both scenery and damageable surface
Exactly one resting projectile at a time, visibly held by the side whose turn it is and separated from the scenery behind it, presented as the pressable interaction target
A drifting air-condition indicator floating above the skyline, showing direction and strength of the force that will bend flight

An ephemeral aiming layer over the scene, readable against whatever lies beneath it: a dotted arc leaving the projectile, the thrower's arm as a live pointing element, and numeric angle and power readouts
Persistent craters and punched holes accumulating on structure surfaces across rounds, reading as clear breaks in the intact surface
A tracking marker riding the top edge of the frame while the projectile is above the visible area
A win announcement resolving the match
experience_progression: Ready: the active side's projectile rests in hand and reads as pressable; the air indicator drifts overhead
Aiming: press and drag continuously shapes direction and strength while the guide, arm and readouts follow the pointer
Flight: release commits the shot, which spins along a curved path bent by the drifting force and gravity
Resolution: the shot leaves the field short or long, punches a crater into a structure, or strikes the opponent
Hand-off: a miss passes the turn to the opposing side, which visibly aims and fires on its own before control returns
Escalation: rounds repeat over a skyline carrying all previous damage, so the field reads as more battered each round
Close: a hit ends the match with a win announcement, then a fresh undamaged skyline is offered
attention_and_information_flow: At turn start, prominence sits on the resting projectile in the active character's hand and secondarily on the drifting overhead indicator, so the visitor knows both that the shot is theirs and what will push it off course
During drag, attention moves onto the dotted arc and the changing angle and power numbers, which reveal the committed shot before it is committed
On release the aiming layer disappears and attention rides the spinning projectile; if it exits the top of the frame, the top-edge marker carries that attention instead
On impact, focus snaps to the new crater or to the struck opponent, making the outcome unambiguous
Between turns, the emphasised projectile moves to the other side, relocating attention across the field
Across rounds, accumulated craters become a persistent secondary readout of how the match has gone

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Aim can be re-adjusted freely and indefinitely while the pointer is held; nothing is committed until release, so a bad aim is recoverable without penalty
interaction_model.state_change: Idle ready state becomes a continuously updating aiming state where direction and strength are both bound to pointer position
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A dotted arc extends from the projectile, the arm rotates to point along it, and live angle and power values update legibly with every pointer move
interaction_model.input: Press and drag on the resting projectile
interaction_model.affected_object: Aiming layer: dotted guide, thrower's arm, angle and power readouts

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Flight is not steerable or cancellable; it always resolves into one of three outcomes, so the visitor is never left in an indefinite state
interaction_model.state_change: Aiming state ends and the projectile enters free flight; the aiming layer is removed
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The projectile spins as it travels a curved path visibly bent by the overhead drifting force and by gravity
interaction_model.input: Release
interaction_model.affected_object: The projectile

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The marker disappears when the projectile re-enters the frame; if the shot leaves the field entirely it resolves as a miss rather than stalling
interaction_model.state_change: Flight becomes off-screen-tracked while remaining in progress
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A marker slides along the top edge, following the projectile's horizontal position so its path stays legible while out of sight
interaction_model.input: Projectile rising above the visible frame
interaction_model.affected_object: Top-edge tracking marker

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Damage is cumulative and not undone between turns; it is cleared only by starting a fresh field
interaction_model.state_change: Intact surface becomes permanently cratered for the remainder of the match
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A hole is punched into the structure at the point of impact, clearly distinct from the intact surface, and stays there through later rounds
interaction_model.input: Projectile impact on a structure
interaction_model.affected_object: Structure surface

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The opposing turn is watchable rather than skipped, and control returns automatically without visitor action
interaction_model.state_change: Active side switches to the opposing side, then back
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The opposing side visibly aims and fires its own shot, after which the near side's projectile again carries the strongest emphasis in hand
interaction_model.input: Miss resolution
interaction_model.affected_object: Turn ownership

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The close is followed by an invitation to a fresh, undamaged skyline, so the experience loops from a clean state
interaction_model.state_change: In-play becomes won
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A clear, high-salience win announcement closes the match
interaction_model.input: Projectile striking the opponent
interaction_model.affected_object: Match state

experience_qualities: Suspenseful: each release has a watchable delay before short, long or true is known
Tactile: pulling and letting go feels like the physical act being depicted
Legible: angle, power, drifting force, flight path and impact form one readable cause-and-effect chain
Escalating: the battered field makes later rounds feel more consequential than the first
Forgiving before commitment, unforgiving after it
Playful and unhurried, with turn-by-turn rhythm rather than continuous pressure
completion_and_return: A hit ends the match with an explicit win moment
After the win, a fresh undamaged field is offered, restarting the loop
Structure damage persists for the whole match and is cleared only on a fresh field
Aim state resets to a resting projectile in hand at the start of every turn
An abandoned aim resolves simply by never releasing; nothing is left mid-flight
locked_observable_requirements: A single resting projectile reads as the pressable target for the side whose turn it is, standing out from the scenery behind it
Direction and strength are both set by one continuous press-and-drag gesture
A dotted path guide, the thrower's arm and live angle and power readouts all follow the pointer during aiming, remain readable over the scene, and disappear on release
Aim remains freely re-adjustable until release; release is the only commitment point
Flight follows a visibly curved, spinning path bent by an environmental drift force that is itself shown on screen above the scene
Exactly three visible outcomes: leaving the field, cratering a structure, or striking the opponent
Craters persist and accumulate on the scenery across rounds within a match, reading clearly as damage against intact surface
A miss hands the turn to the opposing side, whose aim and shot are visible rather than instantaneous
An edge marker tracks the projectile while it is above the visible frame
A hit produces a decisive win announcement followed by a fresh field
adaptable_details: Art style, colour treatment and lighting of the whole scene, and the identity of the two opposing characters and the lobbed object, provided the projectile, guide, readouts and craters stay separated enough to read
Silhouette, count and spacing of the destructible structures
Visual form of the drifting force indicator and the formatting of the angle and power readouts
Exact arc curvature, flight duration and force strength tuning
Crater shape and edge treatment
Whether the scene fills the viewport or sits inside a bounded panel
Whether the opposing side's turn is driven autonomously or by a second visitor, as long as its aim and shot remain visible
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits bounded side-view scenes with two opposing endpoints, open air between them and deformable ground or scenery in the middle, for any theme and any visual treatment built on lobbing something at a distant target. Replacing turn hand-off with continuous real-time control, removing the persistent damage so the field resets each shot, dropping the visible environmental drift that bends flight, or reducing it to single-side target practice with no opposing turn would each produce a different skill.

name: angled_stacking_pit_with_landing_shadow
description: A recessed pit seen from an elevated corner angle within a subdued, low-distraction surround: a high-salience falling piece is steered and turned while a translucent outline on the surface below shows exactly where it will land, the view can swing to another corner, and topping out collapses the whole stack.

canonical_document.name: angled_stacking_pit_with_landing_shadow
canonical_document.description: A recessed pit seen from an elevated corner angle within a subdued, low-distraction surround: a high-salience falling piece is steered and turned while a translucent outline on the surface below shows exactly where it will land, the view can swing to another corner, and topping out collapses the whole stack.
canonical_document.experience_scope: Whole-view experience that owns the main visual area. It begins with the arena held at reduced emphasis behind a short orienting primer, continues as an uninterrupted run of descending pieces, and ends when the stack reaches the top and collapses, followed immediately by an invitation to start again.
content_and_composition: One bounded recessed pit as the single spatial subject, rendered at an oblique elevated angle so its floor plane, depth and walls are all readable
Exactly one active piece at a time, the highest-salience and highest-contrast object in the scene
One accumulating mass of settled pieces resting on the pit floor, forming visible rows and depth layers
One translucent outline projected onto the surface directly beneath the active piece, marking its landing footprint
Low-distraction surrounding setting whose illumination sits at a clearly separated level from the pit, so the pit interior and the active piece stand out
Persistent compact readout of current score and pace, plus a remembered personal-best value
Short primer panel layered above the scene, present only before a run begins
Pit walls and rim as the always-visible legal boundary of movement
experience_progression: Idle state: arena visible at reduced emphasis with a brief orienting primer layered over it
Confirm starts the run and the primer clears away, leaving the scene unobstructed
Attention narrows to the active piece and the gap it should fill; pieces descend, are steered, and settle into the mass
Completed rows vanish and the descent pace tightens progressively as more rows are cleared
Stack reaches the top and the run ends in a spectacular collapse of the accumulated mass
Result is presented against the remembered personal best with an immediate invitation to go again
Confirm wipes the pit clean and the cycle restarts from the first piece
attention_and_information_flow: Before the run, the primer holds prominence and the arena reads as a recessed, low-emphasis backdrop
Once play begins the primer surrenders all prominence and never returns during the run
The active piece and its projected landing outline carry the highest prominence together, forming a single read of intended placement
The settled mass reads as secondary context whose surface shape communicates remaining gaps
Every move, turn or viewpoint change immediately re-informs the outline, so placement information is continuously refreshed rather than confirmed after the fact
Row clears momentarily pull attention to the affected rows and the rising pace
Collapse takes over the entire view, after which score and personal best come forward for the first time

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Has no effect once a run is already active; the primer does not reappear mid-run
interaction_model.state_change: Idle presentation becomes an active run
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Primer clears away and the first piece appears in play with focus on the pit interior
interaction_model.input: Confirm key while idle
interaction_model.affected_object: Primer panel and arena

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Movement that would overlap settled blocks or leave the pit is refused with no displacement at all; the opposite direction reverses any accepted step
interaction_model.state_change: Piece translates one step across the floor plane in the direction seen on screen
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Piece and its translucent ground outline shift together in step, keeping the predicted landing spot current
interaction_model.input: Left or right directional keys
interaction_model.affected_object: Active piece and its projected landing outline

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: A rotation pressed against a wall is nudged back inside the pit rather than refused; an impossible rotation leaves the piece unchanged
interaction_model.state_change: Piece turns a quarter turn to a new orientation
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Piece and the shape of its footprint outline update to the new orientation
interaction_model.input: Rotate key
interaction_model.affected_object: Active piece and its projected landing outline

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Committing is final for that piece; recovery happens through placement of subsequent pieces
interaction_model.state_change: Piece plunges immediately to the marked footprint and joins the settled mass
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Piece travels down fast, lands exactly on the outlined cells, and the next piece enters play
interaction_model.input: Drop key
interaction_model.affected_object: Active piece and settled mass

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Reversible by shifting the other way and cyclable around the corners; after the swing, directional movement continues to follow what is seen on screen so control never inverts
interaction_model.state_change: Vantage moves to the next corner of the pit
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The arena swings to a new oblique angle, revealing previously obscured depth, and the landing outline is read from the new angle
interaction_model.input: Shift modifier with left or right
interaction_model.affected_object: Whole arena viewpoint

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Pace resets to its starting value when a new run begins
interaction_model.state_change: Piece falls continuously, with the interval shortening as rows are cleared
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Visibly faster descent later in a run, raising urgency
interaction_model.input: Autonomous descent timing
interaction_model.affected_object: Active piece

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Not reversible; it is the rewarded outcome of play
interaction_model.state_change: The filled row is removed and the stack settles
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Row vanishes, remaining mass drops into place, score increases and pace tightens
interaction_model.input: A row filled completely by a landing piece
interaction_model.affected_object: Settled mass and score readout

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The same confirm key wipes the pit and starts a fresh run from an empty state
interaction_model.state_change: Run ends and the arena enters its outcome state
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Spectacular collapse of the accumulated mass, then the run result shown against the personal best with a prompt to play again
interaction_model.input: Stack reaching the top of the pit
interaction_model.affected_object: Entire pit contents

experience_qualities: Dramatic and theatrical, with the play space separated from its surround by a strong luminance step so it appears to glow out of it
Spatial and depth-aware: judging how far back a piece sits is as tense as judging left and right
Predictive rather than guesswork, because the projected outline answers where a piece will land before it lands
Escalating urgency as the descent tightens
Decisive and tactile, with refusals that feel like solid walls rather than errors
Spectacular, clearly punctuated ending
Frictionless retry that keeps a visitor in the loop
completion_and_return: A run ends only when the stack tops out; there is no partial success state
Ending plays a full-view collapse before any result is shown
Result is framed as a comparison against a remembered personal best rather than a bare number
One confirm keypress clears the pit and returns the experience to a fresh run
Personal best persists across runs while score, stack, and pace reset each time
locked_observable_requirements: Bounded pit shown from an oblique elevated angle so depth position is visible and consequential, not a flat head-on field
Low-distraction surround in which the active piece holds the strongest luminance and contrast separation from every other element
Exactly one translucent landing footprint projected on the surface below the active piece, updating on every move, turn and viewpoint change
Discrete viewpoint switching between corner vantages, with directional control remaining relative to what is seen on screen afterward
Illegal moves refused with zero visible displacement, while a rotation blocked by a wall is nudged back inside the boundary
Descent pace that visibly tightens as rows are cleared
Orienting primer that is present before the run and clears completely once it begins
Top-out resolved as a spectacular collapse of the whole stack, followed by a personal-best comparison and a single-key immediate restart
adaptable_details: Shapes and colour assignments of the falling pieces
Pit width, depth and height proportions
Palette, theme direction, lighting style and material treatment, as long as the luminance separations still read
Specific key assignments and modifier choice
Scoring values and pace curve
Primer wording and layout
Choreography and duration of the collapse
Number of selectable corner vantages
Placement and styling of score and best-score readouts
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any bounded volume where objects arrive or are placed into a stack and a projected footprint guides depth-aware positioning under keyboard control, with a decisive end state and instant restart. Flattening the view so depth no longer needs judging, removing the projected landing outline, fixing the viewpoint so no corner switching exists, or replacing direct keyed control with pointer dragging or passive playback would each produce a different skill.

name: spotlit_glide_and_collect_rink
description: One small character skates across a glossy, reflective surface toward wherever the visitor aims, arriving late and overshooting, scoring fading grooves behind it, spinning into the air on a press, and bursting a lone high-accent treat that instantly springs up elsewhere.

canonical_document.name: spotlit_glide_and_collect_rink
canonical_document.description: One small character skates across a glossy, reflective surface toward wherever the visitor aims, arriving late and overshooting, scoring fading grooves behind it, spinning into the air on a press, and bursting a lone high-accent treat that instantly springs up elsewhere.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A bounded region or whole-view playfield that begins the moment the visitor arrives, with the character already standing idle in the single pool of illumination, and never concludes; it is a continuous ambient activity that can be embedded as a self-contained area with no entry or exit sequence.
content_and_composition: Exactly one small animated character as the sole protagonist, always visible and always the most strongly lit figure in the field
Exactly one high-accent collectible treat present at a time, placed out on the surface away from the character
One soft pool of illumination on a glossy surface held clearly below it in luminance, with the periphery falling off in a controlled luminance transition so the field has no drawn edge
A mirrored reflection and soft shadow of the character smeared into the surface directly beneath it, moving with it
A dashed thread drawn between the aimed spot and the character, making the pull between intention and figure visible
Pairs of parallel grooves layered beneath the character, accumulating along the travelled path and fading over time
One short persistent line of hint text at the periphery explaining that pressing jumps
experience_progression: Rest: character stands alone in the pool of illumination, no grooves, one treat waiting elsewhere
Pursuit: character accelerates toward the aimed spot, leans into travel direction, appendages sweep back with speed, grooves thin as it accelerates
Arrival: character passes slightly beyond the aimed spot, swings back and settles instead of stopping exactly on it
Reward: proximity to the treat bursts it into scattering pieces and a fresh treat springs up in a new place, immediately re-baiting attention
Loop: the chase repeats indefinitely with no tally, no loss and no ending; grooves fade back to a clean surface between passes
attention_and_information_flow: Two competing focal points: the illuminated, expressively moving character and the high-accent treat waiting somewhere out on the surface
The dashed thread continuously reveals the visitor's aimed destination and how far behind it the character currently is
Groove density and depth read as a record of recent movement: deep, tight marks where the character crawled, faint marks where it raced
The burst of scattering pieces takes attention for a beat, then the newly appearing treat pulls attention to a different part of the field
The luminance falloff at the far edges suppresses the periphery so nothing outside the lit chase competes for notice

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Re-aiming at any moment redirects the pursuit mid-glide; the destination can never be placed outside the field, so the character cannot be dragged over the edge; leaving the pointer still lets it coast to rest
interaction_model.state_change: The destination relocates to the aimed spot, clamped well inside the field, and the character accelerates toward it, overshoots and settles rather than snapping into place
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Dashed thread stretches between spot and character; the character swivels to face its actual travel direction, its appendages sweep further back the faster it moves, and its reflection and shadow slide with it
interaction_model.input: Visitor aims or moves the pointer anywhere over the field
interaction_model.affected_object: Aimed destination spot and the character

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Further presses are ignored while airborne and are not queued; grounded pursuit resumes automatically on landing with no reset of the aimed destination
interaction_model.state_change: The character launches into a spinning leap, higher and with more turns the faster it was already moving, and remains airborne until it lands
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A rising arc with visible rotations, a gap in the groove record while off the surface, and the shadow separating beneath the airborne figure
interaction_model.input: Visitor presses
interaction_model.affected_object: The character

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Nothing is counted or lost; a new target is always available immediately, so the loop cannot stall or be failed
interaction_model.state_change: The treat bursts apart and a fresh one springs up in a different place on the field
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Scattering pieces flung outward from the collection point, followed by a new high-accent treat appearing elsewhere
interaction_model.input: Character drifts within reach of the treat (outcome of pursuit, not a separate input)
interaction_model.affected_object: The collectible treat

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Fading is autonomous and needs no input; marks never accumulate permanently and never obscure the character or treat
interaction_model.state_change: Grooves linger and then slowly fade, cut deep when the character was crawling and barely marking at speed
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A pair of parallel tracks that persist behind the character and gradually dissolve, leaving the surface clean again
interaction_model.input: Passage of time after the character travels over a stretch of surface
interaction_model.affected_object: Groove marks on the surface

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Any new aim resumes the chase from wherever the character came to rest
interaction_model.state_change: Pursuit force falls away and the character decelerates to a standstill
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A gliding slowdown into an idle stance with appendages settling forward, grooves deepening briefly as speed drops, then fading
interaction_model.input: Pointer left still
interaction_model.affected_object: The character

experience_qualities: Weighty and always slightly late, never rigidly attached to the pointer
Loose and playful, with expressive lean, swivel and speed-driven secondary motion
Calm and endlessly repeating, with no pressure, tally or conclusion
Intimate and theatrical: one small figure isolated by a single soft light, with everything beyond it falling away in luminance until it reads as empty surround
Glossy and reflective, so the character feels seated on the surface rather than floating over it
Immediately rewarding, with each collection provoking the desire for the next
completion_and_return: No completion state, score, streak or failure; the activity loops for as long as the visitor stays
Each collected treat is replaced at once by a fresh one in a new location, restarting the pursuit
Surface marks decay back to a clean field, so the scene self-restores rather than filling up
Idleness returns the character to a resting stance inside the pool of illumination rather than ending the experience
Airborne state always resolves back to grounded pursuit on landing
locked_observable_requirements: The character pursues an aimed destination with acceleration, visible overshoot and settling, never snapping to the pointer
Facing direction follows actual travel direction, and at least one appendage or secondary element deforms in proportion to speed
A visible dashed connector between the aimed spot and the character makes the pull explicit while pursuing
Paired lingering surface marks that fade over time, strong at low speed and faint at high speed, and absent while airborne
A press triggers a spinning leap whose height and number of turns scale with the character's current speed, with further presses ignored until landing
Exactly one collectible present at a time, collected by proximity rather than a click, bursting into scattering pieces and respawning elsewhere
The aimed destination is clamped inside the field so the character can never be pulled past the edge
Pointer stillness produces a coast to rest, not an instant stop

A glossy, mark-taking surface sitting clearly below a single soft pool of illumination in luminance, with the character's reflection and shadow beneath it, and a periphery that dissolves through a luminance falloff rather than a drawn boundary
No score, timer, loss or ending anywhere in the experience
adaptable_details: Identity and silhouette of the character and of the collectible

Hue and temperature of the illumination, the surface and the treat, provided the illuminated pool stays clearly separated in luminance from its surround and the treat keeps the strongest accent in the field
Surface material read (ice, polished floor, wet stone) as long as it stays glossy and mark-taking
Number, shape and spacing of the trailing marks
Exact acceleration, overshoot amount, fade duration and leap scaling values
Dash pattern, thickness and hue of the connector thread, as long as it stays readable against the surface it crosses
Wording and placement of the short hint line
Pointer, touch or drag as the aiming input
Shape and count of the scattering pieces in the collection burst
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any bounded playful field where a single lightly-animated figure is led around a mark-taking surface by an aimed point while a lone respawning target keeps the loop going, including mascot moments, empty-state amusements and campaign play areas; the figure, target and surface material can all be swapped, and the illumination and surface may take any hue as long as their luminance separation holds. It becomes a different skill if multiple characters or several simultaneous targets appear, if scoring, timing, hazards or an ending are introduced, if the figure is dragged rigidly to the pointer instead of chasing it with lag, if a hard drawn boundary or level layout replaces the luminance-fading field, or if the view scrolls or follows the character beyond the single illuminated area.

name: soap_film_bubble_toy_stage
description: An empty stage of one uniform, low-distraction tone holding a few familiar bubble-making implements; sweeping one drags a stretching, sagging soap film that keeps pinching free into shimmering bubbles which drift, squash into clusters, can be pushed, dragged or pricked into sparks, and eventually pop on their own.

canonical_document.name: soap_film_bubble_toy_stage
canonical_document.description: An empty stage of one uniform, low-distraction tone holding a few familiar bubble-making implements; sweeping one drags a stretching, sagging soap film that keeps pinching free into shimmering bubbles which drift, squash into clusters, can be pushed, dragged or pricked into sparks, and eventually pop on their own.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A self-contained stage experience with no entry or exit state: it begins the moment the view appears with the implements at rest in an empty field and continues indefinitely, cycling back to a calm empty stage whenever bubbles have gone. Deployable as a full-view page or as one large bounded panel, but it always occupies its own region exclusively and hosts no other content.
content_and_composition: One bare stage of a single uniform, low-distraction tone acting as the entire backdrop, held far enough in luminance from the film and bubble walls that they stay clearly readable, with no headings, labels, instructions or decorative framing
A small set (roughly three) of visually distinct hand implements resting in the stage, each shaped so its own action reads at a glance: a drawing ring, a directional pusher, a fine point
One continuous deformable soap film attached to the drawing implement while it is in use, rendered as a thin elastic membrane that visibly lengthens and slackens
Many free-floating bubbles of varying size with translucent walls carrying a thin-film interference sheen in any hue set, that touch, flatten against one another and hold together as loose clusters
Short-lived, high-salience spark scatter that replaces a bubble at the instant it bursts
Persistent visible stage edges that bound the play area; implements are permanent and always reusable, the stage itself never changes
experience_progression: Rest: implements sit still in an empty field, nothing in motion
Grab and draw: an implement is picked up and swept, the film stretches, sags and wobbles behind it
Pinch-off: the film repeatedly necks and separates, releasing new bubbles
Accumulation: freed bubbles drift, collide, squash and settle into clusters
Self-clearing: bubbles burst on their own over time, thinning the stage
Return to rest: the stage becomes calm and empty again and the cycle can repeat indefinitely
attention_and_information_flow: With an otherwise empty field, the implements are the only things to look at, so they read as the invitation without any prompt
Once a sweep begins, prominence shifts to the film's deformation, its stretch, sag and wobble carrying the sense of effort
At each pinch-off, attention hands over from the film to the newly freed bubble
As bubbles accumulate, focus becomes ambient and distributed across drifting clusters
Bursts and their spark scatter pull a brief, sharp spike of attention before the field quiets again
All information is carried by material behavior: no counters, meters, labels or textual state anywhere

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Only one grab exists at a time; releasing ends it immediately with the implement left in a settled, usable state, and it can never be dragged past the visible stage edges
interaction_model.state_change: Idle implement becomes the single grabbed object bound to the pointer
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The implement leaves its resting spot, follows the pointer, and tilts so it trails the direction of the sweep
interaction_model.input: Press or touch near one of the implements
interaction_model.affected_object: That implement

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Slowing or stopping lets the film settle without breaking; releasing ends the draw cleanly with no half-formed bubble left hanging
interaction_model.state_change: Film lengthens under the ring's motion, then necks and separates repeatedly
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A trailing sheet stretches, sags under its own weight and wobbles, then pinches free into shimmering bubbles that drift away
interaction_model.input: Sweep the grabbed drawing ring across the stage
interaction_model.affected_object: Soap film and the bubbles it produces

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The push exists only while the implement is held and aimed; anything driven past the boundary is eased back into view rather than lost
interaction_model.state_change: A directional push is applied along the implement's aim
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The film balloons and inflates while bubbles in the path visibly shove and drift along the aimed direction
interaction_model.input: Turn or aim the grabbed pushing implement
interaction_model.affected_object: The active film and nearby bubbles

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The burst is final for that bubble and cannot be undone, but new bubbles are always freely makeable, so nothing is permanently lost
interaction_model.state_change: Intact bubble becomes burst on contact, with no delay or confirmation
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The bubble vanishes instantly into a scatter of sparks that fades
interaction_model.input: Bring the fine point against a bubble wall
interaction_model.affected_object: That single bubble

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The pull is capped, so fast or distant motion simply loses hold; releasing returns the bubble to ordinary free drift
interaction_model.state_change: The bubble becomes elastically tethered to the pointer within a limited range
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The bubble follows the pointer with a springy lag, deforming as it is towed and jostling neighbors it passes
interaction_model.input: Press inside an existing bubble and move the pointer
interaction_model.affected_object: That whole bubble

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Fully automatic and unstoppable; it guarantees the stage always self-clears back to a ready state without any reset control
interaction_model.state_change: Bubbles reach the end of their life and burst spontaneously
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Bubbles pop one by one until the stage is quiet and empty again
interaction_model.input: Passage of time, with no user input
interaction_model.affected_object: Every existing bubble

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Continuous and self-correcting, so the stage cannot be emptied or broken by overshooting
interaction_model.state_change: Out-of-bounds material is pulled back into the play area
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Escaped parts ease smoothly back into view instead of clipping, sticking or disappearing
interaction_model.input: Film or bubble drifts past the visible boundary
interaction_model.affected_object: Straying film vertices and bubbles

experience_qualities: Tactile and material-honest: everything stretches, sags, squashes and springs the way real soap film would
Immediately legible with no explanation needed
Calm and unhurried, with slow drift between brief bursts of activity
Forgiving and failure-free: nothing can be broken, scored or lost
Self-clearing, so the stage always returns to invitation rather than clutter
Delicate and shimmering, with thin-film iridescence across the walls and brief high-salience spark accents
Endlessly repeatable without diminishing returns
completion_and_return: No completion, win state, score or end screen exists
The loop is continuous: play produces bubbles, spontaneous bursting removes them, the empty ready stage returns
Releasing the pointer always leaves a settled state with nothing half-finished
Implements return to being available immediately after release; no persistent progress or accumulated state carries forward
locked_observable_requirements: A bare, uncluttered stage of one uniform, low-distraction tone that stays clearly separated in luminance from the film and bubbles, with no instructional text, labels or counters
A small set of visually distinct implements, each producing its own clearly different visible effect
Bubbles must be born from a film that visibly stretches, sags, wobbles and pinches off, never spawned instantly out of nothing
Bubbles must be translucent and shimmer with a shifting thin-film sheen in any hues, drift freely, squash against one another and hold as clusters
Point contact bursts a bubble immediately into a scatter of sparks that reads as a sharp, high-salience flash against the stage
Dragging a bubble from inside is springy and range-limited rather than rigidly attached
Bubbles burst on their own over time so the stage self-clears to a calm ready state
One pointer, one grab at a time, with release always leaving a clean state
Nothing escapes the visible edges: implements are bounded and stray material is eased back in
adaptable_details: Exact number, shapes and resting arrangement of the implements
Hue set, shimmer treatment and lighting of the film and bubble walls, and the stage's own tone, as long as separation and readable contrast hold
Bubble size range, drift speed and lifetime before spontaneous bursting
Amount of film sag, wobble frequency and pinch-off cadence
Spark count, spread and fade duration on burst
Stage proportions and whether it fills the view or sits as one large panel
Strength and range limit of the springy bubble drag
Input device (mouse, pen or touch) as long as a single contact drives everything
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any open-ended play surface where a soft, lifelike physical material is the entire content, no readable information sits on top of it, and the space is expected to keep inviting repeat experimentation on its own. It transfers whole to full-page toys or large dedicated stage sections, under any host tone as long as the stage stays low-distraction and separated in luminance from the film and bubbles. Substituting rigid discrete objects for a continuous deformable membrane, removing the self-clearing lifetime so the stage fills up permanently, adding goals, scoring or levels, or placing text and data on top of the stage would each produce a different Skill.

name: fuzzy_shoveable_ball_in_bare_room
description: A thickly furred ball drops into an empty, evenly lit room, settles, and can be shoved across the floor by dragging anywhere in the view; the coat sweeps back and springs forward with every push, the shadow follows underneath, heavy landings jolt the whole view, and the ball always rolls back to a slow resting spin without leaving sight.

canonical_document.name: fuzzy_shoveable_ball_in_bare_room
canonical_document.description: A thickly furred ball drops into an empty, evenly lit room, settles, and can be shoved across the floor by dragging anywhere in the view; the coat sweeps back and springs forward with every push, the shadow follows underneath, heavy landings jolt the whole view, and the ball always rolls back to a slow resting spin without leaving sight.
canonical_document.experience_scope: A whole-view experience for one region: it begins the moment the view opens with the object falling in, occupies the entire visible area as the only content, accepts input anywhere over the view, and has no end state — it cycles indefinitely between rest and play.
content_and_composition: Exactly one foreground object: a rounded body wearing a thick, dense, fibrous coat that reads as soft and full of loft
One ground plane the object rests, bounces and rolls on, occupying the lower part of the view
A bare, evenly and uniformly lit enclosure as the only backdrop, held visually quieter and lower in salience than the object, with no scenery, decoration or competing objects
A contact shadow anchored directly beneath the object, persistently tracking its position and height
An invisible containment boundary just inside the framing, never drawn but always felt through deflections
No instructional text, no labels, no buttons or visible controls anywhere in the view
experience_progression: Entry: the object falls into the empty room from above
Settling: it lands, the coat compresses and rebounds, and the body loses its remaining bounce
Idle rest: it sits still on the ground with a slow, lazy spin, plainly available to be disturbed
Play bout: a press-and-drag shoves it away and the coat and shadow answer immediately
Free travel: it keeps going after release — arcing, falling, bouncing and rolling — while drags can redirect it at any moment
Decay and return to rest: motion bleeds off on its own until it is idle again, and the loop repeats without limit
attention_and_information_flow: Attention is pinned to the one object from the first frame and never handed to another element
The unprompted entry drop is what communicates that the object is soft and handleable, replacing any instruction or hint
Softness is read from coat motion: the sweep-back and spring-forward lag behind the body's movement
Weight is read from bounce height, rolling persistence, shadow closeness and the brief jolt of the whole view on hard impacts

The bare, evenly lit room — kept low in visual salience so the object separates clearly from it — and the lack of any interface remove all competing information, so only the object's material and behaviour are ever on display
At rest the lazy spin keeps the object quietly alive and signals that it is still available

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The shove can be repeated freely; the object always slows to a stop by itself, so no input can leave it in an unusable state
interaction_model.state_change: Gains a shove along the ground in the drag's direction, with faster drags shoving harder; the impulse is never a straight-up lift
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The object lurches away and travels across the floor while the coat sweeps back against the motion and springs forward again, and the shadow slides along underneath
interaction_model.input: Press and drag anywhere over the view
interaction_model.affected_object: The furred object

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The coast-down always completes on its own and ends in the resting idle state
interaction_model.state_change: Keeps its momentum and continues under gravity — travelling, falling, bouncing and rolling — while friction bleeds the motion away
interaction_model.visible_feedback: An arcing throw, successive shrinking bounces, rolling that turns the coat over, and a gradual coast down to stillness
interaction_model.input: Release of the drag
interaction_model.affected_object: The furred object

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Redirects can be chained indefinitely without waiting for the previous motion to finish
interaction_model.state_change: Its existing motion is immediately overridden and redirected along the new drag
