name: pointer_aimed_glowing_bar_field
description: A quiet, featureless expanse filled edge to edge with a dense grid of tiny upright glowing bars that all pivot to point at the cursor, with a small bright pool of light following it while the rest sinks back to the surround's own level; dragging swings the viewpoint around the field so the glow can be seen from the side or above.

experience_qualities: Atmospheric and low-key, with emitted light as the only material and the surround holding no detail of its own
Immediately understandable within a few seconds of moving the pointer
Hypnotic and calming enough to stay with for a long time
Responsive to the point of feeling physically attached to the hand
Volumetric: the field reads as a real three-dimensional mass, not a flat graphic
Open-ended and consequence-free, with nothing to achieve
locked_observable_requirements: A dense field of many small upright glowing elements filling the view against a single uniform surround that sits far below the elements' peak luminance
All elements orient toward the pointer position simultaneously
Brightness falls off with distance from the pointer so a small area reads far brighter and remote areas settle to the surround's own level
The bright region tracks the pointer with no perceptible lag
Drag orbits the viewpoint around the field, revealing it as a volume with real depth including side and overhead views
Viewing distance never changes, so the field can never be lost, emptied or zoomed away
Aiming and brightening continue during and after viewpoint changes
No completion, reset or failure state
canonical_document.name: pointer_aimed_glowing_bar_field
canonical_document.experience_scope: Whole-view experience that occupies the entire viewport from arrival onward; it has no entry gate and no exit state, and it remains the single continuous scene for as long as the view is open. It can also be scoped to a large self-contained region so long as that region reads as its own luminous volume with its own quiet surround.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any view whose purpose is atmosphere, calm idle play or a luminous visual centerpiece with little or no reading required, and works as a large decorative region or a whole standalone view. Meaning-bearing content can only be layered over it sparsely in the unlit outer areas where luminance has fallen to the surround level. Binding each element to a data value, letting the pointer select or open individual elements, adding zoom or free travel through the field, or replacing the aim-and-brighten response with a different reaction such as ripples or repulsion would create a different Skill.
content_and_composition: A single visual subject: one dense field of many small upright bar-like light elements, numerous enough to read as a continuous luminous surface rather than countable objects
Elements are laid out across a broad ground plane so the field extends toward the edges of the view and suggests real depth rather than a flat printed pattern

A single uniform surround, far below the lit elements in luminance and carrying no texture of its own, provides the only backdrop; there is no framing chrome, panel or caption competing with the field
One transient highlight role: a small localized bright area that reads far brighter than everything around it and is always attached to the pointer position
Persistent elements are only the field itself and the empty surround; nothing else stays on screen
Optional minimal foreground text or a single control cluster may overlay the unlit outer regions, but the field is the primary content, not a backdrop for dense reading
attention_and_information_flow: On arrival the whole luminous surface is read at once as one texture, establishing scale and the emptiness of the surround
Attention then narrows to the small bright pool because its luminance contrast against the surround is extreme
Attention alternates between the local bright pool and the overall field as the pointer moves, so both the detail and the whole are re-read repeatedly
Orientation of the bars conveys direction information: the whole field visibly points at wherever the pointer is, so position is legible even in the unlit regions
Viewpoint change reveals the field's thickness and layering, converting the surface reading into a volume reading
No labels, numbers or explanatory information are revealed at any point; all information is carried by brightness and orientation

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Fully continuous and reversible: moving back restores the previous appearance exactly, and stopping simply leaves the field aimed where the pointer rests
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A soft bright pool travels with the pointer while the surrounding field visibly rotates to face it, with no perceptible lag between pointer motion and field response
interaction_model.input: Pointer moving across the scene
interaction_model.state_change: Each bar reorients to aim toward the pointer position, and its luminance is set by how near it is to that position, so nearby bars go bright and distant ones fall back to the surround level
interaction_model.affected_object: Every bar in the field, plus the localized bright region

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Releasing keeps the reached angle; the aiming and brightening behavior continues uninterrupted during and after the drag, and any angle can be undone by dragging back
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The field rotates as a solid volume, exposing the bars' height and the depth of the lit region rather than re-drawing a flat pattern
interaction_model.input: Press and drag anywhere in the scene
interaction_model.state_change: The viewing angle swings around the field, from a low side-on view through to looking down from above
interaction_model.affected_object: The viewpoint on the whole field

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Resumes immediately and seamlessly on the next pointer movement
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The scene stays quietly lit at its last position, remaining pleasant to look at while idle
interaction_model.input: Pointer leaving or resting without movement

completion_and_return: No completion, goal, score or end state exists

name: hold_to_break_and_place_block_loop
description: Hold on whatever unit sits under the centre crosshair within arm's reach and watch a swinging hand crack it apart in visible stages until it breaks and lands in a numbered belt, then set units from that belt back into the world face by face.

experience_qualities: Tactile and physical, with weight behind each strike
Deliberate rather than instant — effort is visible before result
Forgiving: every interruption returns to exactly the prior state
Legible, with progress and stock always readable on screen
Unhurried, penalty-free and sandbox-open
locked_observable_requirements: Aiming is done with a fixed centre reticle, never with a free-moving cursor.
Only one unit is actionable at a time, and only within a short fixed reach of a few cells.
Breaking must read as staged, visible wear accompanied by repeated strike motion — never an instant disappearance.
Interrupting a hold by releasing or looking away erases all accumulated wear and removes nothing.
Gathered units appear in a persistently visible numbered belt with counts and exactly one highlighted selection.
Placement snaps to the face being aimed at and spends exactly one unit from the selected slot.
Cells that are already filled, and the cell the visitor occupies, are refused with no unit spent.
Selection is switchable both by direct numbered keys and by stepping through slots.
canonical_document.name: hold_to_break_and_place_block_loop
canonical_document.experience_scope: A persistent interaction layer occupying the embodied view rather than a bounded panel. Each cycle begins when a reachable unit is under the reticle and a hold starts, and ends on break, on cancel, or on a placement; the reticle and the belt persist for the whole session.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any grid-organized three-dimensional or two-and-a-half-dimensional scene where the visitor both removes and re-places discrete units from a reach-limited, viewpoint-centred position — sandbox worlds, editable dioramas, tile gardens, modular arrangement toys explored from inside. It depends on discrete cells, a short reach, staged wear and a visible stock. Swapping the centre reticle for free drag-and-drop, replacing staged wear with instant deletion, or hiding the gathered stock would each produce a different skill.
content_and_composition: A fixed centre reticle as the only aiming instrument — there is no free pointer to move over targets.
Exactly one eligible target at a time: the solid cell under the reticle within a short reach of roughly five cells; anything further away stays inert.
A progressive damage treatment on the current target that deepens in discrete visible steps as the hold continues.
A first-person hand or tool that swings in repeated strikes for as long as the hold lasts.
A persistent numbered belt of slots across the view holding gathered units with per-slot counts and one slot visibly highlighted as selected.
The world grid itself as the mutable surface: units disappear from and reappear in cells in place, exposing or covering neighbouring faces.
attention_and_information_flow: Attention collapses from the whole scene to the single unit under the reticle the moment a hold begins.
The deepening cracks carry all of the progress information — how close the unit is to breaking is read off its own surface, not off a separate meter.
The belt keeps a permanently visible answer to 'what is there to build with', with the selected slot standing out from the rest.
Refusals and cancels are read directly from the world: nothing changes and no count moves, so the grid and the belt remain the only source of truth.

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Releasing early, or turning the reticle off the target, cancels immediately — the cracks disappear, the unit is intact, nothing is removed and nothing is gained; the hold can simply be started again
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The hand swings in repeated strikes and crack marks deepen step by step on the targeted unit only
interaction_model.input: Primary button held while the reticle rests on a unit within reach
interaction_model.state_change: That single unit enters a wearing-down state that advances in stages for as long as the hold continues
interaction_model.affected_object: The targeted unit and the first-person hand

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The emptied cell becomes immediately available to build into again; the only way back is to place the gathered unit
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The unit vanishes, leaving neighbouring faces newly exposed, and the belt slot count rises
interaction_model.input: The hold continuing until the wear completes
interaction_model.state_change: The unit is removed from its cell and one unit is added to a numbered belt slot
interaction_model.affected_object: The targeted unit and the belt

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Cells already filled, and the cell the visitor is standing in, are refused — nothing appears and no unit is spent; a regretted placement is recovered by wearing that unit back down
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The new unit appears snapped flush into the grid against the aimed face while the belt count decrements
interaction_model.input: Secondary button pressed while aiming at a face
interaction_model.state_change: A unit of the selected type occupies that cell and the slot's count drops by one
interaction_model.affected_object: The empty cell against the aimed face, and the selected belt slot

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Selection can be changed freely at any time and never alters the world; a slot with nothing in it places nothing
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The highlight moves to the new slot, and that slot's type is what the next placement puts down
interaction_model.input: Number keys, or stepping through slots with wheel movement
interaction_model.state_change: The selected slot changes
interaction_model.affected_object: Belt selection

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Stepping closer brings the same unit into reach and the hold behaves normally
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Distant units never begin to crack no matter how long the hold lasts
interaction_model.input: Aiming at something beyond reach
interaction_model.state_change: No target is acquired
interaction_model.affected_object: Target eligibility

adaptable_details: What the units represent — terrain material, plants, tiles, parts, props
Crack or wear artwork and how many visible stages it has
How long a unit takes to wear down, including different durations per material
Appearance of the hand or tool and the rhythm of its swing
Belt length, screen placement and slot styling
Exact reach distance and cell size
Sound accompanying strikes, breaks and placements
Whether identical units stack in one slot or occupy separate slots
canonical_document.description: Hold on whatever unit sits under the centre crosshair within arm's reach and watch a swinging hand crack it apart in visible stages until it breaks and lands in a numbered belt, then set units from that belt back into the world face by face.
experience_progression: Aim: the reticle rests on a reachable unit and nothing has changed yet.
Wear: the hold begins, the hand starts swinging, and cracks accumulate step by step on that one unit.
Break: the wear completes, the unit vanishes from its cell, and one unit lands in a belt slot with its count rising.
Place: a selected unit is set onto the face being aimed at, spending one from the belt.
The gather-and-rebuild loop repeats indefinitely at the visitor's own pace, with no target quantity and no finish line.
completion_and_return: No score, no failure and no ending; the loop is open-ended and paced entirely by the visitor.
Every hold resolves one of two ways: completed into a gathered unit, or cancelled back to an untouched unit with all wear erased.
Gathered units stay on show in the belt until spent, so the accumulated stock persists visibly through the session.
Removals and placements persist in the world; the world is only ever restored by rebuilding it by hand.

name: keystroke_printed_sheet_over_reacting_machine
description: A sheet of paper fills the focus while text lands on it character by character, and the solid machine body pictured just below dips its matching key with a short click on every keystroke, with a heavier carriage sound when a new line begins.

experience_qualities: Immediately usable: obvious and productive within a second of opening, with nothing to click or configure
Mechanical and tactile: input feels like it moves a physical object
Nostalgic and weighty rather than flat and digital
Tightly synchronized: response lands on the same beat as each character
Forgiving and low-stakes: mistakes are fixed in place and nothing must be finished
Calm and uncluttered, with the written words as the only growing content
locked_observable_requirements: Typing works the instant the view opens, with nothing to click or focus first
Each printable keystroke, space included, adds exactly one character to the paper surface
The key on the depicted keyboard that matches the pressed key visibly dips and springs back for every keystroke
Each keystroke is accompanied by a short mechanical click, and rapid bursts overlap their clicks instead of cutting each other off
A return advances to a fresh line with a distinctly heavier mechanical sound than a normal keystroke
Backspace removes the last character in place, at the point of writing
The machine reads as one solid object positioned beneath the sheet, visually continuous with it
A faint prompt occupies the exact position where the first characters will appear, and only before anything is written
The writing position and freshest line stay visible after the surface fills
A small, quiet running tally of how much has been written is present without competing for attention
The paper surface remains the attention center; the machine never overtakes it
No keystroke is silently dropped, even if typing focus is momentarily lost
canonical_document.name: keystroke_printed_sheet_over_reacting_machine
canonical_document.experience_scope: Whole-view single-screen experience covering the paper surface and the machine beneath it; it is live from the moment the page opens and never ends, with no separate start, submit or finish stage.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits single-surface free-writing views where visitor-authored text is the whole foreground and a depicted device mirrors keyboard input one character at a time: writing pages, letter or note composers, playful keepsake or guestbook-style views, and themed single-object landing centerpieces. It requires a physical keyboard as the driver and a strict per-keystroke visible and audible machine response. It becomes a different skill if input shifts to pointer or tap gestures, if the device responds only in aggregate or on a delay rather than per character, if the surface becomes an editable document with cursor navigation, selection and saving, or if the text becomes one field among structured form content rather than the view's sole growing content.
content_and_composition: One writing surface styled as a sheet of paper, occupying the upper attention center of the view
One machine body directly below the sheet, reading as a single solid mechanical object rather than a set of separate widgets
One depicted keyboard belonging to that machine body, with individually identifiable keys that correspond to real keys
One short invitation line that makes the immediate 'just type' premise obvious without instructions or setup
One faint placeholder prompt sitting exactly where the first characters will appear, shown only while the sheet is still empty
One small running tally of how much has been written, kept quiet and peripheral
Layering: paper in front and above, machine as the base beneath, arranged as one continuous physical stack so the text and the mechanism read as the same object
attention_and_information_flow: The sheet and the newest line hold primary attention throughout; the freshest wording is always the most visible content
Machine motion is confirming peripheral feedback: noticed as physical response, never competing with the text for focus
The faint prompt communicates where writing will land, then yields entirely to real content on the first keystroke
The running tally stays deliberately quiet ambient information, readable on a glance but never drawing the eye away
The invitation carries meaning only at the start and recedes in importance once wording exists

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: No commit step is needed; the last character can be removed immediately, and typing continues without any mode change
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The character appears on the sheet as the pictured key dips and springs back, paired with a short mechanical click
interaction_model.input: Any printable keystroke, including the space bar
interaction_model.state_change: Exactly one character is appended at the writing position and the corresponding key moves from rest to pressed and back
interaction_model.affected_object: Text on the paper surface and the matching key on the depicted keyboard

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Typing simply resumes on the new line; the previous line stays on the sheet as written
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Text visibly drops to a new line accompanied by a heavier carriage-style sound distinct from a normal key click
interaction_model.input: Return key
interaction_model.state_change: The writing position moves to a fresh line below
interaction_model.affected_object: Writing position on the paper surface and the machine's line-advance response

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Acts as the in-place undo for the whole experience; with an empty sheet nothing is removed and the view stays in its empty state
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The character disappears in place so the correction happens where the mistake was made
interaction_model.input: Backspace key
interaction_model.state_change: The last character is removed and the writing position steps back
interaction_model.affected_object: Most recently written character on the paper surface

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Feedback never falls behind or cancels earlier responses; slowing down returns to distinct single clicks
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Every keystroke keeps its own key dip and click, clicks layering over each other so rapid typing sounds and looks dense rather than clipped or dropped
interaction_model.input: Fast bursts of keystrokes in rapid succession
interaction_model.state_change: Multiple key responses overlap in time instead of replacing one another
interaction_model.affected_object: Per-keystroke key motion and click feedback

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Recovery is automatic and unannounced; the visitor never has to click anything to resume writing
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Continued typing keeps landing on the sheet, so no keystroke is silently swallowed
interaction_model.input: Typing focus lost by any incidental means
interaction_model.state_change: Focus returns on its own without user action
interaction_model.affected_object: The typing target of the whole view

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Writing is never hidden behind the surface edge; new input always appears somewhere visible
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The current line and the point where new characters land remain in view as earlier lines move out of sight
interaction_model.input: Wording exceeding the visible sheet
interaction_model.state_change: The view follows the writing position
interaction_model.affected_object: Visible region of the paper surface

Depicted keyboard layout, key shapes and how many keys are shown

Typography, line spacing and sheet proportions
Easing and travel distance of the key dip and the line advance
How earlier lines leave the visible area as writing continues
canonical_document.description: A sheet of paper fills the focus while text lands on it character by character, and the solid machine body pictured just below dips its matching key with a short click on every keystroke, with a heavier carriage sound when a new line begins.
experience_progression: Open state: empty sheet with the faint prompt in the future text position and the short invitation visible; no preparation or click is required
First keystroke: the faint prompt gives way to real text and the machine begins responding in step
Accumulation: wording builds line by line on the sheet, with the tally quietly rising

Full-surface state: writing continues while the view keeps the current writing position and freshest line visible
Open-ended continuation: no completion stage, no saving, no closing sequence

name: tunable_liquid_pool_sandbox
description: A square walled pool of liquid that is already sloshing when you arrive; holding the pointer shows a soft reach ring and gathers liquid toward it, dropped rectangular and round solids can be carried around while liquid shoves aside and swirls past them, and property adjusters reshape the flow instantly without restarting it.

experience_qualities: Immediate, believable cause and effect for every touch and every control
Alive on arrival, self-explanatory without instructions
Tactile and direct: the pointer feels like it is reaching into the liquid
Comparative and experimental, inviting one-property-at-a-time observation
Continuous and unfinished, with no goal or score
Reassuringly contained: the liquid is energetic yet never escapes the pool
locked_observable_requirements: Liquid is already in motion and settling at first view, with no start step or instruction
All motion stays visibly inside one bounded square pool; liquid and solids never cross its walls
Press-and-hold shows the pull's reach as a soft ring at the pointer and gathers nearby liquid toward that spot
The pull tracks the pointer continuously and stops the instant the press ends or the pointer leaves the pool
Two kinds of solid, rectangular and round, can be dropped into the middle and later cleared all at once
A held solid follows the pointer while remaining fully inside the pool, with liquid visibly shoved aside and swirling around it
The liquid pull is suppressed while a solid is held
Every property adjustment takes visible hold immediately on the liquid already in motion, never by restarting it
Freezing preserves the current arrangement exactly and resuming continues from it
Resetting scatters a fresh batch and returns to the arrival impression
A constant, non-intrusive sense of whether the motion is keeping up remains available
canonical_document.name: tunable_liquid_pool_sandbox
canonical_document.experience_scope: A bounded region experience: one square pool stage plus an adjacent persistent control surface. It begins already in motion at first view with no start action, runs indefinitely, and has no end state; freezing and resetting are states within it rather than exits.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any bounded interactive-matter region where the visible medium is a contained flowing, deformable mass with a small set of live properties and pointer-scale manipulation: physics toys, hands-on explanatory demos of tunable behaviour, playful focal regions beside short copy. It stays the same Skill across different droplet rendering, host palettes, control ranges and layout placement. It becomes a different Skill if the mass becomes an unbounded full-page medium flowing behind foreground content, if live tuning is removed so only pointer play remains, if the flowing mass is replaced by discrete rigid objects with no continuous medium, if the pull becomes a purely decorative cursor ornament with no contained volume responding, or if objectives and scoring turn it into gameplay.
content_and_composition: One primary stage: a square pool with visible bounding walls that fully contain the liquid; nothing ever leaves it
One cohesive mass of many small liquid droplets read as a single body that piles, slumps, splashes against walls and settles
One transient soft ring centred on the pointer while a press is held, sized to show how far the pull reaches
Zero to several solid bodies inside the pool, of two shape kinds (rectangular and round), each floating, resting or being carried, always within the walls

One persistent control surface adjacent to the pool holding continuous property adjusters (gravity strength, gravity direction, runniness, resistance to squeezing, neighbour reach, pull strength, amount of liquid) and discrete actions (drop rectangular solid, drop round solid, clear solids, freeze/resume, reset)
One small persistent indication of whether the motion is still keeping up, placed so it never competes with the pool
attention_and_information_flow: On arrival the moving liquid mass alone carries attention; the control surface reads as secondary until touched
During a press, attention narrows to the pointer: the ring declares the pull's reach and the converging liquid confirms it
Solids create local focal points, with the swirl and displacement around them showing more than the solid itself does
While comparing properties the control surface becomes the active object and the pool becomes the read-out; the changed quality of motion is the revealed information
Freezing shifts attention from motion to fine spatial detail of the arrangement
Prominence never leaves the pool for long; every control action is answered inside the pool

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Ends the instant the press is released or the pointer leaves the pool; the ring disappears and gathered liquid immediately falls and settles again; suppressed entirely while a solid is being held
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A soft ring appears at the pointer showing how far the pull carries, and nearby droplets stream and bunch toward that spot while distant liquid keeps behaving normally
interaction_model.input: Press and hold anywhere inside the pool
interaction_model.state_change: Attraction becomes active at the pointer with a defined reach
interaction_model.affected_object: Liquid near the press point, plus the pull-reach ring

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Reversible by moving back; crossing the pool edge cancels the pull rather than dragging liquid outside
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The ring follows the pointer and the gathered liquid is dragged along, trailing and smearing behind the moving centre
interaction_model.input: Move the pointer while the press is held
interaction_model.state_change: Pull centre tracks the pointer continuously
interaction_model.affected_object: Attraction centre and the gathered liquid

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Repeatable to accumulate several solids; undone collectively by the clear action
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Liquid is pushed away from the arrival point and then flows and settles around the new shape
interaction_model.input: Discrete action to drop a rectangular or a round solid
interaction_model.state_change: A new solid of the chosen shape enters at the middle of the pool
interaction_model.affected_object: Pool contents

name: angled_seat_ring_shared_play_surface
description: Personal seat panels arranged around the rim of one shared central board, each rotated to face the person on that side; the seat holding the turn pulses and is the only one that accepts presses, private cards appear only while a peek control is held, committed amounts visibly leave seats and grow a central pool, and each round ends with a plain verdict that rolls into the next deal by itself.

experience_qualities: Physical, tabletop feel: content belongs to sides of a surface rather than to the top of a page
Readable from any seat without anyone having to walk around or rotate the display
Unambiguous turn ownership; nobody has to be told whose move it is
Momentary secrecy on a display everyone can see
Glanceable public state that keeps the round comprehensible mid-action
Calm, self-sustaining rhythm as rounds close and re-open without prompting
Confidence before commitment, since every cost is shown before it is paid
locked_observable_requirements: Personal panels arranged around the rim of one shared central area, each rotated so its content faces the participant on that side.
Exactly one seat visually active at a time, marked by a pulsing treatment, with all other seats inert to input.
A central area readable from every side that shows communal revealed items, an accumulating pool and a climbing stake level.
Private per-seat items concealed by default and visible only while a hold is maintained, re-concealed by a release anywhere on the surface.
Cost shown before commitment: an exact owed amount on the combined confirm control and a previewed total on the incremental assembly, visibly capped by the seat's remaining amount.
Committed amounts visibly leaving the acting seat and appearing in the central pool as the turn passes onward.
One plainly worded round outcome, followed by automatic advance to the next round with an optional one-press skip.
Seats that can be dragged and re-angled to match where people actually sit.
Human-driven and autonomous seats indistinguishable in the ring.
canonical_document.name: angled_seat_ring_shared_play_surface
canonical_document.experience_scope: Whole-view experience on one large shared display. It begins when a short configuration step resolves and the surface takes over the full view, spans an open-ended sequence of rounds, and ends either when one seat holds the entire tracked resource or when the surface is exited back to configuration. The ring of seats, the central board and the round loop form a single composition, not a component embedded in a page.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits co-located group experiences on a single large touch or projected display where each participant needs a personally oriented, privately readable region around shared public state that changes as they act in turn: group games, shared quizzes, workshop voting or allocation boards, tabletop planning and briefing surfaces. It requires one shared display with people positioned on different sides. It becomes a different skill if each participant gets their own device (per-side rotation and hold-to-peek secrecy lose their purpose), if the ring is replaced by a conventional single-orientation stacked layout, if all participants act simultaneously instead of one at a time, or if the experience terminates on a static result instead of looping into the next round.
content_and_composition: One persistent central area carrying communal revealed items, an accumulating pooled amount and a climbing stake level, all sized to be read from any side of the display.
A configurable number of personal seat panels distributed around the rim of the central area, each rotated so its labels, amounts and items face outward toward the person on that side.

Each seat panel shows an identifying label, its remaining amount, the amount it has committed in the current round, its two shielded private items, and a visible marker when it has dropped out of the round.

An action cluster attached to the seat that holds the turn: a withdraw control, a single combined confirm control that states the exact amount currently owed, and an incremental raise assembly that previews the resulting total.
A hold-to-peek control inside each seat panel that keeps private items concealed by default.
A transient outcome banner near the centre naming the winning seat, the amount and the winning combination, accompanied by an advance countdown that can be skipped.
Seats driven by people and seats driven autonomously look identical in the ring; only their source of input differs.
attention_and_information_flow: Exactly one seat is visually alive at a time through a pulsing treatment, so attention lands on the panel that owes an action without any instruction or arrow.
The central area is the constant reference point: the pool grows, the stake level climbs and communal items accumulate, all glanceable mid-round from every side.

Cost information surfaces at the moment of decision rather than in advance: the combined confirm control states the exact amount owed and the incremental assembly previews the resulting total before anything is committed.
Private items stay concealed by default and are revealed only for as long as a hold is maintained, so a display everyone can see never leaks a seat's private holding.
At round close attention moves inward from the ring to a single centred verdict, then back outward as the next round deals and the pulse returns to a seat.
Each seat's own numbers are legible only in its own orientation, keeping personal detail local while public state stays universal.

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Committed on press; the stated amount on the control is the safeguard, since the cost is always visible before the press. When nothing is owed the same control reads and behaves as a pass.

interaction_model.affected_object: The round loop

canonical_document.description: Personal seat panels arranged around the rim of one shared central board, each rotated to face the person on that side; the seat holding the turn pulses and is the only one that accepts presses, private cards appear only while a peek control is held, committed amounts visibly leave seats and grow a central pool, and each round ends with a plain verdict that rolls into the next deal by itself.
experience_progression: Configuration resolves and the surface takes over the whole view with seats seeded around the ring.
A round opens: private items are dealt to each seat, forced stakes are deducted from the seats that owe them, and the turn is handed to the first seat.

name: keystroke_driven_actor_placement_challenge
description: A lesson panel beside a quiet, low-distraction stage where a handful of high-contrast characters glide into new arrangements on every keystroke typed into one highlighted slot of a small code snippet, aiming to land on faint pre-marked spots, with a check mark and confetti burst confirming a correct set and unlocking the next round.

experience_qualities: Immediate, continuous cause and effect between text and spatial arrangement
Forgiving: wrong attempts read as movement and exploration, never as punishment
Instantly legible goal because the destination is drawn before the attempt
Playful and toy-like handling of a technical idea
Gently escalating challenge with an unchanging interaction pattern
Unmistakably celebratory success beat, brief and non-blocking
Calm, low-distraction stage surround that lets the moving actors read as the most salient things in view
locked_observable_requirements: Target positions are visible as faint pre-placed shapes on the stage before any input is given.
Exactly one highlighted editable slot exists inside an otherwise fixed snippet.
Every keystroke re-arranges the actors with visible motion; there is no submit step and no error state for partial or wrong entries.
Matching is tolerant of token order and extra spacing.
Success is confirmed by all three signals together: a matched status label, a check mark, and a transient celebratory burst over the stage.
Forward advancing is gated on a match while backward stepping is ungated.
A restore-to-starting-text action is available at any time within a round.
Lesson title, explanation and one objective sit beside the stage, never overlaying it.
The stage surround is quiet and uniform, actors read as clearly separated high-contrast foreground against it, and ghost targets sit on a lower layer at reduced emphasis so overlap reads as landing.
Difficulty rises from one idea to combined rules across rounds, and the final round resolves into a short congratulatory close with a restart to the first round.
canonical_document.name: keystroke_driven_actor_placement_challenge
canonical_document.experience_scope: A self-contained region occupying one full view or one full-width page section: it begins when a round loads its lesson, snippet and stage, continues per round through typing and confirmation, and ends at a brief congratulatory closing state after the final round that can restart the whole sequence.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any short-text-to-spatial-arrangement lesson or puzzle where a small set of visible objects must land on a small set of visibly marked destinations and the correct answer is a compact set of tokens; it also fits non-code notations as long as the entry stays short enough to retype freely. It stops fitting when the correct outcome cannot be shown spatially in advance, when the output is free-form or unbounded, or when many objects make individual arrival unreadable. Replacing per-keystroke rearrangement with submit-then-check evaluation, introducing error styling for partial entries, hiding the target positions until after success, or dissolving the discrete objective-per-round structure into an open sandbox each produce a different Skill.
content_and_composition: One lesson block per round, placed beside (not over) the stage: a short title, a plain-language explanation, and exactly one concrete objective sentence.
One compact code/markup snippet in the lesson side containing exactly one visually highlighted editable slot; the surrounding snippet text is fixed, quiet context.
One stage panel opposite the lesson, its surround uniform and low-emphasis, containing a small set of movable actors (one to several) rendered in strong contrast against that surround.
Faint ghost target shapes pre-placed on the stage at the round's solution positions, held at lower emphasis than the actors and on a layer beneath them so an actor covering a target reads as arrival.
Persistent controls: step-forward and step-backward round navigation, a restore-entry action, and an advance affordance that is inert until the round is solved.
A compact status area adjacent to the entry showing an unsolved/matched label and a check mark on success.
A transient celebratory particle burst layer above the stage, present only at the moment of a correct match.
attention_and_information_flow: Before any input, the faint pre-placed targets make the goal legible at a glance, so the stage reads as a solvable puzzle rather than a static illustration.
The highlighted slot is the only accented, live-looking element in the snippet, so the place to act is unambiguous.
While typing, the moving actors dominate attention; intermediate, partial or wrong entries produce intermediate positions and no error styling, so nothing reads as failure.
On a match, prominence shifts briefly to the status label, check mark and celebration burst, then settles on the now-active advance affordance.
Progression information stays minimal: the current objective and round position, never a scoreboard or penalty display.
The closing state drops lesson and puzzle emphasis in favor of one short congratulatory message and the replay path.

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Editing is always open; deleting characters moves actors back, and the restore action returns the slot and the arrangement to the round's opening state
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Actors glide and settle into new positions in step with typing; unrecognized or partial input simply leaves them in an intermediate arrangement with no error color, message or shake
interaction_model.input: Typing or editing text in the highlighted slot, evaluated on every keystroke
interaction_model.state_change: The actor arrangement is recomputed continuously as the entry text changes, including for incomplete or incorrect entries
interaction_model.affected_object: The movable actors on the stage

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The solved state can be left by editing again; the celebration is a single non-blocking burst that does not have to be dismissed
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A matched status label and check mark appear beside the entry, a one-shot confetti burst fires over the stage, and the actors rest exactly on their ghost targets
interaction_model.input: The entered token set matching the round's target, with extra spacing and different word order still counting as correct
interaction_model.state_change: The round becomes solved and forward advancing unlocks
interaction_model.affected_object: Status area, stage and advance affordance

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Available at any time, before or after a match, without leaving the current round
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The slot content resets and the actors animate back to their opening arrangement while the ghost targets stay put
interaction_model.input: Restore-entry action
interaction_model.state_change: The slot text reverts to the round's starting text
interaction_model.affected_object: The editable slot and the actors

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Forward stepping stays inert until the current round is matched; backward stepping is always allowed so any earlier round can be replayed
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A new title, explanation and objective appear, the snippet reloads with a fresh highlighted slot at its starting text, and the stage shows a new actor and ghost-target arrangement
interaction_model.input: Step-forward and step-backward round controls
interaction_model.state_change: The active round changes in either direction
interaction_model.affected_object: The whole region: lesson block, snippet and stage

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Restart is repeatable; the sequence can be run through again from the beginning any number of times
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The congratulatory message gives way to the first lesson, snippet and stage in their opening condition
interaction_model.input: Replay action in the closing state
interaction_model.state_change: The sequence returns to the first round
interaction_model.affected_object: The whole region

Exact palette and overall light or dark treatment, as long as the stage surround stays low-emphasis and the actors keep clear contrast and separation against it

canonical_document.description: A lesson panel beside a quiet, low-distraction stage where a handful of high-contrast characters glide into new arrangements on every keystroke typed into one highlighted slot of a small code snippet, aiming to land on faint pre-marked spots, with a check mark and confetti burst confirming a correct set and unlocking the next round.
experience_progression: Opening rounds present one single arrangement idea with the fewest actors, so a one-token answer is enough.
Later rounds add actors and combine several rules in a single objective, raising difficulty gradually while the interaction stays identical.
Within each round: read the objective, see the ghost targets, type, watch actors continuously rearrange, reach a match, then advance.
After the final round the region resolves into a brief congratulatory closing state instead of another lesson.
The closing state offers a restart that returns to the first round.
completion_and_return: Each round completes on a token-set match, marked simultaneously by status label, check mark, confetti burst and the unlocked advance affordance.
Completing the final round leads to a brief congratulatory closing state rather than a further lesson.
The closing state restarts the sequence from the first round.
Backward stepping keeps every earlier round available for another attempt.
Restore resets only the current round's entry and arrangement, leaving the round position intact.

name: seat_oriented_turn_spotlight_board
description: A full-bleed board split into bold zones, one per person, each with its own clearly separable identity fill and rotated to read upright from that person's seat; tapping a zone hands the turn over so it brightens and its large running total begins advancing while every other zone dims, a small marker slides across to the live zone, and a hub at the center expands to reveal hold and clear-all controls.

experience_qualities: Bold, poster-scale and high contrast, readable from across a table and from any side of the screen
One unmistakable focal point at all times, so the current turn needs no verbal announcement
Hand-off feels immediate and physical: touch a zone, that zone lights up, the marker follows
Calm ambient counting between hand-offs rather than urgency or alarm
Controls feel tucked away and deliberate, with the destructive one kept behind the hub
Forgiving and obvious: stopping, resuming and starting over all read as single visible steps
locked_observable_requirements: The viewport is fully partitioned into one zone per participant, edge to edge, with no surrounding page chrome
Each zone's text is oriented to read upright from that participant's own side of the screen
Zones are distinguished by one strong, persistent per-person identity fill each, unmistakably separable from every neighbouring zone whatever palette is used
Exactly one zone is live at a time: it is visibly brightened while all others are visibly dimmed
Only the live zone's total advances; every other total visibly holds still
Each zone shows one large accumulating total legible from a distance
A single discrete marker visibly travels to sit beside the live zone on every hand-off
Tapping a zone is the hand-off gesture, and the very first tap also starts timing from the idle state

All session controls live in one compact center hub that expands in place: hold freezes every total exactly, continue resumes from those values, clear-all zeroes every total and returns the turn to the first seat
A label can be retyped in place without transferring the turn or interrupting the advancing total
canonical_document.name: seat_oriented_turn_spotlight_board
canonical_document.experience_scope: Whole-view experience filling the entire viewport with no surrounding page chrome. It begins on first view with all zones idle and equal, continues indefinitely through hand-offs, holds and resumes across interruptions, and ends only when totals are cleared back to the opening state. The expanding control hub is an in-place overlay at the shared center of the same view, not a separate screen.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits a small set of co-present peers sharing one physical screen where exactly one of them is active at a time and each needs an equally weighted, own-side readable panel with a continuously accumulating measure: turn taking, speaking or debate order, round-based play, station or shift rotation, shared-table scorekeeping. It stops being this skill if each participant gets their own device or remote view (per-seat orientation loses its purpose), if the participant count grows large enough that zones can no longer be read from a seat, if the layout becomes a scrolling or ranked list instead of a full-bleed partition, if more than one participant can be live simultaneously, or if the measure counts down toward expiry so urgency and elimination states rather than a single calm spotlight define the experience.
content_and_composition: A small set of participant zones (typically two to six) tiling the full viewport edge to edge, with no leftover margin, header or navigation around them
Each zone carries one distinct high-separation identity fill of its own, one editable person label and one large accumulating time total
All text inside a zone is oriented to face outward toward that zone's own side of the screen, so opposite zones read upside-down relative to each other and upright relative to their own viewer
Exactly one zone is in the live state at a time; all remaining zones sit in a visibly receded state
One small discrete marker that always sits adjacent to the live zone and travels between zones
One compact control hub anchored at the shared center where zones meet, collapsed by default and expanding in place to reveal hold/continue and clear-all
Persistent across the whole session: the zone partition, per-zone identity fills, labels, per-zone totals, the marker and the hub
attention_and_information_flow: Only one zone is bright at any moment, so the eye lands on the live participant immediately without anyone announcing the turn
Non-live zones drop in prominence but keep their totals readable, so standings remain scannable while never competing with the live zone
The marker's slide gives a second, motion-based read of the hand-off that is legible even at a shallow viewing angle where brightness differences are hard to judge
Totals are sized for reading across the whole surface rather than at arm's length, making each person's accumulated amount ambient information
Controls stay visually subordinate while collapsed and briefly take the center of attention while expanded, then recede again

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Any zone can be tapped at any time to hand off again; tapping the already-live zone changes nothing; no accumulated amount is lost on hand-off because each zone keeps its own running total
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The tapped zone brightens, the previous zone dims, the marker slides across to sit beside the new live zone, and the newly live total starts visibly ticking upward
interaction_model.input: Tap or click anywhere inside a participant zone

name: layered_window_workspace_shell
description: A familiar desktop-style workspace: wallpaper with a few items on it, a thin overhead strip that names whatever is frontmost, a bottom row of launcher icons, and content opening as overlapping panes with exactly one clearly in front.

Direct manipulation: everything is grabbed, dragged, lifted or dismissed rather than navigated to
Legible layered depth with an unambiguous front
Persistent and forgiving — nothing is destroyed by rearranging, and leaving does not lose the arrangement
Playful and exploratory, rewarding poking around

Overhead menu contents change to match whichever pane is frontmost.
Launcher icons show running state and toggle their pane open and closed.
Panes are moved by their top bar and resized from edges and corners, with a visible minimum size floor.
A maximize toggle fills the view and restores the exact previous size and position.
Closing a pane hands focus to the next one in line.
Right-click raises a contextual list at the pointer for the wallpaper, a launcher icon and a pane bar, dismissible by escape or an outside click.
Sign-out returns to the entry threshold and the workspace is later restored as it was left.

Very small touch viewports where dragging and edge-resizing are impractical fall outside this skill's boundary.

name: cascading_panel_desk
description: A bare full-view desk that wakes after a brief startup pause, where opening a small program spawns a fresh panel stepped down from the last; panels drag by their bar, stretch from their bottom-right corner down to a usable minimum, rise to the front with a visible in-use marking when touched, and close from a small box in the bar, while everything left open stays visible but quiet and the whole desk returns exactly as it was left.

Directly manipulable and tactile: things are grabbed, moved, stretched and pushed forward by hand

Exploratory and toy-like: the interface invites trying things without consequence
Continuously legible layering — busy without ever hiding what is still open
Never lossy: nothing is filed away, submitted or discarded behind the visitor's back
A sense of a persistent private space that is waiting rather than being re-created

canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits whole views whose foreground content is a small set of discrete, self-contained working areas that benefit from being open simultaneously and handled directly, each of low-to-moderate density, in contexts where the interface's own character is welcome. It is a foreground environment and cannot act as a visual substrate behind other page content. Reducing it to a single fixed full-view layout, a modal one-at-a-time flow, or a flow that requires explicit saving or submitting would make it a different skill; so would scaling to dozens of simultaneously important panels, long scrolling documents that outgrow a movable frame, or hiding inactive work instead of keeping it visible and quiet.

Each newly opened panel placed at a small constant offset from the previously opened one, so multiple panels read as a stepped cascade rather than a pile
Panel content roles observed here: a row listing of containers and documents with a step-out entry for the enclosing level, and a plain editable text surface for a single document

name: gated_lane_pass_reject_flow

name: retro_command_console_session_log
description: A cryptic retro console that opens with a short banner pointing at one word that lists everything it understands; every typed line is echoed with a prompt marker and answered directly beneath, heavier requests unfold through ordered intermediate stages behind a spinning busy marker before a single final outcome line lands, and other single words wipe the log back to its banner, drop an animated diagram inline, or toggle a falling-character backdrop — all of it monospaced and held to one narrow tonal range at readable contrast, whatever tones the host surface supplies.

Entirely self-explaining: the surface teaches its own vocabulary from the first line
Forgiving and low-stakes: any wrong entry costs one line and an instant retry
Toy-like and playful, with joking and hidden responses rewarding experimentation
locked_observable_requirements: A single continuous downward-growing log with the newest output always in sight and a persistent entry line at the bottom
An opening banner that itself points at the one word revealing the full vocabulary, with no explanation outside the surface
Every submission echoed with a prompt marker and answered directly beneath its echo
Heavier requests reveal ordered intermediate stages before a single final outcome line
While a request is underway the entry line accepts nothing and a spinning busy marker sits below the log
Unrecognized entries produce exactly one brief notice quoting the entry verbatim, with the caret already back for a retry
Blank submissions produce no output whatsoever
A word that wipes the log back to its banner state
An animated diagram that appears inline in the log flow rather than in a separate panel or overlay
A toggleable falling-character backdrop behind the log, each toggle acknowledged by a short confirmation line
Monospaced retro treatment kept within one narrow tonal range at readable contrast against its surround, plus unhurried pacing, shared across all output roles
At least one joking refusal so the session can never be ended from inside

canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any surface where a visitor drives short textual requests and reads machine-like replies from one growing log: playful toy machines, easter-egg consoles, guided product demos, oracle or quiz toys, and command-word exploration of a small body of facts, links or examples — provided replies stay short text with occasional inline animated blocks and the vocabulary is small enough to be listed by a single word. Turning it into free-form conversational dialogue with no fixed vocabulary, splitting output into windows or side panels, making continuous graphics rather than text the primary content, or backing it with a real shell and a genuine exit would create a different Skill. Dropping the staged reveal and the locked-input busy state would reduce it to a plain scrolling text log rather than this experience.

name: live_gadget_shell_carousel
description: A row of faux handheld gadgets in which only the centered one is lit and responsive; its miniature screen is driven by the gadget's own wheel and buttons, drilling from a collection down to one item that takes over the screen, and the running session survives gliding to a different gadget.

experience_qualities: Tactile and mechanical: movement happens in discrete notches and hard stops rather than as free glide
Nostalgic, object-like intimacy from a dense miniature screen inside a physical-looking shell
A hushed periphery around one unmistakably live focus
Progressive narrowing that feels like tunnelling from many things to one thing
Uninterrupted continuity: the session outlives level changes and unit swaps

Endless lateral browsing with no edges to hit

Backing out always restores the originating row as the highlight

canonical_document.name: live_gadget_shell_carousel
canonical_document.experience_scope: A single stage-sized region (typically the whole main view) containing the shell row and its controls. It begins already at rest with one unit centered, awake and its screen showing the top-level list, and it has no terminal state: level changes, item playback and lateral steps all happen inside the same region, and the running session persists across every step.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits small curated collections with a two-to-three level hierarchy ending in a single continuously running or timed item — audio-like streams, video, timed slideshows, episodic readings — presented as the main stage of a page. It needs at least three shell variants for the row to read as a collection, and an item type whose run state can persist while the shell around it changes. It becomes a different skill if several units are live at once, if the highlight moves freely instead of notch by notch, if list ends wrap instead of stopping dead, if each unit holds its own session that restarts on swap, or if the on-shell control cluster is replaced by ordinary page controls outside the device.
content_and_composition: One horizontal row of at least three comparable device shells; exactly one sits in a centered focus slot at full fidelity and illumination, the others sit offset, visually muted and reduced to showing only their model label.
Each shell carries two parts: a small embedded screen area and a cluster of physical-looking controls (a circular wheel or ring, a center confirm key, a back/out key, and two skip keys).
A persistent pair of step arrows below the row, outside the shells, as the only lateral control.
Inside the active screen: a level title plus a short list of rows with exactly one row highlighted at a time.
At the deepest level the screen is replaced by a single-item takeover view: an artwork block, the item title and its running time, with a transport state icon.
A transient level readout overlay that appears over the item view during continuous adjustment and dismisses itself.
Persistent across everything: the shell row, the step arrows, the muted model labels, and the currently playing item with its state.
attention_and_information_flow: Only the centered unit reads as alive; the brightness, scale and detail gap makes neighbours read as inert props identified by name alone.
Attention narrows step by step as depth increases: many small rows, then fewer rows, then one item occupying the entire screen with large artwork and only two or three fields.
During the lateral glide, prominence moves to the travelling row itself; the screen stops being an input target, so nothing competes for the user's action.
Feedback overlays (state icon flip, level readout) briefly claim the screen and then release it without changing the current level or view.
Backing out restores the previous information density and re-points attention at the exact row the user came from.

name: wired_block_board_with_run_reveal
description: An open board where blocks dragged from a grouped side catalogue are joined by pointer-pulled wires into a left-to-right chain, then evaluated by one run that shows each block's result on the block.

experience_qualities: Legible: the arrangement reads as a left-to-right flow that makes a small calculation self-explanatory.
Hands-on and physical: pieces are grasped, dragged and tethered, and wires behave like flexible attachments.
Approachable before commitment: block roles are distinguishable in the catalogue before anything is placed.
Deliberate rather than continuously recomputing: outcome appears because the person asked for it.
Forgiving: half-made connections can be abandoned with no consequence.
Plain-spoken: confirmation and failure are stated in ordinary wording.
locked_observable_requirements: An empty working surface paired with a persistent catalogue whose grouping distinguishes value-supplying from value-consuming pieces before use.
Pieces are placed from the catalogue onto free space and repositioned by grasping a dedicated strip on the piece.
Connections are made by pulling a live wire that trails the pointer from an output socket and commits only when released over an input socket.
Releasing or clicking empty surface abandons a connection attempt with no change.
Each input socket carries at most one incoming connection, and a new connection replaces the previous feed.
Wires stay visibly anchored to their sockets while pieces move.
Removing a piece removes its connections, leaving no dangling ends.
One deliberate run holds a visible busy state until it finishes and then reveals results on the pieces that display them, not in a separate output area.
Failure is communicated in plain wording without discarding the assembly.
A reset returns the surface to empty.
canonical_document.name: wired_block_board_with_run_reveal
canonical_document.experience_scope: A region experience covering the paired catalogue rail and working board; it begins on arrival with an empty board and ends either at a run whose results are shown in place or at a reset back to empty. The rest of the page is unaffected.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any foreground region where a visitor composes a small readable chain of discrete labelled units from a catalogue and then evaluates it on demand, such as step chains, transformation pipelines, filter or signal chains, and rule or automation assemblies; it suits low-to-moderate density where the whole chain is meant to be understood at a glance. Removing the deliberate run in favour of continuous automatic recomputation, moving outcomes out of the units into a separate result panel, allowing multiple feeds per input or free-form arrows drawn without sockets, or reducing the surface to a non-editable diagram would each create a different Skill.
content_and_composition: Two persistent side-by-side regions: a narrow catalogue rail of available block entries and a large open working board.
Catalogue entries are organised into groups that make clear which blocks supply values and which consume them, readable before anything is placed.

Each placed block is a small self-contained card with a title strip used for grasping, its own inline editable content (a field, toggle or choice), one or more input sockets on the incoming edge and an output socket on the outgoing edge.
Blocks that display a result carry an in-card readout area that is empty until a run happens.
Wires form a layer connecting output sockets to input sockets, anchored at both ends; each input socket holds at most one incoming wire.
A transient live wire exists only during a connection attempt, trailing the pointer from its origin socket.
Persistent run and reset affordances, plus a brief status line used for run confirmation or plain-worded invalid-assembly messaging.
attention_and_information_flow: While the board is empty, the grouped catalogue carries the most prominence and communicates what is available and how blocks differ in role.
As blocks accumulate, prominence shifts to the board and the shape of the chain becomes the primary information.
During a connection attempt the moving live wire is the single most salient element, and the sockets it could land on become the meaningful targets.
While a block is being repositioned, the block and its continuously re-aimed wires dominate attention over static neighbours.
During evaluation, a visible busy state holds attention; afterwards the newly revealed per-block results become the freshest information, read along the same left-to-right path as the wiring.
Invalid assemblies redirect attention to a plainly worded explanation rather than to a result.

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Placement never lands on top of existing blocks; an unwanted block can be removed, which also clears any wires it gained
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The block appears on open board space with its title strip, editable content, sockets and empty result area; the catalogue stays in place

interaction_model.affected_object: The working board and a new block instance

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Releasing leaves the block where it was dropped; any position on the board is acceptable, and connections are never altered by moving
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The block follows the pointer and its wires bend and stretch continuously, remaining visibly locked to the sockets they connect
interaction_model.input: Pressing a block's title strip and moving the pointer
interaction_model.state_change: The block moves with the pointer while each attached wire keeps its ends on their sockets
interaction_model.affected_object: That block's position and every wire attached to it

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Releasing over an input socket commits the connection; releasing or clicking on empty board space abandons the attempt, the live wire disappears and nothing changes
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A wire trails from the origin socket to the pointer, showing the connection being considered
interaction_model.input: Pressing an output socket and dragging
interaction_model.state_change: A live wire is pulled from the origin socket and follows the pointer until release
interaction_model.affected_object: A pending connection between sockets

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The replaced connection can be re-made by pulling a new wire; the socket is never left with two competing feeds

interaction_model.input: Releasing a live wire over an input socket that already has a feed
interaction_model.state_change: The new connection replaces whatever previously fed that socket
interaction_model.affected_object: The wire layer at that input socket

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Values can be changed again at any time; editing does not disturb the surrounding assembly or require re-wiring
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The block shows its new value immediately while its wiring and position stay unchanged
interaction_model.input: Editing a block's own field, toggle or choice
interaction_model.state_change: The value updates in place on the block
interaction_model.affected_object: That block's value
