interaction_model.input: Removing a block
interaction_model.state_change: The block and its connections leave the board together
interaction_model.affected_object: The block and every wire attached to it

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: If the assembly cannot be evaluated, plain wording explains the problem and the board is left intact and editable; the run can be triggered again after any edit
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The board stays visibly busy until evaluation completes, then each displaying block reveals its current result in place with a brief confirmation of what just happened
interaction_model.input: Triggering the run action
interaction_model.state_change: The assembly is evaluated once and moves from busy to finished
interaction_model.affected_object: The whole assembly and each block's result area

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Reset is the deliberate way back to a clean start; the catalogue is always available to rebuild
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The board returns to its empty arrival state while the catalogue remains unchanged
interaction_model.input: Triggering reset
interaction_model.state_change: All blocks and wires are cleared
interaction_model.affected_object: The working board

adaptable_details: Visual styling of pieces, sockets and wires, including wire curvature and thickness.
Which side the catalogue sits on and how its groups are labelled.
Number and kinds of piece types and the specific inline controls they expose.
Board dimensions and whether the surface scrolls or pans.
Colour scheme, typography and iconography.
Placement and labelling of the run and reset affordances and the exact confirmation wording.
How a piece is removed and how results are formatted inside a piece.
canonical_document.description: An open board where blocks dragged from a grouped side catalogue are joined by pointer-pulled wires into a left-to-right chain, then evaluated by one run that shows each block's result on the block.
experience_progression: Empty board with catalogue visible, so block roles can be understood before committing.
Blocks are placed onto free board space and repositioned into a rough arrangement.
Sockets are wired so the assembly reads as a left-to-right flow of data.
Block values are adjusted in place; blocks and their wires can be removed.
One deliberate run is triggered and the board stays visibly busy until it finishes.
Results appear on the blocks that display them with a brief confirmation, or plain wording explains why the assembly is invalid.
The assembly persists for further editing and re-running, or a reset returns the board to empty.
completion_and_return: A run completes with results shown on the blocks themselves plus a brief confirmation, ending the busy state.
An invalid assembly completes with plain wording and no results, leaving the board unchanged.
The assembly and its revealed results persist afterwards so it can be edited and run again.
Reset returns the region to the initial empty board while keeping the catalogue intact.

name: arrangeable_drafting_sheet_cards
description: A hairline-ruled sheet with a centred name plate and a few labelled cards, freshly scattered on a first visit, that lift and follow the finger, snap onto line intersections when released, open on a tap, and stay where they were left.

experience_qualities: Measured and instrument-like, as if reading a drawing sheet
Hands-on and tactile — pieces feel physically picked up and put down
Lightly playful, with an implicit invitation to tidy
Loose while moving, exact on release
Quiet and still: nothing moves unless the visitor moves it
Personal, because the arrangement left behind is recognisably the visitor's own
locked_observable_requirements: A visible ruled field whose line intersections are the only resting positions for movable pieces.
One identity plate at the exact centre of the field, fixed and excluded from the movable set.
Cards positioned at varied off-centre spots on a first visit rather than in a regular arrangement.
A held card looks lifted, slightly enlarged and semi-transparent and follows pointer or finger continuously.
Release snaps the card to the nearest intersection and keeps it wholly within the visible field.
A near-static press opens that card's destination in a new tab; a genuine move opens nothing.
Pointing at a card inverts its colours without displacing it.
Stepping through the picture card's images leaves the card's position unchanged.
The last arrangement is still in place on a later visit.
Pointer and touch input produce the same picking-up, snapping and tapping behaviour.
canonical_document.name: arrangeable_drafting_sheet_cards
canonical_document.experience_scope: A whole-view experience filling the visible field. It begins the moment the sheet appears with its cards already placed, continues as an open-ended arranging state with no end point, and hands off only when a card is pressed and its destination opens in a separate tab, leaving the sheet and its arrangement intact behind.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any single-screen view carrying a handful of short, self-contained pieces that each stand for one destination or one small item — profile and contact sets, compact project indexes, curated link boards, small note or credit collections — with at most one image-bearing piece among them. It depends on the piece count staying low enough that free placement never crowds the field, and on each piece reading meaningfully in isolation. Replacing free placement with an automatic or responsive layout, removing the ruled field so releases have nothing to align to, allowing the field to scroll or exceed one screen, or turning the pieces into long-form or scrolling content instead of compact plates produces a different skill.
content_and_composition: One full-bleed substrate layer: an evenly measured field of hairlines whose crossings form visible intersections that act as the only resting anchors for movable pieces.
One identity plate pinned to the exact centre of the field, carrying a name and a short role line; persistent, precisely placed and never movable.
A small set of labelled cards, roughly three to six, layered above the sheet: compact plates each carrying a short label and standing for one outbound destination.
Exactly one card in the set is a picture card holding a photograph plus two small step arrows; the remaining cards are label-only.
Cards sit at slightly different off-centre positions on each first visit, scattered around the centre plate rather than aligned into a row, column or grid block.
While held, a card rises above its siblings; at rest all cards sit flat on the sheet at the same level.
attention_and_information_flow: The centred plate holds first attention as the only exactly-positioned element; the off-centre cards read as secondary and unsettled, which is what draws handling.
While a card is held it becomes the most prominent object — raised, slightly larger and see-through so the hairlines read through it — and the rest of the set recedes.
Pointing at any card inverts its colours, making the currently addressed piece unmistakable without displacing anything.
The picture card carries the only image content and so anchors the scattered set visually; stepping its pictures changes what it shows while its place and prominence stay constant.
On release, prominence collapses back to the flat sheet and the newly aligned card reads as settled and measured.

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Releasing anywhere ends the move cleanly and no card is ever left stuck in the held look; movement toward an edge is held so the card stays entirely inside the visible field rather than being cut off
interaction_model.visible_feedback: It lifts, scales up slightly and turns semi-transparent so the ruled lines read through it, and it tracks the pointer or finger continuously
interaction_model.input: Press and hold a card with pointer or finger, then move
interaction_model.state_change: The card enters a held, moving state and is raised above the other cards
interaction_model.affected_object: The pressed card

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The committed position becomes the card's resting place and survives leaving and re-entering the view; another drag is how it is changed or undone
interaction_model.visible_feedback: It settles onto that intersection, returning to normal size and full opacity, now aligned to the sheet
interaction_model.input: Release after a genuine move
interaction_model.state_change: The card leaves the held state and commits to the nearest line intersection, fully inside the field
interaction_model.affected_object: The held card

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Any genuine movement during the press cancels this outcome, so a real drag never opens anything
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The card stays exactly where it was and its destination opens in a new tab, with the sheet still visible behind
interaction_model.input: Press and release a card with almost no movement
interaction_model.state_change: The press resolves as a tap rather than a move
interaction_model.affected_object: That card's destination

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Moving away restores the normal colours; the inversion never moves, resizes or reorders the card
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Its foreground and background swap, so it reads as a negative of itself against the sheet
interaction_model.input: Point at or hover any card
interaction_model.state_change: The card switches to an inverted colour state
interaction_model.affected_object: The pointed card's surface

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Stepping is repeatable in both directions and must never begin a move or open the card's destination
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A different photograph appears in the same frame while the card's position, size and alignment stay untouched
interaction_model.input: Press one of the two small arrows on the picture card
interaction_model.state_change: The card steps one picture backwards or forwards through its set
interaction_model.affected_object: The photograph shown inside that card

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: With no remembered arrangement, the cards are scattered freshly at varied spots around the centre plate
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The sheet appears with the visitor's own arrangement already in place
interaction_model.input: Returning to the view later (autonomous driver: the arrangement left behind)
interaction_model.state_change: Cards restore their last committed positions instead of being scattered again
interaction_model.affected_object: The whole card set

adaptable_details: Number of cards and the labels and destinations they carry.
Hairline spacing, colour and line weight of the sheet.
Wording and typographic treatment of the centre plate.
Card size, proportion, corner treatment and label styling.
How many photographs the picture card holds and its aspect ratio.
How much lift, enlargement and transparency the held look applies, and how softly a card settles.
Whether the first-visit scatter is freely varied or drawn from a few prepared placements.
How much movement is tolerated before a press stops counting as a tap.
canonical_document.description: A hairline-ruled sheet with a centred name plate and a few labelled cards, freshly scattered on a first visit, that lift and follow the finger, snap onto line intersections when released, open on a tap, and stay where they were left.
experience_progression: First arrival: sheet and centre plate read as exactly placed and fixed, while the cards read as loose pieces dropped at freshly varied spots — an implicit invitation to tidy.
Arranging: repeated pick-up, move and settle actions gradually turn the scatter into whatever order the visitor prefers, each release adding one aligned piece.
Departure: one card is pressed and followed out to its destination while the arrangement stays on screen.
Return visit: the sheet reopens with the last arrangement already in place, so the scatter stage does not repeat.
completion_and_return: There is no completion state; arranging is open-ended and can be picked up again at any time.
Each individual move completes definitively on release, snapped to an intersection and inside the field.
The arrangement persists as the view's state and is what greets a returning visitor.
Following a card out leaves the sheet and arrangement untouched behind it.
With no remembered arrangement, the view returns to a fresh scatter around the centre plate.

name: spotlit_survival_arena_run
description: An unlit bounded arena where a travelling pool of light is the only readable ground around the figure you steer, hands-off shots pop floating damage figures and burst approaching attackers apart as the crowd thickens, and an emptied health meter hands over to an instant run summary with one-step retry.

experience_qualities: Oppressive, closed-in visibility: the field is known only where the light reaches
Readable rising pressure rather than sudden difficulty jumps
Punchy, tactile impact even though attacking is hands-off
Split attention between the field and a personal status meter
Escalation communicated visually, through a glowing standout rather than text
Brief relief beats from flashing grace windows and orb pickups
Low-friction, immediate retry that keeps momentum after failure
locked_observable_requirements: A short goal-explaining static card precedes any motion on the field
Visibility is restricted to a lit area that travels with the controllable figure; everything beyond it sits far enough from the lit region in luminance that no detail resolves there
Held-key gliding movement in eight directions, with a hard boundary that stops the figure instead of letting it leave
Attacking requires no input and happens on a steady cadence against the nearest target in range
Every hit produces both a floating damage figure and a brief high-salience tint shift on the struck attacker that separates clearly from its normal surface; death produces a burst apart
A persistent draining health meter shares attention with the field throughout the run
Rare glowing heavier attackers are the visible marker of each difficulty step
Health is restored only by walking onto distinct dropped pickup orbs
Contact damage is always followed by a brief flashing invulnerable window on the figure
Run end stops control and immediately shows kills, wave reached and duration with retry one step away, resetting to the opening state
canonical_document.name: spotlit_survival_arena_run
canonical_document.experience_scope: Begins on a static how-to card shown over the arena before anything moves, continues as one uninterrupted real-time scene occupying the whole view (or a full-bleed bounded region), and ends when the health meter empties and a closing summary panel takes over; restart returns to the opening card state. The scene is the foreground content, never a substrate behind reading material.
canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits self-contained, bounded, hands-on real-time foreground scenes where one visitor-steered figure faces autonomous objects converging out of the unreadable surround and the visitor's whole attention belongs inside the scene; the content vocabulary of figure, threats and pickups can be re-themed freely as long as approach-out-of-the-unreadable-surround, hands-off attacking, contact damage with a flashing grace window, and endless stepped escalation remain. It becomes a different Skill if visibility is unrestricted or lighting is static, if attacking requires aiming or triggering input, if runs carry progression forward instead of fully resetting, or if the scene is demoted to a decorative substrate behind reading content.
content_and_composition: One controllable figure that is the constant focal point and carries a lit area with it
One bounded unlit ground plane: only the ground inside the lit area is legible, luminance outside it separates far enough that nothing resolves, and the arena edge behaves as a hard wall
Many autonomous attackers that converge on the figure, resolving out of the unreadable surround as they enter the lit area
A rare heavier attacker variant that reads as glowing among the ordinary crowd
Persistent compact status layer: a draining health meter plus run counters for kills, current wave and elapsed time
Transient effect layer above the field: floating damage figures, tint-shifted struck attackers, death bursts, flashing grace state on the figure
Small distinct pickup orbs occasionally left on the ground where attackers died
Two full-view framing panels: the opening how-to card and the closing summary panel carrying a single restart affordance
attention_and_information_flow: Before the run the how-to card is the only readable content on screen
During the run information exists only inside the travelling lit area; threats become known at the moment they enter it, so the unreadable surround holds unresolved pressure
Glowing heavier attackers pull the eye off the crowd and communicate a difficulty step without any label
Floating damage figures and the struck-target tint shift direct attention to whatever is currently being struck; bursts confirm removal
As health drains, the status meter increasingly competes with the field; the flashing grace state briefly makes the figure the loudest element on screen
At the end all field attention collapses into the summary numbers and the single retry affordance

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Direction can be changed or released at any moment; at the arena edge movement is clamped and the figure stops instead of leaving the field
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The figure slides across the ground while newly lit ground appears ahead and previously lit ground drops back below readability behind
interaction_model.input: Direction keys held down (letter or arrow keys, including two at once for diagonals)
interaction_model.state_change: Continuous glide in one of eight directions while keys are held; motion stops on release
interaction_model.affected_object: The controllable figure and the lit area travelling with it

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Targeting reselects on its own when the current target dies or leaves range; there is nothing to aim, trigger or cancel, so positioning is the only control the player has over it
interaction_model.visible_feedback: A shot resolves onto the nearest target, a damage figure floats up and fades above it, and the target briefly shifts to a high-salience tint
interaction_model.input: Autonomous steady attack cadence, no player input
interaction_model.state_change: That attacker takes a hit on each beat of the cadence
interaction_model.affected_object: Whichever attacker is nearest within range

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Irreversible; a pickup orb may be left behind on the ground where it died
interaction_model.visible_feedback: It bursts apart on the spot and the kill count increments
interaction_model.input: Accumulated hits reaching an attacker's limit
interaction_model.state_change: The attacker is removed from the field
interaction_model.affected_object: That attacker, and the kill counter

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: Orbs stay on the ground until stepped on, so a missed pickup can be collected later by returning to it
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The orb vanishes on contact and the meter refills partway
interaction_model.input: Walking the figure onto a dropped pickup orb
interaction_model.state_change: Orb absorbed, part of the missing health restored
interaction_model.affected_object: The orb and the health meter

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: No further hit can land while flashing, giving a short guaranteed opportunity to steer out of the crowd; the window expires on its own
interaction_model.visible_feedback: The meter drops and the figure flashes for the length of the grace window
interaction_model.input: An attacker touching the figure
interaction_model.state_change: Health is reduced, then a brief invulnerable grace window opens
interaction_model.affected_object: The figure and the health meter

interaction_model.control_and_recovery: The restart on the panel is the single next step and returns everything to the opening state; there is no way to resume the ended run
interaction_model.visible_feedback: Field motion stops and the closing panel presents kills killed, wave reached and run duration
interaction_model.input: Health meter reaching empty
interaction_model.state_change: Run ends and control is released
interaction_model.affected_object: The whole view

adaptable_details: Exact key bindings, movement speed, attack cadence, range, damage values and wave curve
Size of the lit area and the softness of its falloff into the unreadable surround
Silhouettes, hues, surface treatment and art style of figure, attackers, shots and burst fragments, as long as the glowing heavier variant and the pickup stay visually distinct
Whether the shot reads as a travelling projectile or an instantaneous strike
Crowd counts per wave and how many pickups are dropped
Wording, layout and extra counters on the framing panels
Whether the scene fills the viewport or an embedded bounded region
canonical_document.description: An unlit bounded arena where a travelling pool of light is the only readable ground around the figure you steer, hands-off shots pop floating damage figures and burst approaching attackers apart as the crowd thickens, and an emptied health meter hands over to an instant run summary with one-step retry.
experience_progression: Static how-to card: nothing on the field moves, so the goal is readable before any pressure exists
Early run: few attackers, wide readable spacing, full health meter
Stepped escalation across waves: crowd density and closing pressure increase, and each step up is announced visually by glowing heavier attackers rather than by text
Late run: attention splits between the crowd closing on the lit edge and the shrinking health meter, punctuated by flashing grace windows after each contact
Collapse: the meter empties, field motion and control stop
Immediate accounting: kills, wave reached and duration are presented on the closing panel with retry one step away
Restart returns the field, counters, health and difficulty to the opening state; waves are endless, so the loop only ever ends in collapse
completion_and_return: There is no win state; waves continue endlessly and a run ends only by the health meter emptying
Ending immediately accounts for the run with kills, wave reached and elapsed duration on one panel
Restart resets field, crowd, counters, health and difficulty with no carry-over between runs
The how-to card is the resting state before the first run and after each reset

name: rippling_line_field_instrument
description: A quiet full-screen field of evenly spaced crossing lines held at low contrast against a uniform ground, bending away from the moving pointer, sharply gaining luminance separation and thickening while dragging their neighbours into an outward ripple, each disturbed line sounding its own pitch, then springing back through rest into even silence.

experience_qualities: Quiet and minimal on an unobtrusive ground, with a single thing to look at
Alive and answering within seconds of arrival
Feels like playing an instrument rather than operating a tool

canonical_document.experience_scope: A single self-contained region: one device block on the page. canonical_document.portability_boundary: Fits any compact, self-contained interactive scene that benefits from being presented as a small piece of nostalgic hardware with one low-fidelity screen and a couple of physical controls — a page centrepiece, an easter egg, a 404 or waiting area, or a promo block. content_and_composition: One browsing lineup: many peer-level selectable style options placed in a loose, deliberately non-grid scatter, each carrying a short name and a one-line humorous quip so the whole set reads as samplable

The wipe and hold empty the field so attention is fully reset before the stage arrives

Whether the glass material is tinted at all and with which hue if so, plus its highlight treatment and apparent thickness
How far the veil drops in luminance and how much it blurs, and the subject of the calm placeholder still
Exact wording of the invitation, the refusal notice and the capture-failure notice
Placement of the capture action and how the resulting picture is presented or handed over
Whether the pointer-bound shape tracks exactly or lags softly, and how much it swells
Which camera is used and whether the image is mirrored or cropped to fill
canonical_document.description: The live camera image fills the whole screen while a few glossy liquid-glass shapes drift slowly across it and bend whatever is behind them; one shape follows the pointer in real time, swells slightly and fuses with the drifting ones when they overlap. Before access is granted a calm still image sits under a luminance-reduced, softly blurred veil with one clear invitation standing out at readable contrast, and a single action keeps the current screen as a picture.
experience_progression: Arrival: calm veiled still, reduced in luminance and blurred, motionless, with a single clear invitation drawing all attention.
Request: the invitation triggers the camera permission ask.
Granted: the veiled placeholder gives way to the full-screen moving image at full clarity and the glass shapes begin their slow drift.
Denied: the view stays in its calm veiled state and a plainly worded notice appears, keeping a second attempt visibly available.
Ambient play: indefinite loop of slow autonomous drift combined with the pointer-following shape swelling and fusing.
Keep: a capture takes exactly what is on screen at that instant as a picture, after which the live experience simply continues.
completion_and_return: The ambient drift loops indefinitely with no natural end state.
The satisfying completion is keeping one picture; afterwards the live experience resumes and more pictures can be taken.
A refused camera returns the view to its calm veiled state with a visible second attempt rather than an empty screen.
Nothing accumulates or persists between visits; each arrival starts again from the veiled placeholder.
